funding_news.full_text:
Labelbox said on October 14, 2026, that it raised more than $100 million in Series E financing at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation, in a round led by Infinitum Partners that combines equity with a credit facility. Wipro Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), B Capital, Tau Ventures, and Snowpoint Ventures also participated, among others. Chief executive and co-founder Manu Sharma detailed the terms in a company blog post, and the company said the financing will support continued research and engineering across its two core products, Horizon and Recursion Managed Agents, as well as expansion of the teams bringing those products to customers. Sharma wrote that access to compute will be central to the company’s next chapter, noting that Infinitum’s John Yetimoglu was an early investor in Groq and is now involved in building large-scale compute infrastructure at GroqCloud. Company Position and History Labelbox stated that it reached profitability in 2026 while growing more than fivefold year over year. The company reports more than 400 customers, including over 90% of leading U.S. AI labs, and says its base spans frontier AI labs, hyperscalers, startups, and Fortune 500 companies. Sharma, Brian, and Dan founded Labelbox in 2018. In a founder’s note, Sharma wrote that he came to the United States to learn to design and build aircraft and rockets, working on computational fluid dynamics and neural networks, and that his later roles at DroneDeploy and Planet Labs showed him how much of the opportunity in machine learning sat in data. The post describes the company’s history in three chapters: training-data software for people building AI; reinforcement-learning environments built after what Sharma calls the ChatGPT moment, when the most capable models began improving by practicing real work; and agents, which the company built for itself first before opening the system to customers. Sharma also wrote that Labelbox builds each layer of its platform itself: an agent harness designed for ultra-long-horizon agents, sandbox infrastructure that runs millions of virtual machines, its own reinforcement-learning post-training infrastructure, and an expert network of more than 4 million people. Horizon Reinforcement-Learning Environments According to the company, Horizon’s WorldSim system builds simulated companies, with code, dashboards, spreadsheets, decks, and documents filled with realistic business data, in which a model attempts a difficult multi-step task end to end while every step is recorded as a trajectory. Deterministic verifiers score each trajectory the same way on every run, and when two trajectories are both correct, an expert’s preference teaches the model what Sharma calls taste. The company describes operating at a scale of thousands of worlds and millions of graded trajectories, tuned to a lab’s pass@k targets across coding, computer use, research, multimodal, and voice work. The Horizon product page lists domains that include autonomous AI research, agent coding and software engineering, multimodal knowledge work, voice with agentic tool use, computer use, and cybersecurity. Sharma wrote that Labelbox now works with 90% of the leading frontier AI labs and hyperscalers. Recursion Managed Agents The funding announcement states that Labelbox opened Recursion Managed Agents to enterprise customers earlier in October 2026. Under the product’s design, a Managed Agent receives a goal, a trigger such as a schedule, an alert, a Slack message, a webhook, or an API call, and a rubric defining what good work looks like. A separate grader agent scores every run against the rubric line by line and points to evidence for each call; when the work misses, the agent revises it. Agents can operate in three modes: multi-agent, in which a coordinator chains specialists that each carry their own model, instructions, tools, and permissions; team, in which copies of an agent split work on a shared board and check each other’s results; and auto, the default, in which the agent decides for itself when a job needs specialists or a team. The company says agents work across more than 100 business applications and any MCP server, with every tool scoped as read only, changes data, or destructive and credentials held in a vault so the model never sees them. Sessions run in isolated sandboxes, and Labelbox says the platform runs with zero data retention at every LLM provider. Its listed compliance program covers SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA, NIST 800-171, and PCI DSS. Pricing is set per agent session hour, with compute and model spend combined in one estimate, and existing Labelbox enterprise customers receive a one-time $100 credit. Describing the company’s internal rollout in a product launch post dated October 8, 2026, Labelbox wrote, “The surprise wasn’t that agents could do the work. It was how quickly they got better at it.” The company reports running 51 agents across 11 teams, spanning software engineering, reliability, security, machine-learning research, evals, product, finance, sales, strategy, and procurement. In one internal example, Labelbox said its pull-request review agent ran 39 graded reviews on a single agent version and model, and that across the 33 reviews that passed the grader, the median cost fell from $13.15 for the first 11 reviews to $8.90 for the last 11, 32% less per review, while the agent’s memory was updated 15 times and time per review held at about 27 minutes. Under the product’s memory mechanics, once five new session reports exist, and at most once an hour, a curator agent reads them and updates the agent’s memory; customers can browse what an agent has learned and delete any lesson that no longer holds.

funding_news.full_text:
Funding will accelerate development of Horizon, which helps frontier AI labs train and evaluate models, and Recursion Managed Agents, which enables enterprises to deploy agents that improve through experience.
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Labelbox, the AI platform powering reinforcement learning for frontier models and managed agents for enterprises, today announced it has raised more than $100 million in Series E financing, including equity and a credit facility. The round was led by Infinitum Partners, with participation from Wipro Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), B Capital, Tau Ventures, Snowpoint Ventures, and others.
Labelbox works with more than 400 customers, including over 90% of leading U.S. AI labs. The company reached profitability in 2026 while growing more than fivefold year over year.
As AI models become capable of performing increasingly complex tasks, the next challenge is enabling them to learn from experience and reliably execute work in real-world environments. Labelbox is addressing this opportunity through two core products: Horizon, which provides reinforcement learning environments and evaluation infrastructure for frontier AI labs, and Recursion Managed Agents, which enables enterprises to deploy fleets of agents that work inside existing business applications and improve with every run.
"Every company will soon run on AI systems that learn from their own work. Getting there takes innovation at every layer, from sandbox infrastructure and the agent harness to reinforcement learning post-training. Labelbox brings those layers together in one platform, and this funding lets us push each one further, so that frontier labs and enterprises can build AI that gets better with every run," said Manu Sharma, CEO and co-founder of Labelbox.
Advancing AI from training to execution
Horizon: Reinforcement learning for frontier AI
Horizon provides reinforcement learning environments, expert feedback, and evaluation infrastructure that help AI labs train and improve frontier models. Its environments simulate complex, multi-step work across coding, research, and other demanding tasks, enabling models to practice, receive feedback on their performance, and improve through reinforcement learning. Labelbox works with leading AI labs and hyperscalers on post-training programs.
Recursion Managed Agents: AI agents for enterprise workflows
Recursion Managed Agents enables companies to deploy fleets of AI agents inside the applications their teams already use. Agents can initiate work in response to schedules, alerts, tickets, and other triggers, coordinate across tools, and have their output evaluated against defined standards. Each run can inform the agent's memory, helping it improve how it approaches future tasks.

product_offering.core_offering: Labelbox provides an AI data factory and reinforcement learning (RL) data engine for AI teams, offering annotation tools, APIs, and expert networks to generate high-quality training data for machine learning models. Its product suite includes Horizon (RL environments and preference signals), Terra (robotics data products), Alignerr (network of 2.6M+ knowledge experts), and Recursion (RL platform for enterprise specialist agents). The platform supports multimodal data annotation across text, image, video, audio, and documents.
product_offering.differentiator: Labelbox differentiates through its RL data engine approach combining Horizon (RL environments), Terra (robotics data), Alignerr (expert network of 2.6M+ experts), and Recursion (enterprise agent RL platform). The company has proprietary research capabilities including AI safety evaluation frameworks and agent evaluation methodologies. Their Multimodal Chat Solution supports text, images, video, audio, and documents.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Provides complete RL data infrastructure for AI teams including RL environments and preference signals for post training, full-stack robotics data products, expert human grounding signals, and enterprise agent development platforms. Enables evaluation of frontier AI reasoning, automated expert recruitment, and scalable training data generation.
product_offering.problem_solved: Labelbox solves the critical bottleneck in AI development: obtaining high-quality, differentiated training data from domain experts at scale. The company addresses the challenge of engaging elite domain experts efficiently, providing RL environments and evaluation infrastructure, and enabling enterprises to build specialist AI agents that improve from real execution.
quantifiable_outcome: Meta released GIM-615 benchmark with 820 expert-authored problems remaining far from saturated with ~20% of items above frontier ability
RL systems outperformed sparse rewards by 300% when using rubric-based rewards and GRPO on real-world e-commerce tasks
product_offering.product_overview: Labelbox is an AI data factory and RL (reinforcement learning) data engine for AI teams. The company offers a platform-plus-products architecture serving both frontier AI labs and enterprises. For frontier AI, the core offerings include Horizon (RL environments and preference signals), Terra (full stack data for robotics foundation models), and Alignerr (expert network of 2.6M+ knowledge experts). For enterprises, Recursion is the RL platform for building, evaluating, and deploying specialist AI agents on real enterprise workflows. Additional products include Labelbox Applied Research (with Labelbox Evals, Labelbox Agents, and Labelbox Robotics), various leaderboards and benchmarks (Deep Research, Complex Reasoning, EchoChain, R-ConstraintBench), and research frameworks (Implicit Intelligence, Agent-as-a-World, Intent Laundering). The platform supports multimodal data processing across text, images, video, audio, and documents, with Python SDK and MCP support for automation.

expansion_highlight.description: Launch of Terra (robotics foundation model data) and Labelbox Robotics (LBRx) in November 2025 expands Labelbox from text/image labeling into physical-world robotics data, opening a new vertical adjacent to its core AI data business.

Launch of Recursion (June 2026) creates an enterprise specialist-agent RL platform, expanding Labelbox from data labeling tooling to full-stack enterprise agent training and serving, addressing a much larger enterprise AI TAM.

Acquisition of Upcraft (February 2026) brings AI agent technology into the Alignerr expert-recruitment workflow, indicating an active inorganic expansion strategy to deepen automation of the expert supply chain.

Partnerships with Google Cloud (Vertex AI integration) and Intuitive Surgical (surgical robotics) extend Labelbox's customer base beyond frontier AI labs into hyperscaler platforms and regulated healthcare/robotics enterprises.

Continuous release of benchmarks and research artifacts (EchoChain audio reasoning, Implicit Intelligence, Agent-as-a-World, Intent Laundering, Deep Research Leaderboard, Complex Reasoning Leaderboard, R-ConstraintBench) builds an external research brand that funnels developer and lab attention back into the platform.

Recursion's "fraction of frontier AI token costs" positioning implies a usage- or outcome-based pricing model for enterprise RL training, departing from per-seat labeling subscriptions and broadening commercial surface area.

company_assessment.market_position: Labelbox is a private, venture-backed company founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company has achieved unicorn status (> $1 billion valuation) following a $110 million Series D round led by SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 in January 2022. Labelbox serves over 200 enterprise customers and partners with over 90% of leading AI labs in the U.S., positioning itself as the leading RL data engine for AI teams. The company has 101-250 employees and serves both frontier AI labs and large enterprises with multiple AI use cases across industries including AI research, cloud computing, healthcare/robotics, and retail/ecommerce.

strengths.details: As frontier model development shifts from pre-training to RLHF and post-training, Labelbox's Alignerr (2.6M+ experts) and Horizon (RL environments) are positioned to capture disproportionate spend — Meta's GIM benchmark (820 expert-authored problems, 200K+ prompt-response pairs) demonstrates the company can deliver differentiated expert-curated RL data at frontier scale.
strengths.headline: Pivots into RL data engine for post-training boom

strengths.details: A 2.6M+ vetted expert network takes years to assemble and cannot be replicated by software-only rivals. As more enterprises and labs require human grounding signals (rubrics, preferences, expert reasoning), this asset compounds — each engagement enriches the network's domain coverage and ability to staff new verticals faster than competitors.
strengths.headline: Alignerr expert network becomes defensible data moat

strengths.details: Recursion (launched June 2026) targets the enterprise specialist-agent market at 'a fraction of frontier AI token costs.' If enterprise RL adoption accelerates, Labelbox can monetize its Alignerr network and RL infrastructure on a far larger customer base than frontier labs alone — converting research positioning into recurring enterprise SaaS revenue.
strengths.headline: Recursion opens enterprise agent RL market

strengths.details: Terra delivers purpose-built hardware-collected video and trajectory data for robotics foundation models — an emerging category where training data scarcity is a known bottleneck. Early positioning with proprietary collection hardware and AI-powered diversity engines positions Labelbox to capture share if robotics foundation models follow LLM-style scaling trajectories.
strengths.headline: Robotics foundation model opportunity via Terra

strengths.details: With over 90% of leading U.S. AI labs already partnered, Labelbox has minimal customer acquisition friction for new product launches — Horizon, Recursion, and applied research can be sold into an existing relationship base, accelerating revenue ramp relative to greenfield peers.
strengths.headline: Land-and-expand with 90%+ U.S. AI lab penetration

weakness.details: Scale AI's ~35% market share gives it structural advantages in pricing, government/defense relationships, and customer lock-in. As Scale expands into RL and evaluation, Labelbox could face share erosion and pricing pressure that compresses unit economics across its core labeling business.
weakness.headline: Scale AI dominance compresses pricing and share

weakness.details: Frontier AI labs (Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) have the engineering depth and capital to internalize RL data infrastructure. If even one major lab shifts expert sourcing and RL environments in-house, Labelbox would lose a flagship reference customer and demonstrate reduced strategic defensibility to remaining prospects.
weakness.headline: Frontier AI labs may build RL data infrastructure in-house

weakness.details: Recursion enters a market where incumbents (Scale, Surge, Snorkel) and hyperscalers (Vertex AI Agent Builder, Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock Agents) are all racing to own enterprise agent tooling. If the category fails to consolidate around specialist RL platforms, Labelbox's enterprise expansion could stall and dilute R&D impact across products.
weakness.headline: Enterprise agent RL market is nascent and crowded

weakness.details: With ~$188.9M raised total and a 2022 last round, supporting Horizon, Terra, Alignerr, Recursion, plus applied research labs and recent acquisition (Upcraft, Feb 2026) at 101–250 employees strains capital. If revenue growth lags the 2022–2026 AI capex surge, runway may force prioritization that weakens one or more product lines.
weakness.headline: Capital efficiency concern given breadth of product bets

weakness.details: Managing annotation and rubric quality across a 2.6M+ contributor network (Alignerr) is operationally complex; a single publicized quality incident on a frontier AI benchmark (e.g., contaminated data, faulty rubrics) could damage the credibility that underpins premium pricing versus software-only competitors.
weakness.headline: Expert network quality is hard to police at 2.6M+ scale

competitive_moat.details: Alignerr network of 2.6M+ knowledge experts (some sources cite 1M+ domain experts) provides differentiated, human-generated training signal that frontier AI models cannot self-generate. This human expert pool is the core asset underlying Horizon RL environments, Terra robotics data, and Recursion enterprise agent training.

Partnerships with over 90% of leading AI labs in the U.S. create compounding network effects where lab adoption drives expert engagement, benchmark legitimacy, and further lab adoption. Named enterprise partnerships with Meta, Google Cloud (Vertex AI integration), and Intuitive Surgical reinforce this gravity.

Proprietary research artifacts (Intent Laundering framework, Agent-as-a-World, Implicit Intelligence, EchoChain, R-ConstraintBench, Deep Research Leaderboard) plus benchmarks such as GIM with Meta create reputation and methodological IP that competitors must replicate from scratch.

Native IAM-delegated integrations with AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage plus Python SDK and MCP support embed Labelbox into enterprise data pipelines and AI agent workflows, raising migration costs once training data, rubrics, and RL environments are operationalized.

An applied research team producing peer-reviewed-style work (NeurIPS 2025 participation, arXiv publications) and a named executive bench (CEO Manu Sharma, plus acquired Upcraft co-founder Greg Caplan) supports the credibility required to win frontier-lab engagements.

Enterprise customers investing in custom rubrics, RL environments, and Alignerr-managed expert pools face operational switching costs: re-platforming annotation workflows, re-validating expert-screened datasets, and re-running evaluation harnesses against internal benchmarks.

key_risks.details: Scale AI holds approximately 35% of the dedicated AI data labeling market, dwarfing Labelbox's share and giving Scale significant advantages in customer relationships, pricing power, and government/defense contracts.
key_risks.headline: Scale AI holds 35% market share as dominant incumbent

key_risks.details: Disclosed marquee customers are concentrated among a handful of frontier labs and large enterprises (Meta, Google Cloud, Intuitive Surgical). With 200+ customers but reliance on AI labs for the Alignerr volume, a slowdown at one or two top labs would meaningfully impact utilization.
key_risks.headline: Customer concentration risk on a small set of frontier AI labs

key_risks.details: Series D closed at a $1B+ valuation in January 2022. With no subsequent disclosed round in the source data and an undisclosed revenue/ARR figure, the gap between the last mark and current fundamentals (4+ years later) is material for any diligence conclusion.
key_risks.headline: Last priced round was January 2022 — no fresh signal on current valuation or runway

key_risks.details: Labelbox operates at least four major product lines (Horizon, Terra, Alignerr, Recursion) plus several research frameworks and benchmarks. Spreading 101–250 employees across frontier AI data, robotics data, enterprise agents, and applied research raises execution risk versus focused competitors.
key_risks.headline: Product portfolio breadth may strain execution

key_risks.details: Labelbox acquired Upcraft in February 2026 to integrate AI agent technology into Alignerr. Recent acquisitions in fast-moving AI markets frequently under-deliver on integration synergies, and the acquisition adds another product surface area.
key_risks.headline: Acquisition integration risk from Upcraft

key_risks.details: Operating geographies are listed primarily as San Francisco Bay Area and broader North America, with no documented international expansion outside U.S.-led AI labs — limiting exposure to growing AI ecosystems in Europe and Asia.
key_risks.headline: Geographic concentration in U.S. limits diversification

launches.full_text: According to reports from IT Home citing foreign media, Anthropic is enhancing the performance of Claude Code through a project involving about 1,000 human software engineers. This project is internally referred to as 'Marlin' at the data labeling company Snorkel AI, and its core focus is on fine-tuning Claude Code's responses to make them closer to the real working environment of developers. AI companies like Anthropic typically outsource data work to third-party companies like Snorkel, which hire contractors to teach AI various specialized fields and perform other tasks to improve the model. Two contractors involved in the Anthropic project revealed that they are paid $280 (approximately 1,902 RMB) for each task they complete, which involves writing prompts and reviewing code. In the Marlin project, contractors with a software engineering background are asked to conduct A/B testing on code produced by two different models. They compare two sets of outputs, choose their preferred results, and assess whether the model has truly met the level of detail required by the prompts. One contractor stated that, essentially, it is about training Claude Code to produce simpler and more maintainable code. It is reported that the project is still ongoing, and the contractors do not know which version of the model they are evaluating.

launches.title: The “Invisible Army” of Developers: How Thousands of Freelancers Around the World Teach Claude Code to Write Code Correctly
launches.ai_summary: Anthropic uses feedback from nearly 1,000 software engineers to fine-tune Claude Code, with contractors paid $280 per task. The Marlin project, run via Snorkel, has freelancers A/B testing code and choosing better versions, and the project is ongoing.
launches.full_text:
To improve the performance of Claude Code, Anthropic uses feedback from nearly 1,000 software engineers.

To improve the performance of Claude Code, Anthropic uses feedback from nearly 1,000 software engineers. AI companies like Anthropic often outsource their data work to third-party contractors, who in turn hire experts to teach the AI ​​various specialized subjects and perform other tasks to improve the models. Business Insider took a look behind the scenes at how developer Claude Code's "invisible army" operates around the world. Two contractors working on the Anthropic project told Business Insider that they are paid $280 for each task of creating prototypes and reviewing code. According to them, each task takes about an hour, although some materials required additional approvals during the approval phase with Snorkel, a company that creates datasets to improve AI models and tests for chatbots. The project, called Marlin within Snorkel, focuses on fine-tuning Claude Code's responses so that it can accurately mimic the work of a professional developer. According to Snorkel’s instructions, the freelancers (all of whom have experience in software development) were tasked with A/B testing code written by two different models. In the process, they compared the performance of both models and chose the best one. One of the contractors noted that the goal of the project was to ensure that the model was capable of producing code with the required level of detail specified in the prompt. In effect, this was teaching Claude Code how to write simpler, more maintainable code. The project is still ongoing. The freelancers themselves do not know which versions of the models they are evaluating. As AI becomes smarter and more capable, data-marking platforms are moving from general tasks to increasingly specialized ones that require expert knowledge in a specific field or even degrees. Snorkel’s website states that the company works with professionals who have advanced degrees and degrees (such as Ph.D.s, M.D.s, or J.D.s) or equivalent experience. According to the company, top experts earn more than $3,000 per week. In addition to Snorkel, platforms like Scale AI and Mercor are also willing to pay software engineers up to $110 per hour. The Marlin project participants were to create a series of scenarios in which software developers could use Claude Code. The contractors were tasked with choosing a GitHub repository from a list of thousands of options. They then had to create a Pull Request, a stage where a developer proposes changes to the code, such as new features or bug fixes. The contractors also had to write a prompt, a series of questions explaining exactly what they expected from the model. In one of the tasks, the contractor asked the model to reorganize how the system stores and processes “execution metadata”—additional information about how processes are run. The goal was to make the code clearer and more user-friendly for developers, without changing the logic of the product itself or its functionality. The model produced two versions of the code, after which the contractor chose the one he thought was more effective. According to the project instructions, participants were also required to send clarification prompts to “check how the models work with the context of the conversation.” As part of another task, the executor created a security patch request for the model. It concerned the way MLFlow (an open source machine learning platform) loads Python packages when loading some models. The task instructions required the following from the contractor: "Evaluate the production-ready code based on its correctness, security, reliability, and maintainability. The fix should effectively block command injection attempts while maintaining access for all legitimate whitelisted pip installer options." launches.title: Introducing BigLaw Bench: Research
launches.ai_summary: The article discusses the launch of BigLaw Bench (BLB): Research, a new benchmark focused on legal research problems using AI, developed with Snorkel AI. The benchmark evaluates AI models' ability to perform complex, realistic legal search and research tasks, aiming to improve and measure future AI research capabilities.
launches.full_text: The second of our major BigLaw Bench (BLB) expansions this quarter is BLB: Research. This dataset focused on hard agentic legal research problems. Working with our data partner Snorkel AI, a leader in creating complex expert data for frontier AI, we identified a series of US Case Law research problems that leading models are currently unable to solve — even when provided with search tools like web search. The purpose of BLB: Research is twofold. First, to identify how foundation models are improving on research tasks and the failure modes that continue to cause them to return unsatisfactory answers. Second, to investigate ways to improve AI-based legal research through agentic systems and access to non-public data in addition to foundation model capabilities. By enabling us to both identify the best model and to build better infrastructure for those models, BLB: Research helps us build deeper and more accurate research capabilities for our customers. Benchmarking Beyond Models BLB: Research is our first benchmark that requires models to operate end-to-end over more than documents. Models must use tools to perform searches in order to identify relevant research context and provide a grounded, cited response. While historically we had measured search capabilities independently, evolutions in agent building and model deployment led us to combine search and response into a unified benchmark. The main driver of this change is the growing consensus on search as the primary means for providing grounded model responses across the industry. On the research side, as models are increasingly trained to use search rather than training data for up-to-date knowledge, benchmarking their capabilities without search unrealistically undersells what they can do. “ Building a holistic search benchmark allows us to measure performance in the way that tracks how research capabilities are being developed and how our customers expect them to be delivered. ” Search is also becoming table stakes in practice, with customers relying on knowledge sources and expecting pin-cited sources as the default for research-driven use cases. Building a holistic search benchmark allows us to measure performance in the way that tracks how research capabilities are being developed and how our customers expect them to be delivered. Building Realistic Complexity Given its ubiquity as a paradigm, models are, perhaps unsurprisingly, very good at search. They can write booleans and web searches and have learned to use search to explore, understand, and refine their research. A primary objective for BLB: Research was to validate these baseline capabilities, as well as identify areas in which the models were still not capable of turning their search capabilities into meaningful research outcomes for lawyers. In short, we wanted to create a hard benchmark. A good way to make benchmarks hard is to make them esoteric. This is unfortunately also a great way to make a benchmark useless. While we could show the models fail at a number of tasks, if succeeding at those tasks wouldn't actually help a legal professional, that failure is beside the point. Accordingly, we needed to ensure that tasks were difficult and realistic. Realistic tasks are both intrinsically useful and represent a research pattern that is generally useful, such as identifying the best case to cite for a proposition, drafting a research memo, or planning a claim or defense. From these realistic task types we then had to find those that were hard. We did this not by predicting what should be hard but by actually finding the frontier of model capabilities. First, we identified what failure looked like on a structured rubric: How poorly must a model perform before its answer is unhelpful to a legal professional? We found that many partly correct answers are still helpful. For example, slightly-off analysis with good citations to principal cases still gives users a research head start. In general, we found that model answers become unhelpful once the model completes less than 60% of the required task criteria. On these tasks, models are often missing critical reasoning junctures, making wrong turns in their research, or providing answers that are too surface level to be useful. Here are some research tasks that Harvey will use to benchmark models’ research capabilities: Practice Area Task Objective Task Description Corporate Assessing Earn-Out Manipulation Claims After Asset Sale A strategic buyer acquires a Delaware company's assets with a multi-year earn-out, then consolidates the business, reallocates overhead, shifts pricing strategy, and reassigns key salespeople. Assess whether the buyer's integration decisions breach the Asset Purchase Agreement. Securities Litigation Evaluating Securities Fraud Claims Against EV Company for Prototype Misrepresentations A publicly traded hydrogen fuel-cell truck company's CEO made statements about fully functional prototypes and secured partnerships that internal documents contradict. Evaluate material misrepresentation, scienter pleading, and PSLRA safe harbor defenses after a 45% stock price decline. Privacy and Cybersecurity Analyzing Defenses to Nationwide Class Action Arising from FinTech Data Breach A financial-technology company with 650,000 affected users faces a putative nationwide class action after a breach caused by a compromised contractor API credential. Evaluate Article III standing for speculative-harm plaintiffs, choice-of-law barriers to nationwide class certification, and Rule 12(b)(6) strategies. Other practice areas included in the benchmark are: Intellectual Property, Commercial Litigation, Constitutional Law, Regulatory, Employment & Labor, Health Law & Life Sciences, Tax, Tort, Real Property, Media and Technology, Immigration, and Family Law. What’s Next for BLB: Research Sifting through troves of documents to find answers, narratives, and trends is one of the most common tasks in legal practice. The same search capabilities that make models good at case law research also underpin the ability to search EDGAR, an investigation corpus, a deal room, or even a law firm’s own internal knowledge. BLB: Research will build towards measuring all these capabilities and finding the right tools for enabling models to move lawyers from sifting to solving. The next step-change in search capabilities can come from various sources: model capabilities, unique data sources, or the tools to enable the former to interact with the latter. BLB: Research will allow us to track and design innovations in all of these spaces, and convert them into the best possible research results for our customers.

launches.full_text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (December 10, 2025) — The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), in partnership with the U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM), has selected the ten startup teams for the inaugural cohort of the Blue Object Management Challenge Accelerator Program.

This accelerator is designed to rapidly identify and prototype dual-use commercial technologies that support USINDOPACOM’s operational priorities. In military operations, “blue objects” refer to friendly forces which include U.S. warfighters, equipment, and infrastructure. Blue object management involves the real-time tracking and coordination of these assets, providing commanders with accurate, up-to-date operational awareness, particularly in dynamic or contested environments.

These 10 companies were competitively selected through DIU’s Prize Challenge process. Companies were selected by the mission partner for their focus on advancing AI-enabled decision-making capabilities that seek to improve how mission-critical data is integrated, accessed, and used across Department of War (DoW) platforms and forces.

The 2025 cohort includes:

CI-PHER Tech, Inc

Countifi, Inc

Dunedain Systems

Exia Labs

Kinnami Software Corporation

Lumbra, Inc

MAIK

Snorkel AI

Unstructured Technologies, Inc

Valinor Streamline, Inc

Over the course of the program, participating teams will work alongside DIU and USINDOPACOM to test, validate, and transition solutions that can strengthen operational readiness and address the unique challenges of the region.

The Blue Object Management Challenge Accelerator was launched in August 2025, and applicants were evaluated through a competitive downselect process. Finalists will receive a share of the $500,000 in prize awards.

The challenge highlights DIU’s and INDOPACOM’s shared commitment to accelerating innovation in the Indo-Pacific theater, where commercial technology can deliver mission-critical capabilities faster. By working directly with early-stage startups, the program ensures the DoW has access to adaptable, dual-use solutions that enhance resilience, logistics, and decision-making in contested environments.

launches.title: Terminal-Bench 2.0: Raising the bar for AI agent evaluation
launches.ai_summary: Stanford University and Laude Institute have released Terminal-Bench 2.0, an updated benchmark for evaluating AI coding agents in command-line environments, featuring 89 curated tasks with enhanced verification and higher difficulty than the original version. Snorkel AI was a top external contributor to the project, providing reliable difficulty assessment, failure mode analysis, and task contributions to the dataset. The team also announced Harbor, a new framework for scaling containerized AI agent environments to enable developers to parallelize execution across thousands of containers on neocloud providers or Kubernetes clusters.
launches.author: Kobie Crawford
launches.full_text:
Terminal-Bench 2.0: Raising the bar for AI agent evaluation

Terminal-Bench, a joint project between Stanford University and Laude Institute, has quickly become the gold standard for evaluating AI coding agents’ capabilities in command-line environments. Since its launch earlier this year, the benchmark has garnered over 1,000 GitHub stars and attracted contributions from nearly 100 developers worldwide. At Snorkel AI, we’re proud to be one of the top external contributors to this project, and we’re thrilled to see the release of Terminal-Bench 2.0–a significant leap forward in both difficulty and quality. Why Terminal-Bench 2.0 matters From the beginning, Terminal-Bench was designed as a living benchmark that would evolve alongside AI capabilities. As frontier models improved, with performance climbing over 50% on the original benchmark, the team knew it was time to raise the stakes. Terminal-Bench 2.0 delivers on this vision with 89 carefully curated tasks that push the boundaries of what AI agents can accomplish in terminal environments. Each task underwent rigorous verification, with the development team meticulously reviewing every challenge to ensure it meets the highest standards. What’s new in 2.0 Increased difficulty: Terminal-Bench 2.0 is substantially more challenging than its predecessor. Tasks now better represent the frontier challenges that distinguish truly capable agents from those that can only handle routine operations. This ensures the benchmark remains relevant as AI capabilities advance—maintaining the crucial 50% performance ceiling where there’s clear room for improvement while still delivering meaningful signal for evaluation. Enhanced verification: One of the most significant improvements in 2.0 is the dramatic increase in task quality and reproducibility. The original benchmark included several problematic tasks—some were unsolvable for artificial reasons, others set arbitrary thresholds, and a few lacked robustness (like the YouTube download task affected by changing anti-bot protections). Terminal-Bench 2.0 eliminates these problems. Every task is now reproducible, properly specified, and genuinely solvable, with the team confident that near-100% performance is attainable for sufficiently capable agents. Real-world impact: Terminal-Bench 2.0 removes tasks that don’t reflect valuable real-world work. The easy “Hello World” debugging task is gone, along with other challenges that, while interesting academically, don’t provide meaningful details about an agent’s economic impact or ability to perform valuable tasks that engineers actually get paid to do. Snorkel AI’s contributions Snorkel’s researchers joined other contributors to Terminal-Bench to help the project achieve its goals of delivering a thoroughly vetted, challenging dataset. The team’s main contributions to the project centered on three areas: Reliable difficulty assessment: Our research team leveraged its expertise to develop a systematic assessment of Terminal-Bench 2.0 task difficulty, providing consistent criteria that could be applied across all contributed tasks. Extended failure mode analysis: We developed a failure taxonomy and collected traces to better understand where LLMs fail when executing Terminal-Bench tasks. These insights can help with better task design and inform how to improve agents and models under test. Tasks: The Snorkel team is a top contributor to the Terminal-Bench registry, and we’re pleased that we have been able to provide tasks to the Terminal-Bench 2.0 dataset. The next level: Introducing Harbor In addition to Terminal-Bench 2.0, the team has just announced an exciting new project named Harbor (site | repo). Harbor represents a significant evolution in how developers can scale up containerized AI agent environments. Born from observing how the community actually used Terminal-Bench, Harbor abstracts away the complexities of container-based rollouts—a challenge that seems simple but quickly grows complex at scale. The framework emerged after the Terminal-Bench team noticed users deploying the benchmark in unexpected ways—for example, as CI/CD tests for agents, for reinforcement learning with synthetic tasks, and for prompt optimization. All these use cases had the same abstraction in common: containerized environments performing rollouts that return tokens and rewards. Harbor makes this pattern accessible with minimal code, allowing developers to scale from local testing to thousands of parallel containers across neocloud providers like Daytona, E2B, and Modal, or on self-managed Kubernetes clusters. Better together: the benchmark and the framework Terminal-Bench 2.0 represents more than just a version update—it’s a commitment to maintaining the highest quality evaluation infrastructure as AI agent capabilities increase. By prioritizing rigorous verification and meaningful difficulty over arbitrary metrics, the benchmark ensures that progress on Terminal-Bench translates to genuine improvements in AI agents’ ability to perform complex, real-world tasks. And now, with Harbor, practitioners can parallelize the execution of entire datasets for faster iteration and greater efficiency. For teams building the next generation of AI coding assistants, Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harbor provide an evaluation framework with the necessary robustness and reproducibility to measure true progress in this rapidly evolving space. At Snorkel, we enthusiastically support the Terminal-Bench community and are confident that reproducible, containerized environments will accelerate the development of accurate and reliable agentic AI systems. If you need to build or improve your agents with expert-verified data in an RL environment, come talk to us! Terminal-Bench is an open-source project led by Stanford University and Laude Institute, with contributions from a vibrant community of individuals and organizations, including Snorkel AI. To learn more about the benchmark, contribute tasks, or evaluate your own agents, visit tbench.ai or join the project’s Discord community. To find out more about Snorkel’s data development platform and our work with frontier AI labs, visit us at snorkel.ai and connect with our team.

launches.title: How Rox achieved 99% accuracy with Snorkel Evaluate

launches.full_text:
CUSTOMER STORY How Rox achieved 99% accuracy with Snorkel Evaluate 99% Achieved accuracy with specialized evaluators +24 Point improvement in shipped critical outbound email feature

Enterprises facing aggressive revenue targets without more headcount are turning to agentic AI innovator Rox. Rox is redefining the revenue stack with it’s AI-powered sales productivity platform, starting with the Rox sales agent swarm which provides agents that can perform at the level of top sales reps. Rox is redefining the revenue stack with our AI-powered sales platform. Off-the-shelf models aren’t capable of delivering the quality we need to ensure our agents are accurately personalizing outbound emails. With Snorkel Evaluate we have been able to confidently assess our outbound email agent, then identify and fix issues to achieve human-level accuracy. The level of visibility and control Snorkel delivers is a huge advantage as we build trustworthy, agentic AI at scale. – Shriram Sridharan, co-founder, Rox Challenge Rox’s ability to ensure outbound emails are fully accurate and aligned with each customer’s brand and objectives is a key differentiator. However, when developing models Rox found that off-the-shelf evaluation approaches were not able to deliver the required quality for critical custom evaluation tasks. Initially Rox wrote it’s own LLM-as-a-judge. While the model seemed to score well, the Rox team wanted higher confidence for production deployment. Solution Using the Snorkel Evaluation Suite, Rox scored the judge against human experts and found it aligned only around 75% of the time. The team used Snorkel to iterate on the judge to increase alignment. The aligned judge surfaced an issue with the prototype outbound model, which used the wrong recipient name around 11% of time, enabling Rox to correct the model’s behavior. Outcomes Achieved 99%+ accuracy with specialized evaluators enabling sufficient trust to ship a critical email outbound feature.

funding_news.full_text:
Every AI product being built by a UK startup or enterprise right now depends on training data. The large language models they fine-tune, the foundation models they build on, the evaluation benchmarks they use to measure quality all of it was built on data that someone had to construct, curate and validate. Most of the time, that someone is Snorkel AI. Follow every UK startup and tech story at BestStartup UK.
On September 22 2026, Snorkel AI raised $350 million in a Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation, co-led by Insight Partners and S32. Its annualised revenue run rate reached $375 million an eighteenfold increase in twelve months. For context: twelve months ago Snorkel AI was generating approximately $20 million in annualised revenue. Today it is generating $375 million. That is the pace at which frontier AI data demand is growing.
What This Means for UK AI Companies
UK artificial intelligence is a £16 billion sector and growing. DeepMind, Wayve, Stability AI, Synthesia, Darktrace and dozens of other UK AI companies are building products that require training data, evaluation frameworks and reinforcement learning environments to function. Many of them particularly the ones building on or fine-tuning foundation models are already customers or potential customers of the infrastructure Snorkel AI provides.
The broader implication for UK AI founders is that the training data layer is not a commodity. It is a specialised capability that requires deep technical expertise, domain knowledge and the ability to construct expert-level datasets at scale. Snorkel AI’s 18x revenue growth tells you that frontier AI labs and large enterprises have concluded they cannot build this capability internally at the speed and quality they require and are willing to pay premium prices to a specialist supplier who can. What Snorkel AI Actually Builds
Snorkel AI describes itself as the frontier AI data lab. It builds training datasets, evaluation frameworks, synthetic data environments and reinforcement learning setups for AI systems that need more than publicly available data to reach frontier capability.
The shift from its original positioning as a data labelling automation tool to its current positioning as a finished data products company is significant. Labelling automation helped companies create their own data faster. Finished data products means Snorkel creates expert-constructed datasets covering specific domains, capabilities and evaluation benchmarks that frontier AI labs and large enterprises cannot easily produce internally and that take even the most qualified humans hours or days to construct individually. Snorkel AI has built the factory that produces these at scale, reliably, and with the quality controls that frontier model training requires. funding_news.title: Snorkel AI's $350M Funding Highlights Industry Shift Toward AI Data Solutions
funding_news.ai_summary: Snorkel AI raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation in a Series E led by Insight Partners and S32. The company's annualized revenue run rate reached $375 million, an 18-fold increase, as it expands from data labeling to data-as-a-service.
funding_news.author: Win Warfield
funding_news.full_text: Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in new funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, a jump that reflects how quickly demand for high-quality AI training data has intensified across the industry, according to TechCrunch, and a company announcement from co-founder and CEO Alex Ratner. The Series E round was led by New York’s Insight Partners and S32, formerly known as Section 32, with backing from existing investors including Addition, Lightspeed, Greylock, GV and Wells Fargo. The new valuation is nearly triple the $1.3 billion mark Snorkel reached 17 months ago when it raised a $100 million Series D, underscoring how rapidly investor enthusiasm has shifted toward companies selling the infrastructure behind AI models. Founded from research at a Stanford AI lab, Snorkel launched commercially in 2019 after four years of development. What began as a niche tool for making data labeling more efficient has evolved into a larger bet that the most valuable layer in AI may not just be models, but the data pipelines that feed them. Besides Ratner, the other co-founders of Snorkel AI are Christopher Ré, Paroma Varma, Braden Hancock and Henry Ehrenberg. Ratner completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University and is also an affiliate assistant professor at the University of Washington. Snorkel originally built software to automate data labeling, but the company has since moved into a broader business it describes as data-as-a-service. Instead of selling only tools for humans to label examples, it now delivers finished datasets and reinforcement-learning environments that are assembled through a mix of software, synthetic data generation and subject matter experts. That approach is designed to serve frontier labs, hyperscalers, enterprise customers, vertical AI companies and U.S. government agencies, Ratner said in the company’s announcement. The company said its annualized revenue run rate has reached $375 million, an 18-fold increase over the past year. That growth mirrors a wider boom in the market for AI data providers, as model developers seek more specialized, higher-quality training material to improve performance in increasingly competitive systems. Other startups in the space have also reported striking growth. Mercor said its gross annualized revenue has climbed to $2 billion, Handshake reached $1 billion earlier this year and TechCrunch reported that Micro1 had scaled to $500 million. Those figures, however, do not all mean the same thing. Several of these companies reportedly pay a large share of revenue to the experts doing the work, which means gross revenue can overstate the economic value retained by the business. Snorkel argues its model is different because the payments it makes to experts are reflected in cost of goods sold rather than in the headline annualized revenue figure. That distinction matters for investors comparing fast-growing AI data businesses, particularly as the market expands beyond simple labeling toward more complex products such as finished datasets and simulated environments. [Noah Wire Services helped in the writing of this article.]

funding_news.full_text:
フロンティアAI向け学習データを作るSnorkel AI、Insight PartnersとS32の共同リードで3.5億ドルを調達——評価額は35億ドル
AI 開発向けの学習データを手がける Snorkel AI は現地時間22日、Insight Partners と S32 が共同でリードするラウンドで3億5,000万ドルを調達したと発表した。 評価額は35億ドルで、資 […]
AI 開発向けの学習データを手がける Snorkel AI は現地時間22日、Insight Partners と S32 が共同でリードするラウンドで3億5,000万ドルを調達したと発表した。
評価額は35億ドルで、資金はフロンティア AI 向けの「データファクトリー」の拡大に充てる。新規に March Capital、Blumberg Capital、Allegis Capital、Frontline、Standard、Third Point Ventures が加わり、既存投資家の Addition、Greylock、Lightspeed、GV、Factory、Prosperity7、Walden Catalyst、Wells Fargo も参加した。
画像に写っているものが猫か犬かを人手でラベル付けする。AI 学習データといえば長らくそうした単純作業を指していた。だが、業務を丸ごと任せるエージェント型の AI を鍛えようとすると、話が変わる。
保険の引受審査を任せるなら、申請書類を読み、社内規程に照らし、必要な追加情報を取りに行き、最後に判断根拠まで書かせる必要がある。どの手順が正しく、どこで間違えたのかを判定できる基準がなければ、そもそも訓練も評価もできない。
共同創業者兼 CEO の Alex Ratner 氏は、こうした専門家が設計するタスクや環境、採点基準を「Data 2.0」と呼び、人員を増やすだけでは解けない研究課題だと説明している。
Snorkel AI が提供するのは、その「作り方」ごと請け負うサービスだ。ツールを売って顧客に使ってもらうのではなく、専門家が関与してデータセット、ベンチマーク、評価、環境そのものを構築して納品する形態をとり、研究チームが定義した非独占のデータセットや環境を「Snorkel Data Series」として提供し、四半期ごとに更新すると案内している。
同社は、良いデータは集めるものではなく作るものだと表現する。具体的には、対象分野の専門家の知見に、タスク設計、プログラムによる自動チェック、校正された専門家レビュー、評価環境を組み合わせ、学習に使える測定可能なシグナルへと変換する。まずモデルがどこで失敗するかを評価し、その失敗に合わせてデータや環境を作り、また評価する。そうした反復を回す運用だと述べている。
分かりやすいのが「Enterprise environments」と呼ぶ製品群だ。企業の実際の業務フローを高い忠実度で再現した模擬環境の中で、AI エージェントに仕事をさせ、訓練と評価を行う。保険の引受審査を再現した環境では、一度目の試行で正解にたどり着けた割合（pass@1）が10.9%から42.0%へ改善したと同社は自社の計測結果として示している。

funding_news.title: Snorkel AI triples valuation to $3.5 billion in $350M raise
funding_news.ai_summary: Snorkel AI closed $350 million in new funding, valuing the company at $3.5 billion. Annualized revenue run-rate now exceeds $350 million, up from about $20 million a year earlier. The company plans to use the capital for hiring, scaling enterprise and government work, and expanding into new verticals.
funding_news.author: Camila Nogueira
funding_news.full_text:
Share

CEO Alex Ratner said Snorkel AI has closed $350 million in new funding, putting the company's valuation at $3.5 billion as demand from frontier AI labs for increasingly complex training data and simulated environments accelerates. Insight Partners and S32 led the round, and existing backers Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo also took part. Annualized revenue run-rate at the company now stands above $350 million, compared with roughly $20 million twelve months prior. That new figure is close to triple the $1.3 billion valuation Snorkel carried after its $100 million Series D round in May 2025, a raise that also debuted Snorkel Evaluate alongside an expert data-as-a-service product. Growth remains the priority for now, though Snorkel anticipates turning profitable this year. Plans for the new capital include hiring additional researchers and engineers, scaling up enterprise and government work, and building third-party AI evaluation services, plus expansion into fresh verticals and data categories. The company traces back to 2019, when a group of researchers exited Stanford's AI lab to start it. Snorkel initially sold software for labeling and managing training data before moving toward direct delivery of finished datasets and reinforcement-learning environments, a data-as-a-service line it opened in September 2025. Tens of thousands of specialists across disciplines such as coding, law and medicine make up Snorkel's network, and the company charges for the finished data products this group produces instead of billing hours worked. Ratner said the approach means contributors get paid more generously while margins stay protected. Coding data currently outpaces other categories in demand at the company. Snorkel refers to its offering as an "agentic data development platform," combining human specialists with thousands of purpose-built AI models and agents to construct and verify data quality. Specialists handle the design work, setting scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics, and automated systems take on most of the intensive review labor. Frontier AI labs, hyperscalers, enterprises and the U.S. federal government are among Snorkel's customers, the company said. On the balance between human and automated work, Ratner said human involvement isn't disappearing anytime soon, noting that all the data labs draw real value from will still carry some human input for the foreseeable future, even as the volume of that data increasingly depends on synthetic and automated methods to keep pace with rising complexity. S32 partner Andy Harrison, who co-led the funding round, summed up the shift: "Data is becoming more rare, more specialized, more difficult to find." This funding lands within a wave of investment that followed Meta's $14.3 billion acquisition of a 49 percent stake in Scale AI in June 2025. Competitors Surge AI and Mercor have likewise seen strong investor demand, backed by their own revenue growth.

funding_news.ai_summary: Snorkel AI raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation in a round co-led by Insight Partners and S32. funding_news.author: Amit Chowdhry
funding_news.full_text:
Snorkel AI, a San Francisco-based company developing advanced data infrastructure for artificial intelligence, has raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation in a financing round co-led by Insight Partners and S32. Existing investor Addition also participated significantly. The funding will support the expansion of Snorkel’s agentic data factory, which supplies the specialized datasets, environments, and evaluation frameworks used to train and assess increasingly sophisticated AI systems.

New investors in the round include March Capital, Blumberg Capital, Allegis Capital, Frontline, Standard, and Third Point Ventures.

Existing investors Greylock, Lightspeed, GV, Factory, Prosperity7, Walden Catalyst, and Wells Fargo also participated.

Snorkel plans to use the financing to increase its capacity to serve leading AI laboratories and enterprises while extending its research and technology into additional industries, AI modalities, and applications.

Founded in 2019 out of the Stanford AI Lab, Snorkel develops tools and services for building the specialized data required to improve advanced AI systems.

The company is expanding beyond conventional data labeling, which typically involves assigning categories or other relatively simple annotations to existing information.

Its newer offerings focus on what Snorkel describes as Data 2.0, an approach designed for advanced and agentic AI models that must complete complex, multistep tasks.

These systems require sophisticated training and evaluation materials, including realistic task environments, expert-developed instructions, and detailed assessment criteria.

Creating such materials can take highly qualified specialists hours or days, particularly in industries where accurate outcomes depend on substantial professional knowledge.

Snorkel’s agentic data factory combines expert human involvement with proprietary technology to produce these research-grade datasets and evaluation environments at greater scale.

The company works with leading AI laboratories and enterprises on data used for frontier model training, evaluation, and performance measurement.

Its expert Data-as-a-Service offering, launched in September 2025, addresses the growing demand for specialized data development among organizations building advanced AI systems.

Snorkel intends to expand this business into additional high-value sectors, including healthcare, law, and software engineering.

These industries require AI systems to perform complex tasks involving specialized knowledge, detailed reasoning, and accurate responses to information that may evolve throughout a workflow.

The new funding will also support development of Snorkel’s core research capabilities and enable the company to expand into additional types of data and model architectures.

Snorkel’s founding team has made extensive contributions to data-centric artificial intelligence. According to the company, its research includes more than 250 peer-reviewed papers with over 25,000 citations.

The company plans to continue supporting open research through initiatives such as its Open Benchmarks Grants program, which encourages the development of publicly available AI evaluation resources.

The financing provides additional resources as Snorkel expands its role in the development of training and evaluation infrastructure for frontier and enterprise AI.

KEY QUOTES:

“The teams pushing the frontier want a research data partner who pioneers the science of data development. That’s what Snorkel was built to be: the frontier lab for agentic data, combining human excellence with over a decade of research and technology.”

Alex Ratner, Co-Founder and CEO of Snorkel AI

“Snorkel’s research-grade approach to AI data, environments, and measurement is becoming an increasingly important ingredient in building capable and reliable AI systems – and their demonstrated growth at scale reflects that. We’re excited to back Alex and the team as they continue to bring their frontier AI data factory capabilities to longer-running, complex work in high value industries like healthcare, law, and software engineering.”

Lonne Jaffe, Managing Director at Insight Partners

“Snorkel’s expert-agentic environments create a unique flywheel between human expertise and AI, delivering data at the speed and quality that enables a new era of efficiency and accuracy for model development. Working with Snorkel ensures the highest frontier model success rate and creates a true partnership between model developer and data provider.”

Andy Harrison, CEO and General Partner of S32

funding_news.author: Ekemini September
funding_news.full_text:
Snorkel AI Raises $350 Million To Build Data Factory for Frontier AI Labs

By Ekemini 23 September 2026

Key Takeaways Snorkel AI secures $350M in a round co-led by Insight Partners and S32.

The startup leverages decade-long Stanford research to deliver programmatically constructed datasets for enterprise deployment.

The investment targets scaling agentic data factories for training complex frontier artificial intelligence systems.

AI models study data. Lots and lots of data. It was easier to train AI in the old days, but now, AI has progressed. More than labeling photos, you can now use AI to do virtually everything. So, it makes sense to create better and harder training models for today’s AI models. Snorkel AI raises $350 million to do this. This is what most people now call Data 2.0. Snorkel Raises $350M for The Data 2.0 Shift Snorkel AI announced it raised $350 million. The round was co-led by Insight Partners and S32, with a lot of help from existing investor Addition. Snorkel built what they call an agentic data factory. It pairs tens of thousands of human experts with thousands of specialized AI agents. The human experts design the hard scenarios, the tasks, and the rubrics, meaning how to grade if the AI did it right. Then their own AI does the boring quality check work to make sure everything is perfect. So humans bring the brains, AI brings the speed. And the best part for the experts is how they get paid. Most old labeling companies pay people by the hour. Snorkel says they do not sell human labor; they sell the final data product. That lets them pay the experts way better while still keeping good profit for themselves. funding_news.title: Snorkel AI Triples Valuation to $3.5B on Training Data Demand
funding_news.ai_summary: Snorkel AI raised $350 million in Series E funding on September 22, tripling its valuation to $3.5 billion. The data startup's annualized revenue run rate is $375 million, an eighteenfold increase over the past year. The company pivoted to data-as-a-service, combining synthetic data with expert contributions.
funding_news.author: Abdul Wasay
funding_news.full_text:
Snorkel AI raised $350 million in Series E funding on September 22. The data startup tripled its valuation to $3.5 billion in just seventeen months. This remarkable growth reflects an urgent crisis consuming the AI industry globally. Frontier models now hunger for training data faster than companies can provide it.

Insight Partners and S32 led the round alongside existing investors Addition, Lightspeed, Greylock, GV, and Wells Fargo. The seven-year-old startup originally provided software automating manual data labeling tasks. However, Snorkel shifted strategy last year toward data-as-a-service, delivering completed datasets directly. This pivot proved transformative for company growth and margins significantly.

The hybrid approach combines synthetic data generated by Snorkel’s models with subject matter expert contributions. This strategy differs fundamentally from pure human labor marketplaces operating today. Snorkel’s annualized revenue run rate now stands at $375 million. This represents an eighteenfold increase over the previous twelve months alone. Such explosive growth underscores how desperately AI labs need training data access.

Competing data companies are experiencing similar trajectories now. Mercor achieved $2 billion in gross annualized revenue. Handshake crossed the $1 billion milestone earlier this year. Micro1 scaled to $500 million gross run rate recently.

However, these figures merit careful interpretation because these companies pay 60-70% directly to domain specialists doing the work. Snorkel operates differently through its hybrid model structure. Its payments to human experts land in cost of goods sold rather than inflating headline revenue metrics.

CEO Alex Ratner co-founded Snorkel following four years researching at Stanford’s AI lab. The company launched commercially in 2019 with this academic foundation. Since then, Snorkel built deep relationships with major AI labs and corporations worldwide.

As frontier models scale toward trillion-parameter scales, training data demand grows exponentially. Snorkel positioned itself perfectly to capture this expanding opportunity through innovative data strategies.

funding_news.title: Insight Partners, S32 back Snorkel AI at $3.5B valuation with $350M raise — TFN
funding_news.ai_summary: Snorkel AI raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation, nearly triple its price 17 months ago. Its annualized revenue jumped from about $20 million to over $350 million in a year. The company expects to turn a profit this year.
funding_news.author: Abhinaya Prabhu
funding_news.full_text:
- Snorkel AI raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation, nearly triple its price 17 months ago.
- Its annualised revenue jumped from roughly $20 million to more than $350 million in a year.
- The round underlines a broader shift: AI labs now pay for finished, expert-built data.
Snorkel AI just got a lot more expensive, and it’s not because it labels data faster than anyone else anymore. The company, which used to sell software for tagging training data, now builds and sells the finished datasets and simulated work environments that frontier labs train their models on.
That pivot has taken its annualised revenue from around $20 million a year ago to more than $350 million now, and investors have responded by tripling its valuation to $3.5 billion in a $350 million round.
Insight Partners and S32 co-led the raise, with existing backers Addition, Greylock, Wells Fargo, Lightspeed, GV and several others returning, alongside new investors including March Capital and Third Point Ventures. It brings Snorkel to nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation it held after its $100 million round in May 2025.
From labelling software to a data factory
Snorkel was founded in 2019 by Alex Ratner, Chris Ré, Paroma Varma, Braden Hancock and Henry Ehrenberg, spinning out of Stanford’s AI Lab, where Ratner and Ré had built the original open-source Snorkel project. For years, the company sold tools that let enterprises label their own data.
Since launching a data-as-a-service business in September 2025, it has flipped that model: human specialists across coding, law and medicine now design tasks and grading rubrics, while a layer of AI models automates quality control, producing datasets and reinforcement-learning environments it sells directly to labs, hyperscalers, enterprises and the US federal government.
“Our strong view is that 100% of the data that labs will get value out of will have some human input in the foreseeable future. But 100% of that data will have to use synthetic and automated approaches to keep up with this complexity ,” said Ratner.
The data race is getting more competitive
Snorkel isn’t the only one cashing in on labs running out of usable internet text. Scale AI raised $1 billion at close to a $14 billion valuation before Meta later bought a 49% stake worth roughly $14.3 billion. Mercor went from a $30 million seed round to a $10 billion valuation on a similar bet, and has since been in talks to double that again. Surge AI, meanwhile, was reportedly weighing a first-ever outside raise at north of $25 billion.
Snorkel’s pitch against that crowd is that it designs the tasks and grades the output, which is a harder thing to compete away on price.
Snorkel says the capital will fund more researchers and engineers, expand its enterprise and government business, support third-party model evaluations, and push into new industries and data formats. It expects to turn a profit this year.
“Data is becoming more rare, more specialized, more difficult to find. If you want to train the most frontier, complex and capable models, now you need superior data,” said Andy Harrison, partner at S32 who co-led the funding.
If the last 18 months were about labs discovering they’d run out of internet to scrape, the next stretch is about who gets paid to manufacture what’s missing. Snorkel just put $3.5 billion that it can be the one doing the manufacturing — the harder question is whether that job stays defensible once every well-funded rival is building the same expert-plus-AI pitch.

funding_news.author: Maria Deutscher
funding_news.full_text:
Training data provider Snorkel AI raises $350M at $3.5B valuation
Snorkel AI Inc., a provider of artificial intelligence training data, today disclosed that it has raised $350 million in funding.
Insight and S32 led the Series E deal. They were joined by more than a half-dozen other backers including Alphabet Inc.’s GV startup fund.
Snorkel AI was founded in 2019 by researchers from the Stanford AI Lab. Its first product was Snorkel Flow, a software platform that reduced the amount of work involved in supervised learning projects. Supervised learning is an AI development method that trains neural networks using labeled datasets. Such files comprise prompts and correct, human-generated answers to those prompts.
Creating labeled datasets is a highly time-consuming process. Snorkel Flow automated the process using statistical methods developed by the company’s founders at Stanford. According to Snorkel AI, those methods addressed the accuracy issues that made earlier automation approaches ineffective.
Last year, the company changed its business model. It pivoted from selling software that helps developers create training data to providing ready-to-use training datasets. Additionally, Snorkel AI expanded its focus beyond supervised learning to a second, more complex AI training approach known as reinforcement learning.
Whereas supervised learning uses datasets that contain prompts and correct answers to those prompts, reinforcement learning datasets contain unanswered questions. The AI model being trained must figure how to answer them without any human assistance. Once it produces a response, human reviewers or an automated system verify its accuracy. They then provide the AI with feedback that helps improve its reasoning.
Snorkel AI relies on tens of thousands of human experts to generate reinforcement learning training tasks. The company also provides customers with other technical assets that are needed for AI training runs.
When an AI model completes a reinforcement learning task, human reviewers check its work based on predefined evaluation criteria. Those criteria can span several pages. In the case of a programming task, for example, the evaluation guidance must cover all the cybersecurity and performance requirements that AI-generated code must meet.
Snorkel AI develops AI evaluation rubrics for customers. Furthermore, it improves those rubrics over time based on feedback from the human AI reviewers who use them. Some of that feedback is generated when two human reviewers give different scores to an AI prompt response. Such differences usually point to an inconsistency in the underlying evaluation criteria.
AI models are often trained in specialized virtual environments. A code generation model, for example, might require a simulated version of a developer workstation. Snorkel AI provides such as training sandboxes alongside its datasets and evaluation rubrics.
“Since launching our new data-as-a-service offering nearly a year ago, we’ve grown over 18 times, and this week crossed an annualized revenue run rate of $375 million,” co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Alex Ratner detailed in a blog post.
The company will reportedly use its newly raised funding to hire more engineers. Snorkel AI also plans to invest in AI safety initiatives and support the development of open-source model evaluation benchmarks.
