The companies will continue supporting Mercari's payment security and customer experience.
launches.full_text: Forter, a company providing an AI judgment platform for next-generation commerce (headquartered in New York, USA), and GMO Payment Gateway, Inc. (CEO: Kazunari Aihara, hereinafter referred to as GMO-PG), which is part of the GMO Internet Group, announced that Mercari, Inc. (headquartered in Minato-ku, Tokyo, CEO: Shintaro Yamada, hereinafter referred to as Mercari), which operates Japan's largest flea market app "Mercari," has fully introduced Forter's AI judgment platform as a measure against fraudulent credit card transactions. Forter and GMO-PG jointly verified from the initial stage with Mercari, resulting in the introduction of Forter's AI judgment solution. Additionally, GMO-PG provides an API (Application Programming Interface) that standardly implements Forter's fraud detection function in its online comprehensive payment service "PG Multi-Payment Service." 【Background of Introduction】 Mercari has been implementing various fraud measures to create a safe and secure environment for customers, including measures against fraudulent credit card transactions. Until now, they have applied 3D Secure (Note 1) to transactions deemed necessary for authentication based on their own rules and conducted visual checks for transactions deemed necessary for confirmation. However, as fraudulent methods have become more sophisticated, they faced challenges such as the degradation of the payment experience due to the friction of 3D Secure (Note 2), increased human costs for chargebacks (Note 3), and the need to balance "security assurance" with "providing a smooth payment experience for genuine customers," leading to the selection of a new solution for fraudulent payment measures. (Note 1) A mechanism for authenticating the cardholder in online credit card payments. Card companies may require additional authentication based on the information they hold. (Note 2) The hassle or interruption that users experience during the payment process. This includes transitions to authentication screens and entering passwords. (Note 3) A system where, if a cardholder claims they did not consent to a transaction due to fraudulent use of their credit card, the card company cancels the sales of that transaction, and the merchant bears the cost. 【Selection of Forter and Results of Preliminary Verification】 In the preliminary verification conducted prior to full implementation, Forter demonstrated results exceeding the evaluation criteria set by Mercari in the following three areas: ① Reduced the usage rate of 3D Secure and improved credit card GMV (Note 4) Forter returns a judgment with three options at the time of transaction request: "OK (approved) / NG (rejected) / 3D Secure (recommended)." If it is a three-choice option, merchants (Note 5) can avoid applying 3D Secure to low-risk transactions and focus recommendations on transactions that require judgment. Compliance with the mandatory introduction of EMV 3-D Secure (Note 6) is also automated within the same mechanism. In the preliminary verification, the usage rate of 3D Secure decreased without expanding fraud risk, and credit card GMV improved. ② Reduced chargeback amounts to about one-tenth Forter has a global identity network (Note 7). It analyzes approximately 6,000 data attributes in real-time and assesses reliability for each transaction. Fraudulent methods evolve across borders. Therefore, Mercari emphasized the importance of a global data infrastructure that does not rely solely on its own data during the selection process. Although the chargeback occurrence rate was originally below the industry standard, it further improved in the preliminary verification, keeping chargeback amounts to about one-tenth of the previous system. No incidents were observed where genuine transactions were mistakenly hindered for transactions judged as rejected. ③ Reduced costs for visual checks and rule maintenance Forter updates its AI model and responds in real-time to new fraudulent methods occurring globally. Therefore, merchants do not need to maintain rules on their side. Visual checks are also automated, relieving Mercari of the burdensome manual tasks in fraud prevention. (Note 4) Sales from transactions made using credit cards. (Note 5) Businesses that accept payments via credit cards. In this case, it refers to Mercari. (Note 6) Based on guidelines from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, it refers to the introduction of EMV 3-D Secure (the latest standard of 3D Secure) required for EC merchants as a measure against fraudulent credit card use. (Note 7) A data infrastructure used to cross-sectionally accumulate transaction histories across multiple businesses to assess the identity and reliability of purchasers. 【Introduction through GMO-PG's Integrated API】 In this introduction, GMO-PG utilizes the Forter integrated interface built on the "PG Multi-Payment Service." Since the series of flows from Forter's fraud detection requests, the application of 3D Secure based on judgment results, to payment processing are consolidated in GMO-PG's API, Mercari was able to introduce Forter as an extension of its existing payment integration. This eliminated the need for separate API connection development and infrastructure construction with Forter, leading to reduced development workload and shortened the period from the start of verification to actual operation. 【Comments from Each Company】 ■ Mercari, Inc. Executive Officer VP of Customer Service / Trust and Safety Marketplace Keisuke Tanaka Mercari prioritizes creating an environment where everyone can conduct transactions safely and securely, and providing a smooth customer experience (UX) that minimizes friction during payment. Until now, we have countered increasingly sophisticated fraudsters with our own fraud detection rules and risk-based judgments of 3D Secure, but we faced a dilemma with genuine customers experiencing "cart abandonment." In the preliminary verification conducted in strong partnership with GMO-PG and Forter, we achieved the result of reducing chargebacks to about one-tenth while improving the success rate of payments, thus increasing credit card GMV. We are now completely free from tuning our own fraud detection rules and visual inspection tasks, and we are confident that we have built a solid payment infrastructure for scalable business development in the future. ■ Forter Country Manager for Japan Yosuke Noda We are very pleased that Mercari, a representative of Japan's e-commerce, has adopted Forter as a partner responsible for enhancing security and customer experience in payments. launches.full_text:
Ahead of peak season, merchants can now identify trusted AI agents and enable secure, headless checkout with a single no-code integration NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Forter, the Trust Intelligence platform for the future of commerce, introduced new capabilities designed to give commerce leaders the visibility, trust and control to securely embrace this rapidly emerging revenue channel. Forter's Agentic Commerce Engine enables merchants to verify agentic shoppers and provides the infrastructure to manage their end-to-end experience. Agentic orders across Forter's network have increased more than fourfold since August, while automated fraud has doubled in the last two months. Consumers are rapidly adopting AI personal assistants like Muse, Instinct and Grok Bot to search, compare and buy on their behalf. Bad actors are attempting to blend in to this traffic by using malicious agents or taking over legitimate ones to scale fraud and abuse. The ability to distinguish a trusted agent from a fraudulent one has never been more important. "Every merchant is now effectively opted in to agentic commerce, whether or not they've prepared for it," said Eran Vanounou, chief technology and product officer, Forter. "The choice merchants have isn't whether agentic traffic engages with their site this holiday season; it's whether they are equipped to control, optimize and drive revenue from it." Now available, Forter's Agentic Commerce Engine is the first complete solution for this channel combining trust intelligence with flexible infrastructure. The capabilities include: Fraud Management for Agentic Commerce identifies and decisions scraper- and agent-driven traffic in real time, distinguishing legitimate AI assistants from fraud and abuse bots. The capability is an extension of Forter's core Fraud Management offering and is now available for all customers.

The capability is an extension of Forter's core Management offering and is now available for all customers. Agentic Orchestration enables headless checkout via agentic protocols so that merchants can optimize how agents purchase and set the conditions for each transaction. Through a single, no-code Forter integration, merchants can manage the full checkout experience for AI agents.

Through a single, no-code Forter integration, merchants can manage the full checkout experience for AI agents. AI Activity Dashboard shows merchants which AI agents are transacting on their site, so they can make informed decisions instead of guessing or blanket-blocking traffic that could represent new revenue. Merchants can analyze their transactions in the portal or with Forter Prism. Unlike the invite-only agentic pilots launched earlier this year, the new AI assistants can default to scraping a merchant's site when there isn't a headless checkout flow optimized for agents. Screen scraping is significantly slower, more costly and error-prone, negatively impacting the customer experience. In a controlled experiment, Forter found headless protocols were roughly 10 times faster and 5 times more token-efficient, and overall more likely to succeed, than scraping. Forter's Agentic Commerce Engine allows merchants to provide a superior customer buying experience by enabling headless checkout with a single integration. "There's a greater sense of urgency for agentic readiness as we head into peak season. Agentic traffic has had a meteoric rise over the last month and we expect that trend to continue," said Adam Davies, Director of AI, Forter. "We're giving merchants the intelligence and infrastructure to know which agentic transactions can be trusted and to control the end-to-end agentic shopping journey." launches.title: Forter launches five AI agents for commerce teams
launches.ai_summary: Forter has launched five AI agents for commerce teams as part of its Forter Prism product suite, targeting workflows in fraud analytics, chargeback disputes, abuse prevention, payment approvals, and system integration. The agents are designed to automate manual tasks that merchant teams handle across different functions, reducing manual reviews and improving response times. Forter has also opened early access to its Model Context Protocol, enabling its data to be accessed directly inside general AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, allowing teams to analyze performance trends and investigate transactions without switching between separate systems.

launches.full_text:
JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor

Forter has launched five AI agents and opened early access to its Model Context Protocol, with the new products aimed at commerce teams handling fraud, payments, disputes and system integration. The rollout expands Forter Prism, the company's agent-based product suite, with tools focused on analytics, chargeback disputes, abuse prevention, payment approval rates and integration work. The agents are designed for specific workflows that merchant teams often handle manually. The Analytics Agent is intended to give users information on risk analysis, transactions, decision rationale, business performance and customer profiles. The Dispute Agent is aimed at automating chargeback disputes, while the Abuse Agent is designed to help merchants set policies around returns, promotions and loyalty misuse. The Payments Agent focuses on payment performance and recommendations intended to lift authorisation rates. The Integration Agent is designed to connect Forter with existing systems through an AI coding assistant that can reduce deployment time. Forter is also making early access available to its Model Context Protocol, or MCP. The system allows Forter's data to be used inside AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, so merchant teams can work with the information inside software they already use. According to Forter, the protocol lets teams analyse performance trends, investigate transactions and produce executive summaries without switching between separate systems. The same corporate permissions and security controls apply when data is used through those AI tools. The launch comes as merchants face pressure to make faster decisions at key points in the customer journey, including account sign-up, payment approval and post-purchase disputes. Fraud checks, payment issues and customer claims often require staff to gather information from several sources, slowing responses and affecting sales or customer experience. Forter said its products are built on a network of more than two billion shoppers and nearly one million merchants. That data network has become central to how the company positions its fraud and commerce decision tools to retailers and online businesses. AWS was among the outside companies quoted in support of the launch. "The merchants winning right now are the ones who can move from signal to action faster than their competitors, and that gap only grows," said Vince Koh, Global Head, AWS Digital Commerce. "Forter's agents ground fraud and revenue decisions in a network of two billion shoppers, giving commerce teams that edge." Forter has framed the launch as part of a wider shift in online commerce, where AI is changing how consumers discover products, interact with sellers and complete transactions. In turn, merchants must process more information in real time when deciding whether to approve orders, investigate activity or respond to disputes. Workflow focus The five agents map to functions that often sit across different teams. Analytics and payments tend to be handled by commercial and operations staff, disputes by finance or risk teams, and abuse prevention by fraud and customer experience teams. Integration work usually falls to technical teams responsible for connecting third-party software to internal systems. By separating the tools in this way, Forter is targeting practical operational tasks rather than offering a single general-purpose assistant. The approach reflects a broader shift in business software towards narrower AI systems built around defined jobs and data sources. Market pressure Payments and fraud vendors have been adding more AI-led products as merchants look for ways to reduce manual reviews, cut fraud losses and improve approval rates on legitimate transactions. Chargebacks and policy abuse have also become more expensive issues for retailers, especially in sectors with high volumes of returns and promotions. For companies already using large language model tools internally, the MCP element may be one of the more notable parts of the announcement. Rather than requiring staff to sign into a separate dashboard to query Forter data, the protocol is intended to bring that information directly into general AI interfaces already used for internal analysis. Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer, Forter, said the aim was to make the company's data and decision tools easier to use in day-to-day work. "We've always built AI solutions for the people behind commerce who work tirelessly to offer the best experience to their consumers," said Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer, Forter. "Intelligence is now accessible in seconds, in context, and with the accuracy our global network has built over 13 years. These AI agents create a competitive advantage for every Forter customer, who can now accelerate time to impact across the entire customer journey."

With advances in artificial intelligence and cloud technologies, this market is set to experience rapid expansion, driven by the need for more sophisticated and integrated security solutions. Let's explore the current market outlook, key players, emerging trends, and the major segments that define this evolving sector.



Projected Market Size and Expansion of the Bot Security Market

The bot security market is anticipated to grow substantially, reaching a valuation of $2.12 billion by 2030. This growth reflects a robust compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.0%. Several factors contribute to this surge, including the rising adoption of AI-driven bot security systems, the integration of threat intelligence platforms, expanding cloud-based security services, growth in fintech and digital service sectors, and heightened emphasis on identity verification technologies. Key trends during the forecast period will feature advancements in bot detection and mitigation, improvements in API security, wider deployment of cloud-based bot security solutions, the expansion of managed security services, and the incorporation of threat intelligence.

Significant Acquisition Highlighting Market Consolidation

In January 2023, Forter, a US-based SaaS company specializing in unified identity protection, acquired Immue, a bot detection firm, for an undisclosed sum. This strategic move aims to enhance Forter's fraud management platform by integrating Immue's cutting-edge technology, which includes a bot mitigation layer, an undefeatable Captcha system, and the capability to manage bot activity during high-demand events such as flash sales and hype periods.

Key Trends Shaping Opportunities in the Bot Security Sector

Top players in the bot security market are increasingly focusing on advanced SaaS-based security portfolios to protect applications comprehensively. These portfolios emphasize securing cloud investments, assessing vendor security, maintaining data privacy, and ensuring compliance across services. For instance, in April 2023, F5-specializing in multi-cloud application security and delivery-introduced new security features aimed at giving customers greater control over applications and APIs across on-premises, cloud, and edge environments. By leveraging machine learning, these enhancements enable advanced API endpoint discovery, anomaly detection, telemetry, and behavioral analysis, helping organizations defend against malicious bots and automated attacks targeting web and mobile platforms.



Detailed Segmentation of the Bot Security Market

The bot security market is categorized into several segments as follows:

1) Component: Solutions and Services

2) Security Type: Web Security, Mobile Security, and Application Programming Interface (API) Security

3) Deployment Mode: Cloud-Based and On-Premises

4) Vertical Markets: Retail and eCommerce, Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), Government and Defense, Healthcare, Media and Entertainment, Travel and Hospitality, and Information Technology (IT) and Telecom



Further subsegments under solutions include bot detection and mitigation, authentication and identity verification, monitoring and reporting, API security, web application firewalls (WAF), and threat intelligence. Service subsegments cover consulting, implementation, managed services, support and maintenance, as well as training and education.

launches.full_text:
MPE 2026: Forter on Preparing Merchants to Safely Engage with Agentic Commerce

Share this post: Share on LinkedIn Share on Email Share on WhatsApp At MPE 2026, Adam Davies, Director of AI at Forter, dives into how they are redefining fraud prevention and payment processing, turning what used to be a business drag into a driver for growth. Davies explains that when Forter launched 13 years ago, the main goal was to modernize fraud management by replacing outdated, static rules with automated, scalable technology. Forter notes that those old systems often failed by declining valuable, trustworthy customers or, conversely, letting fraudulent ones through. Davies highlights that Forter has expanded its focus significantly beyond just fraud management to include payment optimization. Today, Forter’s mission is to help merchants grow by transforming their fraud and payment systems from being a simple cost center into a powerful revenue optimization engine. According to Davies, while most industry players focus on minimizing chargebacks from fraudulent transactions, many overlook the substantial revenue loss caused by falsely declining good customers. Forter addresses this by accurately assessing the trustworthiness of every transaction, ensuring legitimate customers enjoy a frictionless, excellent buying experience that drives up merchant conversion rates. On the payment side, Davies details how Forter uses intelligent decision-making, for instance, choosing the right payment rail, network, or PSP, to boost approval rates and simultaneously reduce processing costs. Looking ahead, Davies identifies agentic commerce as the major trend with real substance behind the buzzword and this new channel introduces complex security and engineering challenges. Davies emphasizes that Forter is heavily investing in solutions to equip merchants with the technology required to engage with this channel safely. By embedding their core capabilities around identity, trust, and payment optimization into this new infrastructure, Forter ensures that transactions originating from AI agents are secure while maintaining high conversion levels. Finally, Davies speaks positively about the value of attending MPE and describes the event as a crucial meeting place where partners, vendors, and merchants connect to have real conversations. The primary benefit, Davies concludes, is the efficient networking opportunity, getting all the experts in one room to discuss merchant pain points, find synergies for future solutions, and explore new opportunities for partnership and client engagement.

launches.title: Forter unveils AI copilot to tackle surging fraud risk
launches.ai_summary: Fraud prevention specialist Forter has launched an AI copilot called Forter Prism, reporting a 2,107% surge in agentic commerce activity and a 202% rise in automated fraud attempts across its network of 400,000 businesses over the past year. The new product provides merchants with natural language querying, transaction investigation, and benchmarking tools to identify and respond to AI-driven fraud threats. The launch comes as retailers prepare for the 2025 peak shopping season amid rising volumes of AI-driven traffic and evolving fraud tactics.
launches.author: Sofiah Nichole Salivio
launches.full_text:
Fraud prevention specialist Forter has launched an artificial intelligence copilot called Forter Prism, as the company reports a sharp rise in automated fraud attempts and agent-driven online shopping activity across its network. The company said it has recorded a 2,107% increase in what it terms agentic activity over the past six months. It also reported a 202% rise in automated fraud attempts over the last year among the 400,000 businesses that use its services. Forter positions Prism as a conversational tool that sits inside its existing portal for merchants. The product focuses on faster investigation of transactions, streamlined analysis, and the creation of dashboards that summarise performance trends. The launch comes as retailers prepare for the 2025 peak shopping season. Many brands face rising volumes of AI-driven traffic and shifting fraud tactics alongside pressure to maintain approval rates and customer experience. Rising agent activity Forter uses the term agentic commerce for transactions or traffic that involve software agents or automated tools. These can research prices, place orders or attempt to exploit vulnerabilities at scale. The company said its latest product updates address what it describes as a visibility gap for merchants. Many businesses struggle to see how much of their traffic and transaction volume involves agents and how much of that activity links to fraud. Forter has expanded its Agentic Activity dashboard with new benchmarks. Merchants can compare their AI-related traffic against aggregated patterns drawn from Forter's global network. The benchmarks show how individual businesses sit against peers on measures such as volume, growth rates and fraud exposure. The company has also added more granular views by region and vertical. It said merchants can examine how agentic commerce differs across markets and sectors and can track shifts over time. Inside Forter Prism Forter Prism functions as an in-portal copilot that responds to natural language queries from merchants. Users can ask questions about specific performance indicators, such as approval rates or chargebacks, and the tool returns summarised data. The company said Prism can explain why a particular metric has changed in recent periods. It can also generate dashboards that present operational views of performance, which would otherwise require manual set-up. Prism includes a transaction investigation feature. It surfaces the data points that Forter's systems used when approving or declining an individual transaction. The copilot then summarises the rationale in non-technical language. One customer described the launch as part of a broader drive for efficiency. "Every retailer, merchant, and direct-to-consumer brand is looking to find ways to be more efficient - not just for the sake of cost savings, but truly to keep pace with the speed of evolving consumer behaviour and expectations", said Rachel Levy, Chief Operating Officer, Brooklinen. "Forter has always stood out in how they put the retailers and brands at the heart of their solutions. With Forter Prism, they are delivering yet another major innovation that will support the balance of revenue generation and consumer satisfaction." Benchmarking fraud risk Forter said many merchants do not know whether AI agents are just referring users or actively making purchases on their sites. The company added that some merchants do not know whether agents feature in fraud attempts against their businesses. The new network benchmarks aim to set a baseline for each customer's exposure to AI-driven traffic. Forter said this should make it easier for merchants to decide which areas of their fraud and customer experience strategies need earlier attention. The firm has also updated its public AI dashboard. It now contains more detailed regional and sector breakdowns and uses AI to generate explanations of the patterns it shows. Forter said the combination of Prism, benchmarks and updated dashboards offers a fuller view of the emerging agentic commerce channel. It argued that this channel is now material for both growth and fraud risk as more consumers and businesses adopt AI tools. Eran Vanounou, Chief Technology Officer at Forter, said the pace of change in the market demanded faster decision-making. "With market shifts and threats moving this fast, businesses can't afford to risk missing a critical agentic insight or manually translate complex data into decisions," said Vanounou. "These latest innovations are giving businesses the speed, insight and confidence to navigate peak season with ease."

product_offering.core_offering: Forter provides a SaaS Trust Platform for digital commerce that delivers real-time, automated fraud prevention, payment optimization, chargeback management, account protection, and abuse prevention for online merchants and payment service providers. The platform is built on an identity graph of more than 2 billion consumers across 250,000+ storefronts, uses patented Decision AI to approve or decline transactions in under one second, and processes more than $400 billion in annual transaction value.
product_offering.differentiator: Identity intelligence at scale (2B+ identities across 250,000+ storefronts, 25% of global population); patented Decision AI that decodes both human and agent behavior plus issuer logic; consortium network effect where every merchant strengthens collective intelligence; first-mover in establishing the Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol open standard for AI agent authentication; fully automated real-time decisions (under 1 second, 99% of the time) versus legacy rules-based or manual review systems.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Increases transaction approval rates while reducing false declines (46% average reduction in false declines); reduces chargeback losses (72% average reduction in chargeback rates); automates manual fraud and payment review workflows; enables PSD2 compliance without sacrificing conversion; provides chargeback liability shift via Smart 3DS; supports multiple payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, ACH, gift cards); delivers unified fraud, payment, dispute, account protection, and abuse prevention decisions in a single platform.
product_offering.product_overview: Forter is a unified Trust Platform for digital commerce built on an identity graph of more than 2 billion consumers across 250,000+ storefronts and over $400 billion in annual transaction value. Its architecture combines a core decisioning platform with five primary product modules — Fraud Management, Payment Optimization, Dispute Management, Account Protection, and Abuse Prevention — augmented by Forter Element (a white-label offering for payment service providers) and an AI layer comprising Forter Prism (the AI copilot), Forter Agents (Analytics, Payments, Dispute, Abuse, and Integration Agents), and the Agentic Orchestration Suite (which connects merchants to agentic commerce protocols and powers the Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol). Together these products enable merchants to identify trusted customers in real time, automate fraud and abuse decisions, optimize payment authorization, recover chargeback revenue, and safely engage with agentic commerce initiated by AI agents.

expansion_highlight.description: Launch of the Agentic Orchestration Suite (Feb 2026) and the Forter Prism AI Agents suite (June 2026) — five agents (Analytics, Payments, Dispute, Abuse, Integration) plus MCP integration with ChatGPT/Claude. This represents a pivot from fraud SaaS to an agentic commerce and AI-ops platform, opening a new TAM estimated in the tens of billions as AI shopping agents proliferate.

Strategic alignment with Mastercard Agent Pay and the Agent Pay Acceptance Framework, plus partnership on Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), and OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP). Authoring TACP as an open standard positions Forter as the identity layer beneath competing agentic commerce protocols — a deliberate standards-formation play.

EU Data Center launched in Ireland (Oct 2024) for GDPR-compliant processing, Japan expansion via Atmos and Toys R Us Japan case studies plus GMO Payment Gateway and Veritrans partnerships, and reported 2,107% surge in agentic commerce activity across the network (Jan 2026). Geographic footprint now spans North America, EMEA, APAC, and Japan with localized PSP rails.

McDonald's global partnership (announced Jan 2026) marks Forter's first major QSR anchor and signals expansion into food service and franchisee-protected digital ecosystems beyond traditional retail/travel verticals. The QSR vertical has distinct fraud patterns (loyalty, mobile order-ahead, franchise risk) that broaden product surface.

Forter's Trusted Agentic Commerce was listed in the AWS Marketplace AI Agents and Tools category (July 2025) and the Adobe Exchange marketplace (Nov 2025), enabling procurement via AWS committed spend (EDP) and direct Adobe merchant self-service — a shift from pure direct enterprise sales to marketplace-led mid-market reach.

Significant C-suite buildout: new CFO Jim Lejeal and CPO Cyndy Lobb (Mar 2025), new CCO Ozge Tuncel Ozcan, and creation of a first-ever Chief Merchant role filled by Jennifer Howard (May 2026). The Chief Merchant hire signals an explicit pivot toward merchant community expansion and product co-development, typical of pre-IPO or large-stage scaling.

company_assessment.market_position: Forter is a privately held, venture-backed SaaS company founded in 2013 and headquartered in New York, with engineering roots in Tel Aviv and regional offices in London, Singapore, and an EU Data Center in Ireland. The company operates a Trust Platform for digital commerce and is recognized as a Leader in fraud detection and prevention by Frost & Sullivan (four consecutive years) and has been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 for five consecutive years, with a $3 billion valuation following its 2021 Series F.

strengths.details: Forter's first-mover position in agent authentication (TACP open standard, Agentic Orchestration Suite, partnerships with Mastercard Agent Pay, Google UCP, and AWS Marketplace AI Agents) positions the company to capture disproportionate share of a new trust-and-identity spend category as AI agents become meaningful commerce initiators. The 2,107% year-over-year surge in agentic commerce activity across Forter's network (reported January 2026) provides early evidence that the market is forming around Forter's data assets and protocol.
strengths.headline: Foundational identity layer for agentic commerce

strengths.details: Each merchant added to Forter's 250,000+ storefront network strengthens the identity graph that powers fraud decisions for all customers. As the platform scales toward more than 1 million merchants serving 2B+ shoppers, the data advantage over single-tenant or regional fraud vendors becomes increasingly defensible, supporting pricing power and reduced churn over time.
strengths.headline: Network-effect moat deepens with each merchant

strengths.details: Forter's evolution from a single-product fraud vendor to a unified Trust Platform (Fraud Management + Payment Optimization + Dispute + Account Protection + Abuse Prevention + AI Agents + Agentic Orchestration) enables cross-sell into existing accounts. Adoption of Forter Prism AI agents and Predictive Payment Routing at existing customers like Priceline, ASOS, and Adidas creates meaningful ARPU expansion without requiring new logo acquisition.
strengths.headline: Platform expansion drives ARPU and wallet share

strengths.details: Forter Element's OEM motion with PSPs (Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, PayU, GMO, Veritrans) brings Forter's capabilities to thousands of merchants via single integrations, including small and mid-market merchants who would not buy direct. This channel expands total addressable market while Forter also monetizes usage-based pricing on transaction volume.
strengths.headline: Embedded PSP distribution unlocks SMB and mid-market

strengths.details: Flagship alliances with McDonald's (January 2026 global rollout), Mastercard (Agent Pay), Google (UCP/AP2), AWS (Retail Competency, AI Agents Marketplace), Shopify (Premier Partner), and Salesforce (no-code integration) collectively position Forter as the de facto trust layer for digital commerce. These partnerships expand distribution, validate the platform, and create references that accelerate enterprise sales cycles.
strengths.headline: Strategic partnerships validate platform positioning

weakness.details: Stripe Radar, Shopify's built-in fraud analysis, Adyen risk engine, and PayPal's own fraud products are increasingly capable and bundled free or at marginal cost with payment processing. As merchants consolidate vendors, Forter's standalone value proposition could erode, particularly in mid-market and SMB where usage economics matter most.
weakness.headline: Platform-native fraud tools compress direct-vendor opportunity

weakness.details: Forter's TACP competes with Google UCP, OpenAI ACP, Mastercard Agent Pay, and emerging merchant-direct frameworks. If the market consolidates around a competitor's protocol, Forter's Agentic Orchestration Suite could become a single-customer integration rather than the foundational standard, materially reducing the long-term TAM the company can capture from agentic commerce.
weakness.headline: Agentic commerce standard wars risk stranded investment

weakness.details: Forter monetizes via enterprise subscriptions tied to transaction volume and a usage component (over $400B in annual transaction value processed). A consumer-spending recession or e-commerce contraction would directly compress revenue, while a large fixed cost base (501-1,000 employees, global offices) would amplify operating-leverage risk.
weakness.headline: Usage-based revenue exposed to macro-driven transaction slowdown

weakness.details: Forter's last disclosed valuation was $3B in May 2021, and no subsequent funding round has been publicly disclosed. With public-market peers Riskified and Signifyd trading well below historical highs, Forter may face down-round pressure or delayed liquidity. The hiring of a CFO (Jim Lejeal, March 2025) signals IPO preparation, but execution risk around timing and valuation is material.
weakness.headline: Stale valuation creates IPO/M&A uncertainty

weakness.details: A 202% year-over-year rise in automated fraud attempts across Forter's network signals an arms race in which attackers rapidly adapt to AI-based detection. Persistent false-positive declines (despite reported 46% reductions) or high-profile chargeback incidents at marquee customers could undermine trust in the platform's core promise of fully automated trust decisions.
weakness.headline: Rising automated fraud erodes core value proposition

competitive_moat.details: Forter's network spans 2 billion+ identities across 250,000+ storefronts with up to 6,000 behavioral and hard data attributes per identity — covering roughly 25% of the global population. This dataset is proprietary, grows with every transaction, and underpins the predictive accuracy of every model Forter ships; it cannot be replicated by competitors without comparable merchant scale and years of historical signal collection.

Every merchant added to the network improves fraud, payment, and abuse detection for all others. Named brand customers (Wayfair, Instacart, Adidas, Priceline, McDonald's) materially strengthen collective intelligence, and the consortium design means Forter's accuracy improves with scale rather than degrades — a classic two-sided network effect.

Forter holds a patented Decision AI and authored the Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol (TACP), an open cryptographic standard for AI agent authentication using JSON Web Encryption (RFC 7516), published on GitHub. The TACP authorship positions Forter as a foundational standards-setter in a new market (agentic commerce) rather than a feature vendor.

Forter is the only fraud prevention partner with Shopify Premier status and AWS Retail Competency, and is integrated natively with Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Adobe Commerce, SAP, commercetools, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, PayU, Mastercard, and Google. Forter Element embeds Forter's decisioning inside PSP platforms, creating downstream lock-in across thousands of merchants per PSP partner.

The Trust Platform unifies fraud, payment routing, disputes, account protection, and abuse prevention into a single decisioning layer; replacing it would require re-instrumenting checkout, account, and back-office workflows plus losing the historical chargeback evidence and issuer optimization models. Annual contracts and embedded PSP integrations amplify churn friction.

Forter Element (OEM motion) and AWS Marketplace listings allow Forter to reach thousands of merchants without a direct sales touch, while the IMPACT conference series (NYC, London, Jinan) and a deep SI partner network (PwC, Infosys, Perficient, Endava) compress enterprise sales cycles. Distribution is strong but still dependent on direct enterprise field sales for large flagship deals.

key_risks.details: Forter's last disclosed capital raise was the $300M Series F at a $3B valuation in May 2021. With ~$525M+ raised to date and 501-1,000 employees, the absence of subsequent primary funding rounds over 4+ years could indicate capital constraints, a longer path to profitability, or delayed liquidity plans relative to public-market-ready peers (Riskified, Signifyd).
key_risks.headline: No fresh funding round disclosed since May 2021 Series F

key_risks.details: Direct competitors include Riskified, Signifyd, Sift, Kount (Equifax), and Ravelin, alongside platform-native solutions such as Stripe Radar, Shopify's built-in fraud analysis, Adyen's risk engine, and PayPal's own fraud products. Network-effect advantages may be partially neutralized by merchants consolidating spend with their payment processor's bundled risk offering.
key_risks.headline: Intense competition from well-funded direct peers and platform-native fraud tools

key_risks.details: Forter reported a 2,107% surge in agentic commerce activity across its network alongside a 202% rise in automated fraud attempts (reported January 2026). As Forter pioneers agent authentication, it also becomes the high-value target whose detection failures would be highly visible to enterprise customers.
key_risks.headline: Agentic commerce opportunity creates parallel attack surface for fraudsters

key_risks.details: CEO/co-founder Michael Reitblat and CTO Eran Vanounou (author of TACP) are the public faces of Forter's AI strategy and the agentic commerce bet. Departure of either would materially impact continuity of the most differentiated technical roadmap.
key_risks.headline: Key-person dependency on founder-CEO and CTO for strategic direction

key_risks.details: A large share of marquee customers operates in retail/apparel (Adidas, Puma, Nordstrom, Saks, PacSun, Shein, ASOS, Deckers), travel (Priceline, Kiwi.com), and marketplaces (eBay, G2A, Wayfair). Macro consumer-spending slowdowns directly compress merchant transaction volumes, which underpins Forter's usage-based pricing.
key_risks.headline: Customer concentration in cyclical discretionary verticals (apparel, luxury, travel)

key_risks.details: Forter's strategic bet on the Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol depends on AI agent developers, merchants, and PSPs choosing Forter's standard over competing agentic frameworks (Google UCP, OpenAI ACP, Mastercard Agent Pay). Failure to achieve network adoption would reduce the Agentic Orchestration Suite to a single-vendor product rather than the foundational trust layer.
key_risks.headline: TACP open standard requires broad ecosystem adoption to deliver value

key_highlights.details: Forter's Identity Intelligence Network covers ~25% of the global population with up to 6,000 attributes per identity, processing $400B+ in annual transaction value. This consortium scale creates a structural data moat that strengthens with every merchant added and is materially difficult for competitors to replicate.
key_highlights.headline: Massive identity data network spanning 2B+ identities across 250,000+ storefronts

key_highlights.details: Named customers include Adidas, eBay, Nordstrom, Wayfair, Priceline, Instacart, HelloFresh, McDonald's, Chewy, ASOS, Shein, Saks Fifth Avenue, LG, Deckers Brands, SeatGeek, and Grubhub. A global McDonald's partnership (announced January 2026) extends reach into QSR digital ordering and loyalty.
key_highlights.headline: Blue-chip enterprise customer roster across retail, travel, marketplaces, and QSR

key_highlights.details: Series F of $300M closed in May 2021 at a $3B post-money valuation, led by Tiger Global with participation from Sequoia Capital Israel, Bessemer, Salesforce Ventures, L Catterton, March Capital, Scale Venture Partners, NewView Capital, Citi Ventures, Samsung NEXT, and others.
key_highlights.headline: Last private valuation of $3B backed by tier-1 venture investors

key_highlights.details: Forter authored the Trusted Agentic Commerce Protocol (TACP), an open standard using JSON Web Encryption (RFC 7516) for AI agent authentication, with a public GitHub repository. The Agentic Orchestration Suite, partnerships with Mastercard Agent Pay, Google UCP, and AWS Marketplace AI Agents category listing position Forter as a foundational identity layer for agent-initiated transactions.
key_highlights.headline: First-mover position in agentic commerce trust with proprietary open standard (TACP)

key_highlights.details: Named to the Forbes Cloud 100 for the fifth consecutive year (2025) and recognized as a Leader in the Frost & Sullivan Radar Report for Fraud Detection & Prevention (KYU) for the fourth consecutive year. Also holds AWS Retail Competency (only fraud partner with this distinction) and Shopify Premier Partner status.
key_highlights.headline: Consistent third-party recognition with five-year Forbes Cloud 100 streak

key_highlights.details: Beyond core Fraud Management, Forter now offers Payment Optimization (Predictive Payment Routing, Issuer Optimization, Smart 3DS, PSD2/Japan 3DS), Dispute Management, Account Protection, Abuse Prevention, and the Forter Prism AI agent suite. Forter Element embeds fraud decisioning into PSPs (Checkout.com, Nuvei, Stripe, PayU) as an OEM channel.
key_highlights.headline: Platform expansion from fraud to payment optimization and agentic orchestration increases wallet share

key_highlights.details: Distribution spans direct enterprise sales, channel/partner ecosystem (PwC, Infosys, Perficient, Endava, Jellyfish), OEM via PSPs, AWS Marketplace listing, and the proprietary IMPACT Conference series across NYC, London, and China. Offices in New York, Tel Aviv, London, Singapore, plus an EU Data Center in Ireland launched October 2024.
key_highlights.headline: Multi-channel distribution and global operational footprint

customer_concentration.details: Forter's customer base sits between concentrated and distributed. Marquee enterprise anchors — McDonald's, Priceline, Wayfair, ASOS, Adidas, Nordstrom, eBay, Instacart, HelloFresh, Shein, Saks Fifth Avenue — account for material revenue given enterprise quote-based, multi-year contracts, but the broader network spans 250,000+ storefronts and ~400,000 online businesses, of which the majority access Forter indirectly through PSP partners (Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, PayU) or via Forter Element embedded offerings. This dual structure reduces top-line concentration risk relative to pure-play enterprise SaaS, while the PSP channel creates a long tail of smaller merchants that smooths revenue volatility. However, the named enterprise anchor set is dominated by retail and travel with overlap on the IMPACT Awards roster (Priceline, Wayfair, McDonald's), suggesting meaningful wallet share among a relatively small number of large logos. Net: Moderate concentration risk with the largest revenue dollars concentrated in a few dozen enterprise deals, but the underlying transaction volume is broadly diversified across the consortium.

launches.title: Sama to reveal case prototypes, PSUs and AIO coolers at Computex 2026
launches.ai_summary: Sama will showcase PC case prototypes, AIO liquid coolers, and power supplies at Computex 2026. The cases include the V80 and V70 with alternative layouts, while the Q80 and Q40 AIOs feature dual screens and rotating pump blocks. New PSUs like the P1650 and G850 comply with Intel ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 standards.
launches.author: João Silva

industries.name: Cooling & Thermal Solutions (Air/Liquid, fans, thermal paste)

launches.full_text:
Sama has announced its product showcase for Computex 2026, which takes place next week. At the event, they will preview the upcoming lineup of PC cases, as well as new AIO liquid coolers and power supplies.

The showcase includes two PC case prototypes designed around alternative internal layouts. The Sama V80 features a dual-curved tempered-glass front panel built into a floating chassis design with integrated ambient lighting, a built-in 60W fast-charging port, and an isolated internal airflow duct directed at the graphics card. The Sama V70 relies on a front-mounted power supply to clear up internal viewing angles, shifting away from a traditional box-shaped exterior.

Sama is also expanding its AIO liquid cooling lineup with the Q80. This one has a metal-finish enclosure and a dual-screen configuration with interchangeable 4-inch and 6-inch IPS display panels, letting users separate hardware-monitoring from desktop content. The Sama Q40 uses a motorised rotating outer ring on the pump block to produce three-dimensional physical motion, paired with a central customisable LCD and three pre-installed 28mm-thick cooling fans trimmed with side-facing ARGB infinity mirrors.

As for the PSUs, the lineup has been updated with a series of new models, including the P1650, P1350, P1200, P1000, G1000, and G850. The entire lineup complies with Intel ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 standards, and feature a fully modular cable layout.

launches.title: Sama launches S50 PC case with back-connect support and ARGB fans
launches.ai_summary: Sama launched the S50, a compact ATX case with four pre-installed 120mm ARGB PWM fans, priced at $110. It supports ATX, Micro-ATX, Mini-ITX, and back-connect motherboards, plus GPUs up to 410mm and CPUs up to 165mm. The case is available in black or white.
launches.author: Matthew Wilson
launches.full_text:
Sama has introduced the S50, a compact ATX case that ships with four pre‑installed 120mm ARGB PWM fans, aiming to deliver strong airflow and lighting straight out of the box.

The S50 uses a front‑mounted PSU compartment to reduce overall footprint while maintaining hardware compatibility. It supports ATX, Micro‑ATX, Mini‑ITX, and back‑connect ATX/Micro‑ATX motherboards, along with graphics cards up to 410mm long, CPU coolers up to 165mm tall, and ATX power supplies up to 180mm long. For expanded cooling, the case accommodates up to 11 fans and a 360mm radiator at the top.

In the table below, you can see the full spec sheet for the case:

launches.title: Es'hailSat expands channel offerings
launches.ai_summary: Es'hailSat added Sama Jordan TV to its video distribution lineup at the 26° East orbital position via the Es'hail-2 satellite. The move brings a leading regional news broadcaster to the satellite's footprint, which covers the Middle East and North Africa.
launches.author: Qatar Tribune

industries.name: Satellite Video & Media Distribution (DTH, Contribution/Distribution, Occasional Use)

iptc_codes.name: air and space accident and incident

launches.full_text:
DOHA: Es'hailSat, the Qatar Satellite Company, announced that it has expanded its channel offerings by incorporating Sama Jordan TV channel into its video distribution lineup at the 26° East orbital position, facilitated by the Es'hail-2 satellite.

"Es'hailSat is delighted to welcome Sama Jordan TV channel and bring on board one of the region's leading news broadcasters to our satellite hotspot," President and CEO of Es'hailSat Ali Ahmed Al Kuwari said.

"We believe that the reliability and expertise in providing satellite services by Es'hailSat aligns perfectly with Sama Jordan's vision to serve as a leading news broadcaster, providing comprehensive and reliable information to the country's public," he added.

CEO of Sama Jordan TV, Rabea Al Awamleh, stated: "We have chosen to broadcast via the Es'hailSat satellite due to its strategic importance at the orbital position of 26° East. This ensures that Sama Jordan TV will be alongside the majority of key channels in the region that also transmit through Es'hailSat."

The Es'hailSat satellite footprint strategically encompasses the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, optimising signal coverage and enabling significant viewership potential for the news broadcaster's channel from Jordan throughout this expansive area.

launches.title: Data Curation Capabilities and Enhanced 3D & LiDAR Annotation Features
launches.ai_summary: Sama announced new data curation and enhanced 3D and LiDAR annotation features for its ML platform. The features aim to improve model accuracy with less data, with 3D and LiDAR annotations producing up to 94-98% IOU. The company also highlights active learning and expert partnerships for quality rubrics and integrations.
launches.full_text: Table of Contents Prioritize labels that will have the biggest impact on your model’s performance with Sama Curate Sama Curate can bring you better model accuracy with less data for higher ROI on your models. Sama Annotate: New and improved 3D and LiDAR features Sama delivers high-quality 3D and LiDAR labels at scale. Talk to an Expert Today, Sama is thrilled to announce a host of new offerings which will allow us to continue to power our customers’ ML models with unmatched accuracy, scale, and efficiency.This includes data curation and enhanced 3D and LiDAR annotation features. Here’s a rundown of what’s new. Prioritize labels that will have the biggest impact on your model’s performance with Sama Curate Many sources cite that 80% of a data scientist’s time is spent finding, cleaning, and organizing data. This is because the most effective ML engineers understand that this sort of preparatory work is key to accelerating the development of their models in the long run. “Give me six hours to chop down a tree, and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.” - Abraham Lincoln It’s also why Sama is excited to introduce our data curation solution. Sama Curate offers seamless integration with the Sama Data Annotation Platform to provide the highest degree of automation to cost-effectively select and label massive amounts of data quickly with accuracy. Sama Curate ensures every labeled asset adds value for better accuracy with less data — and a quicker, more cost-effective path to production. With Sama Curate, ML engineers can be more strategic in selecting the data they send for annotation. Powerful visualization tools empower them to understand the diversity of their data and quickly identify edge cases. State-of-the-art data curation approaches such as Active Learning provide a continuous feedback loop to ensure AI practitioners are always prioritizing the most high-value data for their models. Sama Curate can bring you better model accuracy with less data for higher ROI on your models. Sama Annotate: New and improved 3D and LiDAR features Safety prerequisites in the autonomous vehicles industry have created the need for redundant perception, with companies requiring a fully integrated sensor suite — including LiDAR, RADAR, and 360-degree cameras — to train their models. The resulting data is notoriously difficult and expensive to label, leading to steep costs and poor model performance in unpredictable conditions. For years, Sama has been working to solve these challenges for the world’s largest vehicle and parts manufacturers, and today we’re ready to launch our enhanced 3D and LiDAR annotation features. Sama provides unparalleled tools and expertise to deliver uncompromisingly high-quality ground truth annotations for your 3D and LiDAR data. Sama annotation experts leverage our ML-powered platform to deliver labels with unmatched accuracy and speed for your sensor fusion, semantic and instance segmentation, and object tracking use cases. State-of-the-art 3D and LiDAR annotation tools boost annotation efficiency and allow you to achieve high quality at scale, predictably producing up to 94-98% IOU.In addition to our ML-powered platform, Sama machine learning researchers and technical solutions teams partner with you to become experts on your data: they develop robust quality rubrics for your requirements, seamless integrations for your systems, and solve for edge cases that can otherwise slow your path to production. Sama delivers high-quality 3D and LiDAR labels at scale. “Give me six hours to chop down a tree, and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.”- Abraham Lincoln This adage may come from a by-gone era, but the sentiment holds true.At Sama, we have long believed that efficiency improvements early in the ML model development process — whether curating your data, iterating early and often, or selecting the right annotation partner — have significant positive compounding effects, resulting in better label quality and model performance.These are just a few of the many exciting new features Sama has been working on to help you “sharpen your axe” before you set out to build your ML models — to ultimately bring you cost savings, efficiency improvements, and quicker time to market. Author Girish Kulkarni

launches.title: Sama Eliminates Repetitive Work in AI Data Labeling with Launch of Bulk Annotation
launches.ai_summary: Sama announced the launch of a new Bulk Annotation feature to improve AI data labeling efficiency and quality. The new tool significantly reduces manual effort and increases consistency during data annotation, with early pilots showing up to 80% faster results and a 25% reduction in inconsistencies.

launches.full_text:
This page contains press release content distributed by XPR Media. Members of the editorial and news staff of the USA TODAY Network were not involved in the creation of this content. Sama Eliminates Repetitive Work in AI Data Labeling with Launch of Bulk Annotation Sama New data classification feature transforms how enterprises build high-quality training data, delivering up to 80% faster results and 25% improvement in consistency, without sacrificing quality Sama , delivering data certainty for enterprise AI through tech-enabled annotation, validation and evaluation services, today announced a major advancement in how AI training data is created. The company’s new classification product with Bulk Annotation eliminates one of the industry’s most persistent inefficiencies: the need to manually label nearly identical items over and over again. Sama’s Bulk Annotation capabilities significantly reduce effort while increasing efficiency, accuracy and dataset consistency. Early pilots have shown to increase throughput up to 80% and reduce annotation inconsistencies as much as 25%, while maintaining Sama’s industry-leading quality standards. The repetitive process of data labeling is slow, expensive and prone to inconsistency, and it impacts every company building AI systems at scale. Whether categorizing thousands of product variants for e-commerce, validating outputs from large language models, or organizing vast document libraries, teams have traditionally needed to review and label each individual item, even when many items are essentially the same. Sama’s Bulk Annotation feature uses advanced machine learning techniques within the platform to identify groups of similar items, including duplicates, variants and near-matches, and present them together so annotators can classify entire groups at once. A single annotation is then applied across all related items, dramatically reducing wasted effort while improving the consistency of the final dataset. “As AI becomes mission-critical for more enterprises, the quality and efficiency of training data is now a competitive advantage,” said Duncan Curtis, SVP of AI product and technology at Sama. “Companies can’t afford to build AI on inconsistent data, but they also can’t afford to spend months on repetitive labeling work. Our Bulk Annotation feature solves both problems at once.” Unlike traditional annotation tools that simply speed up manual work, Sama’s solution rethinks the workflow entirely. The platform’s intelligence layer handles the complexity of grouping related items, so clients don’t need to prepare or restructure their data in advance. Quality assurance also becomes more efficient, with review teams able to validate at the group level rather than checking every individual item. This technology addresses a growing need across industries. Retailers managing catalogs with thousands of product variations can now annotate entire product families in one step. Companies deploying generative AI can validate model outputs more efficiently and consistently. Financial services and healthcare organizations dealing with complex documents benefit from faster classification even as their data requirements evolve. Bulk Annotation is designed to work whether data structures are stable or constantly changing, giving enterprises flexibility as their AI initiatives mature. “We created Bulk Annotation by listening to our workforce and clients,” said Karan Vasdev, product manager at Sama. “Following UX research and sampling from our R&D team that further validated frustrations we were hearing from both our annotators and our clients, we were able to design, build and deliver this new capability in under four months.” While other solutions rely on generic annotation tooling or fragmented labor pools, Sama integrates platform innovation with a managed, expert, in-house workforce. This alignment allows the company to optimize workflows end to end, achieving throughput and quality gains that are difficult to replicate elsewhere in the market. Bulk Annotation is available now to all Sama clients, and existing projects will be migrated seamlessly to the new version. About Sama Sama delivers data certainty for enterprise AI through tech-enabled annotation, validation and evaluation services. By combining advanced platforms with expert human judgment, Sama helps some of the world’s largest companies, including 30% of the Fortune 50, move AI models from development to production with confidence. With thousands of skilled data professionals and industry-leading quality guarantees, Sama tackles the critical challenge that over 63% of AI models fail to reach production due to poor data quality. Founded in 2008, Sama has delivered more than 40 billion data points and created employment opportunities that have helped over 70,000 people lift themselves out of poverty. As a certified B Corporation, Sama is committed to advancing both technological innovation and social impact. Learn more at www.sama.com . Wednesday, 19 November 2025 08:00 AM
Company Update
New data classification feature transforms how enterprises build high-quality training data, delivering up to 80% faster results and 25% improvement in consistency, without sacrificing quality
SAN FRANCISCO, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2025 / Sama, delivering data certainty for enterprise AI through tech-enabled annotation, validation and evaluation services, today announced a major advancement in how AI training data is created. The company's new classification product with Bulk Annotation eliminates one of the industry's most persistent inefficiencies: the need to manually label nearly identical items over and over again. Sama's Bulk Annotation capabilities significantly reduce effort while increasing efficiency, accuracy and dataset consistency. Early pilots have shown to increase throughput up to 80% and reduce annotation inconsistencies as much as 25%, while maintaining Sama's industry-leading quality standards.
The repetitive process of data labeling is slow, expensive and prone to inconsistency, and it impacts every company building AI systems at scale. Whether categorizing thousands of product variants for e-commerce, validating outputs from large language models, or organizing vast document libraries, teams have traditionally needed to review and label each individual item, even when many items are essentially the same.
Sama's Bulk Annotation feature uses advanced machine learning techniques within the platform to identify groups of similar items, including duplicates, variants and near-matches, and present them together so annotators can classify entire groups at once. A single annotation is then applied across all related items, dramatically reducing wasted effort while improving the consistency of the final dataset.
"As AI becomes mission-critical for more enterprises, the quality and efficiency of training data is now a competitive advantage," said Duncan Curtis, SVP of AI product and technology at Sama. "Companies can't afford to build AI on inconsistent data, but they also can't afford to spend months on repetitive labeling work. Our Bulk Annotation feature solves both problems at once."
Unlike traditional annotation tools that simply speed up manual work, Sama's solution rethinks the workflow entirely. The platform's intelligence layer handles the complexity of grouping related items, so clients don't need to prepare or restructure their data in advance. Quality assurance also becomes more efficient, with review teams able to validate at the group level rather than checking every individual item.
This technology addresses a growing need across industries. Retailers managing catalogs with thousands of product variations can now annotate entire product families in one step. Companies deploying generative AI can validate model outputs more efficiently and consistently. Financial services and healthcare organizations dealing with complex documents benefit from faster classification even as their data requirements evolve. Bulk Annotation is designed to work whether data structures are stable or constantly changing, giving enterprises flexibility as their AI initiatives mature.
"We created Bulk Annotation by listening to our workforce and clients," said Karan Vasdev, product manager at Sama. "Following UX research and sampling from our R&D team that further validated frustrations we were hearing from both our annotators and our clients, we were able to design, build and deliver this new capability in under four months."
While other solutions rely on generic annotation tooling or fragmented labor pools, Sama integrates platform innovation with a managed, expert, in-house workforce. This alignment allows the company to optimize workflows end to end, achieving throughput and quality gains that are difficult to replicate elsewhere in the market.
Bulk Annotation is available now to all Sama clients, and existing projects will be migrated seamlessly to the new version.

By combining advanced platforms with expert human judgment, Sama helps some of the world's largest companies, including 30% of the Fortune 50, move AI models from development to production with confidence. funding_news.ai_summary: Leila Janah, a social entrepreneur and founder of companies aimed at reducing global poverty, died on January 24 at the age of 37 due to complications from epithelioid sarcoma. She founded Samasource, LXMI, and Samaschool, employing thousands in countries including Kenya, Uganda, and India to provide decent wages and training. Her efforts helped over 50,000 people escape poverty, illustrating the potential of marginalized individuals in the global economy.

funding_news.full_text:
Woman Entrepreneur Leila Janah, a social entrepreneur who was on a mission to end global poverty dies at 37 Leila Janah founded three companies - Samasource, LXMI and Samaschool to help marginalised and poor people the opportunity to earn a decent wage. She had a rare form of soft-tissue cancer. Nirandhi Gowthaman312 Stories Monday February 03, 2020 , 2 min Read Leila Janah, a social entrepreneur who was on a mission to end global poverty died on January 24 in a hospital in Manhattan. She died from complications of epithelioid sarcoma. She was 37.

She was the founder of Samasource, an artificial intelligence company which employs nearly 3,000 people in Kenya, Uganda and India. She believed that the intellect of the poorest people in the world was an untapped source in the global economy.

Leila Janah was on a mission to end global poverty. (Image credits:Lucas Jackson/Reuters) Leila was also the founder and CEO of LXMI, a fair-trade, organic skin care company, and Samaschool, a nonprofit organisation that trains people in digital skills, according to Samasource. The luxury cosmetic brand that she started also employed marginalised people and gave them a decent wage. She started the company in 2015 after she saw local people harvesting local nuts in Benin.

It employs hundreds of poor women along the Nile River Valley, largely in Uganda, to harvest Nilotica nuts and turn them into a butter that is exported to the United States for use in the production of its skin-care products. The company has hired more people from other African countries and in India to harvest other ingredients for its products.

According to Samasource, at least half the people hired by the company are women. Its employees have worked under contracts with companies including Microsoft, Google, Facebook, Walmart, Getty Images, Glassdoor and Vulcan Capital. According to the company’s website, it is one of the largest employers in East Africa and has helped more than 50,000 people lift themselves out of poverty.

In a Facebook post in November, she opened up about her battle with cancer. She wrote, "Epithelioid sarcoma is a rare, strange beast. As it moves through my body, I'm trying to understand what it could possibly teach me. My biggest lesson is awe: I'm awe-struck by the complexity of human biology, and equally by the almost mystical power of human connection and love flowing my way." Sign up for our exclusive newsletters. Subscribe to check out our popular newsletters. * indicates mandatory fields

Epithelioid sarcoma is a rare, slow-growing type of soft tissue cancer and typically starts as a painless bump.

She was born to Indian immigrant parents, Sahadev Chirayath and Martine Janah in 1982 in Lewiston, New York, near Niagara Falls. She is survived by her parents, her husband Tassilo Festetics; her parents; a brother, Ved; and her stepdaughter.

These are supported by platform-level features including SamaAssure (quality guarantee up to 99.5%), SamaHub (project management and reporting workspace), and SamaIQ (proprietary analytics and insights engine). Recent product additions include Sama Automate (AI+human-in-the-loop automation), Bulk Annotation (ML-powered batch classification), and Smart Review (selective quality review reducing review rates to 10%). Specialized offerings include ADAS & Autonomous Vehicles, Generative AI for BFSI, Consumer & Media, Agriculture & Food, and Robotics & Manufacturing industry solutions.

leadership_change.description: Meta officially terminated its partnership with Kenyan outsourcing firm Sama following controversy over privacy concerns tied to Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, resulting in 1,108 Sama employees in Nairobi losing their jobs within six days notice.
leadership_change.title: Meta Contract Termination

leadership_change.description: Sama shifted its business model away from content moderation toward AI data labeling services after years of legal battles since 2022, though it continues offering AI data labeling services to tech clients including Meta.

leadership_change.description: Sama announced plans to lay off more than 1,000 workers in Kenya after Meta ended its contract, with the decision effective April 16, 2026, following unsuccessful discussions with the client to safeguard jobs.
leadership_change.title: Nairobi Mass Layoffs After Meta Contract End

expansion_highlight.description: Sama Automate (April 2025), Smart Review (October 2025), and Bulk Annotation (November 2025) collectively shift Sama from pure human annotation services toward an AI-automation-plus-human-validation platform, opening a lower-cost product tier and broader addressable market.

Sama Automate is explicitly targeted at retail, automotive, and finance organizations, indicating a deliberate move down-market from Fortune 500 enterprise-only to mid-market and smaller organizations that previously could not afford human-led annotation services.

Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) is positioned as a primary segment with dedicated generative AI and LLM solutions for conversational AI, document summarization, RAG evaluation, and compliance use cases, expanding beyond historical computer vision dominance.

Montr\u00e9al R&D expansion funded by CDPQ's $70M Series B with a stated $100M three-year investment and a target of 54+ local employees by end of 2023 indicates a commitment to building North American technical capacity adjacent to the Mila AI research ecosystem.

Pursuit of ISO 42001 (AI management system) and AICPA SOC-2 certifications, both listed as in progress in 2024, signals regulatory positioning to serve highly regulated buyers and prepare for emerging AI governance regimes in EU and North America.

Strategic partnership with Mila (Montr\u00e9al Institute for Learning Algorithms) and the Sama-Coco pre-annotated dataset product indicate an effort to build a research and dataset ecosystem around the core annotation service.

company_assessment.market_position: Sama, founded in 2008 and headquartered in San Francisco with delivery operations in Kenya, Uganda, and a Montréal R&D hub, is a leading enterprise-focused AI training data and annotation services provider. The company serves Fortune 500 and high-growth AI customers across ADAS and autonomous vehicles, generative AI, BFSI, retail and e-commerce, robotics, and agriculture, with named customers including Google, Microsoft, Walmart, Continental, SWIFT, and Getty Images. Differentiated by a 4,000+ full-time in-house workforce (not crowdsourced), B Corp certification, and ISO/GDPR/TISAX-aligned security posture.

strengths.details: Sama's explicit generative AI/RLHF capabilities (instruction following, preference ranking, RAG evaluation, model evaluation) are positioned at the highest-growth segment of AI services spend. As foundation model labs continue scaling post-training workflows, Sama's existing Microsoft, Google, and Meta-adjacent relationships position it to capture disproportionate share of this expanding wallet.
strengths.headline: Generative AI and RLHF demand supercharges Sama's GenAI book

strengths.details: Sama Automate's goal of 10x annotation time reduction, combined with Bulk Annotation and Smart Review, materially compresses cost-to-serve. This enables Sama to move down-market from Fortune 500 enterprise into retail, automotive, and finance mid-market customers previously priced out, expanding TAM and revenue diversification away from concentrated large accounts.
strengths.headline: Sama Automate unlocks SMB and mid-market expansion

strengths.details: EU AI Act, ISO 42001 (in progress at Sama), TISAX, and GDPR requirements are pushing regulated buyers toward certified data partners with documented quality systems. Sama's first-mover certifications and B Corp status create a defensible positioning as 'responsible by design' against less-certified competitors.
strengths.headline: Regulatory tailwinds favor certified, ethical data providers

strengths.details: Sama's vertical-segmented teams across ADAS/autonomous vehicles, BFSI, retail/e-commerce, and healthcare produce industry-specific workflows that compound customer switching costs. With 8-year average customer tenure and dedicated team matching, Sama is well-positioned to expand wallet share within existing accounts as their AI initiatives scale.
strengths.headline: Vertical specialization deepens enterprise lock-in

weakness.details: Foundation model improvements in self-supervised and AI-assisted annotation are reducing the marginal value of human labeling for many computer vision and NLP tasks. Sama's revenue model depends on volume-based managed services pricing; if auto-labeling quality catches up, per-unit pricing and margins could compress materially over a 2-3 year horizon.
weakness.headline: Auto-labeling advances threaten managed services economics

weakness.details: The Meta contract termination eliminated a major engagement and 1,108-person delivery team. If remaining large customers (Microsoft, Google, Walmart) similarly consolidate vendors or bring annotation in-house as AI tooling matures, Sama's revenue base could contract further without offsetting customer wins.
weakness.headline: Customer concentration risk after Meta loss

weakness.details: With no disclosed funding since the 2021 Series B and a major customer loss, Sama may need additional capital at unfavorable terms. Given current AI valuation compression and competitive pressure from well-funded Scale AI and Surge AI, the next round could come at a flat or down valuation, weakening founder and employee equity outcomes.
weakness.headline: Capital scarcity may force dilutive or distressed funding

weakness.details: Following the 1,108-person Nairobi layoff, Sama must rebuild or backfill specialized annotation capacity in Uganda and Montréal. Until scaled, customers may experience throughput constraints or quality variability, risking SLA breaches and account churn at exactly the moment when competitive alternatives are most aggressive.
weakness.headline: Delivery capacity gap after Nairobi layoffs

competitive_moat.details: Sama employs a full-time in-house workforce of 4,000+ data experts, never crowdsourced, with average tenure of 2+ years and vertically segmented teams trained on specific industry workflows. Enterprise customers integrate through API/CLI, SSO, and customized quality calibration processes that require iterative setup and dedicated team matching. Average customer tenure of 8 years and NPS of 64 indicate high stickiness once integrated.

Sama processes 10 billion annotation points per month across 300 million frames and 850 million shapes while maintaining a 99% first-batch client acceptance rate. This scale-throughput-quality combination is operationally difficult to replicate and supports multi-year enterprise contracts.

First AI company to achieve B Corp certification (recertified 2024), 15+ years operating history, and ISO 9001/27001/TISAX/GDPR certifications form a credibility stack that is difficult for newer entrants to match, particularly for regulated enterprise buyers.

Proprietary Sama-Coco Dataset and cross-industry exposure across automotive, retail, BFSI, and agriculture produce accumulated edge-case knowledge. Sama IQ analytics engine proactively identifies edge cases and data distribution issues across this installed base.

Established enterprise sales motion with dedicated account teams, expert-consultation entry points, and Fortune 500 references (Microsoft, Google, Walmart, Continental, Siemens). Average 8-year customer tenure indicates high renewal economics once landed.

key_risks.details: Meta terminated its partnership with Sama in April 2026 following privacy controversy around Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses footage review. Sama issued redundancy notices to 1,108 Nairobi employees within six days, representing its largest single workforce disruption and a meaningful revenue concentration shock.

key_risks.details: Sama's last disclosed capital raise was the $70M Series B in November 2021 led by CDPQ. Absence of subsequent rounds despite layoffs and a major customer loss raises questions about runway, growth trajectory, and investor appetite at current operating performance.
key_risks.headline: No new funding round since 2021 Series B

key_risks.details: Sama operates in a market with heavily funded direct competitors (Scale AI, Surge AI, Labelbox, Appen, CloudFactory). Many competitors have raised significantly more recent capital and may outcompete on price, automation depth, or technical capabilities, especially as model-assisted labeling commoditizes.
