company_assessment.market_position: Fresha is a London-headquartered marketplace platform founded in 2015 that connects consumers with over 140,000 beauty and wellness businesses across 120+ countries. The company processes more than $15 billion in annual GMV and reports a $140 million+ annualized revenue run-rate with 60%+ annual growth, operating profitably. Fresha achieved unicorn status in May 2026 following an $80 million Series C led by KKR, bringing total funding to $285.8 million. The company is the only beauty and wellness booking platform named to the VivaTech Top 100 Rising European Startups and is consistently ranked among the top 10 lifestyle apps globally by monthly downloads.

strengths.details: With 35M+ monthly appointments and 823,000+ professional profiles, Fresha possesses a uniquely rich vertical data asset that powers AI Agent Nova, Dynamic Reassignment (recovering 11% of lost demand), and AI Concierge. As competitors attempt to replicate features, Fresha's data advantage widens, creating a defensible AI-native moat that compounds with every booking.
strengths.headline: AI moat compounds as platform data scales

strengths.details: Multi-location brand revenue is growing 67% YoY, indicating successful upmarket motion. As chains consolidate fragmented software onto Fresha, average revenue per business rises materially, and the company captures share of the $15B+ GMV pool at a higher effective take rate through enterprise contracts.
strengths.headline: Enterprise expansion unlocks higher-ACV SaaS revenue

strengths.details: Fresha Capital has already disbursed $5.5M+ in loans with an 80% repeat borrowing rate and zero credit risk exposure (Adyen-assumed). With 140,000+ businesses needing working capital, the lending product has multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue potential as it scales, capital-free to Fresha.
strengths.headline: Embedded finance scales into a high-margin adjacency

strengths.details: Operating in 120+ countries but with meaningful density only in NA, UK, EU, and ANZ. Emerging markets in LatAm, MENA, and APAC represent underpenetrated beauty/wellness economies where Fresha's free-for-business, transaction-fee model can rapidly capture share. Recent GM expansion in Mexico and Japan signals continued geographic buildout.
strengths.headline: Global penetration runway remains substantial

strengths.details: Top 10 lifestyle app status with 1M+ monthly downloads (up 300% since 2024) and 3M+ new client connections in 2025 reflect strong organic consumer pull. As the marketplace deepens, both consumer search and business acquisition costs decrease, allowing Fresha to sustain 60%+ growth without linear marketing spend.
strengths.headline: Network effects drive organic, capital-efficient growth

weakness.details: Approximately 25% of bookings (1.2M+ monthly) flow through Google Gemini and AI-driven referrals. Google's ongoing search evolution and AI agent strategies could shift economics, de-prioritize third-party booking referrals, or terminate partnership terms. A 50% reduction in Google-sourced bookings would remove 12-15% of platform GMV overnight.
weakness.headline: Google AI integration could be repriced or removed

weakness.details: Square Appointments, Mindbody, and other payment-platform competitors can subsidize booking software with payment processing economics. As payment processors vertically integrate, Fresha's pure-play take-rate model may face pricing pressure, and the company lacks a payment processing moat to defend its economics.
weakness.headline: Take-rate compression from well-funded payment competitors

weakness.details: AI Concierge, Dynamic Reassignment, and AI Agent Nova are all replicable in concept by competitors with similar data scale. As foundation model costs decline and AI agent builders proliferate, Fresha's current AI differentiation could narrow rapidly, especially against Square/Mindbody which can bundle AI features into broader commerce stacks.
weakness.headline: AI features could be commoditized by horizontal platforms

weakness.details: 100% of Fresha's revenue is exposed to discretionary consumer spending on beauty and wellness services. In a recession or sustained inflation scenario, consumer visits to salons and spas historically decline 10-20%, which would flow directly through to Fresha's GMV and transaction fee revenue with no offsetting segment to buffer.
weakness.headline: Beauty/wellness spending contraction in macro downturn

weakness.details: As multi-location brands grow (the 67% YoY growth segment), they may elect to build proprietary booking systems, white-label Fresha, or migrate to enterprise SaaS that gives them direct client ownership. Loss of marquee enterprise customers would both remove a high-growth segment and reduce marketplace liquidity for consumers.
weakness.headline: Multi-location chains may bypass platform at scale

competitive_moat.details: Fresha operates a two-sided marketplace with over 140,000 beauty and wellness businesses, 450,000+ professionals, and 35 million monthly appointments across 120+ countries. This scale creates strong flywheel dynamics: more businesses attract more consumers via SEO and app discovery, which in turn attracts more businesses seeking customer flow.

Deep integration with Google Gemini and other AI agents now drives approximately one in four bookings on the platform, with over 1.2 million appointments per month originating from Google alone. This positions Fresha as the de facto plumbing layer for AI-mediated beauty and wellness discovery, a distribution moat that is difficult for late entrants to replicate.

The platform supports over 823,000 professional profiles and processes $15 billion+ in annual GMV across 120+ countries, accumulating a proprietary dataset on beauty demand patterns, professional performance, and consumer behavior that feeds AI features such as Dynamic Reassignment and recommendation.

An 83% client retention rate after the third appointment indicates strong consumer-side lock-in built through appointment history, stored payment methods, and reviews. For businesses, accumulated client history, integrated payments, and operational data raise the cost of migration.

Fresha has developed proprietary AI capabilities including AI Agent Nova (resolving 80%+ of support tickets at 4.6/5 satisfaction), AI Concierge for front-desk automation, and AI Security Agents stopping 99% of fraud attempts. These are differentiated, vertically-tuned AI assets rather than generic LLM wrappers.

key_risks.details: Approximately 25% of platform bookings (1.2M+ monthly) flow through Google Gemini and AI integrations. Any change to Google's AI search algorithms, partnership terms, or ranking logic could materially disrupt a quarter of the company's booking volume, creating a single-point-of-failure risk.
key_risks.headline: Heavy dependency on Google for AI-driven booking referrals

key_risks.details: With ~$15B GMV and $140M revenue, the implied take rate is under 1%, but any successful business has a continuous incentive to migrate repeat clients to direct booking. As merchants scale on the platform, defection risk increases and the take-rate ceiling is capped without adding differentiated value.
key_risks.headline: Transaction-fee model structurally incentivizes businesses to bypass the platform

key_risks.details: 100% of GMV flows through beauty, wellness, and self-care verticals which are highly discretionary and historically contract sharply in economic downturns. The business has no countercyclical exposure to offset demand softness in SMB customer base.
key_risks.headline: Concentrated exposure to discretionary beauty/wellness spending cycles

key_risks.details: Customer base skews toward independent salons, barbers, and wellness studios, which face higher closure rates and churn risk than enterprise SaaS. Fresha Capital's embedded lending ($5.5M+ to date) creates indirect exposure to SMB financial health despite Adyen's risk assumption.
key_risks.headline: SMB-heavy customer base with elevated churn and credit risk exposure

key_risks.details: Competitors include Square Appointments (Block), Mindbody, Vagaro, Booksy, Treatwell, Phorest, GlossGenius, and Boulevard. Several competitors are owned by or backed by larger payment/processor companies with potentially deeper enterprise distribution and capital reserves.
key_risks.headline: Competitive threat from well-capitalized incumbents and vertical SaaS players

key_risks.details: Core platform depends on Adyen (payments/embedded finance), Twilio/Google (RCS messaging), and Google (AI-driven bookings). Concentration of critical infrastructure with three providers creates operational, pricing, and partnership risk if any relationship deteriorates.
key_risks.headline: Reliance on third-party infrastructure providers (Adyen, Twilio, Google)

key_highlights.details: KKR led an $80M Series C primary growth investment valuing the company at over $1 billion, with disclosed post-money of $1.175B. Total funding reached $285.8M across rounds from KKR, General Atlantic, Partech, J.P. Morgan, and others.
key_highlights.headline: Achieved unicorn status in May 2026 with $1.175B post-money valuation

key_highlights.details: Company is already profitable while maintaining 60%+ annual growth rate. The $140M revenue run-rate on $15B+ annual GMV implies a take rate of ~0.93% with significant operating leverage potential as scale increases.
key_highlights.headline: Profitable with $140M+ revenue run-rate and 60%+ annual growth

key_highlights.details: Platform serves 140,000+ beauty and wellness businesses across 120+ countries, with 450,000+ professionals and 35 million+ appointments facilitated per month. Annual GMV exceeds $15 billion, representing a deep liquidity pool on both sides of the marketplace.
key_highlights.headline: Massive marketplace scale with 140,000+ businesses and 35M+ monthly appointments

key_highlights.details: Google Gemini and AI agents drive over 1.2 million monthly appointments (25% of platform bookings). Proprietary AI Agent Nova autonomously resolves 80%+ of global support tickets with 4.6/5 satisfaction. AI Security Agents stop 99% of fraud attempts.
key_highlights.headline: Deep AI integration drives 1 in 4 bookings and 99% fraud detection

key_highlights.details: Marketplace flywheel with 130,000+ businesses and 450,000+ professionals generated over 3 million new client connections in 2025. 83% client retention rate after third appointment and 9x median ROI for partners signal strong two-sided engagement.
key_highlights.headline: Strong network effects with 3M+ new client connections in 2025

key_highlights.details: Platform revenue from large multi-location business segments increased 67% year-on-year with 23.4% bookings growth for these operators. Enterprise sales motion complementing the SMB-led product-led growth model enables expansion upmarket.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise segment growing 67% YoY with multi-location chain adoption

key_highlights.details: Embedded lending product in partnership with Adyen has distributed $5.5M+ in working capital loans across 7 markets, with 80% repeat borrowing rate and Adyen assuming all credit risk. Creates high-margin, capital-light revenue stream adjacent to the core marketplace.
key_highlights.headline: Embedded finance (Fresha Capital) achieved 80% repeat borrowing rate

launches.full_text:
Boulevard Expands Clinical Capabilities for Medspas with Launch of ePrescribe

Share

New integration with ScriptSure enables seamless e-prescribing directly from patient profiles

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Boulevard (www.joinblvd.com), provider of the business management platform trusted by the fastest-growing salons, spas, and medspas, today announced the launch of ePrescribe, a new feature that brings secure electronic prescribing directly into patient profiles. ePrescribe enables medspas and other clinical wellness practices to manage prescriptions alongside scheduling, charting, payments, and the broader patient experience within the Boulevard platform, eliminating system switching, reducing duplicate data entry, and minimizing risk of error. “Medspas shouldn’t have to stitch together separate systems just to deliver great care,” said Matt Danna, co-founder and CEO of Boulevard. Share Powered through a partnership with D.A.W. Systems (dawsystems.com) and its ScriptSure e-prescribing solution, Boulevard ePrescribe is designed to support protocol-driven care, repeat visits, and collaborative wellness teams that require both speed and precision. “Medspas shouldn’t have to stitch together separate systems just to deliver great care,” said Matt Danna, co-founder and CEO of Boulevard. “We built Boulevard to create a seamless experience for patients and providers alike, but prescribing has been one of the last workflows pushing teams outside that system. With ePrescribe, it finally lives in the same place, giving care teams a connected workflow inside the patient record and a better experience from consult to follow-up.” Integration with ScriptSure means Boulevard’s customers gain direct access to the industry’s leading e-prescribing solution, one used by more than 30,000 licensed prescribers nationwide. By partnering with ScriptSure, Boulevard enables clinicians and practitioners to initiate prescriptions, select medications and directions, review automated safety alerts, and send prescriptions to the pharmacy, all from the same patient profile they already use to manage clinical charting, photo markups, treatment documentation, and purchase history. “D.A.W. Systems is proud to partner with Boulevard, the industry’s leading medspa software platform,” said John Ketcham, CRO, D.A.W. Systems. “This integration brings together the two tools that top-performing medspas already rely on, giving providers a fully unified workflow from booking to prescribing and setting a new standard for what great medspa technology looks like.” Designed for Modern Medspas Most establishments in the fast-growing medspa industry provide medical-grade treatments—from IV therapy and hormone optimization to GLP-1s and other prescription-based services—but have historically needed separate EMRs or standalone e-prescribing systems to manage medications. This forced teams to manually re-enter patient information across platforms, creating operational inefficiencies and compliance risk. Now, with Boulevard ePrescribe, prescriptions, purchases, and paperwork live together in one place. Boulevard ePrescribe supports controlled, non-controlled, and compounded medications. Built to the highest EPCS and HIPAA compliance standards, Boulevard supports identity verification and multi-factor authentication. Other key capabilities include: Built-in safety checks with allergy and drug interaction alerts

Real-time prescription benefit checks

Refill management, allowing providers to approve, deny, or re-prescribe based on prescription history

Automatic documentation, ensuring every prescription is recorded in the patient record

Team-based workflows, enabling support staff to assist while providers maintain clinical control and compliance Boulevard ePrescribe is available now. To learn more, visit www.joinblvd.com/features/prescriptions. About Boulevard Boulevard offers the business management platform trusted by the fastest-growing salons, spas, and medspas. Boulevard empowers business owners and professionals alike to deliver personable, enjoyable experiences to their clients through online appointment scheduling, messaging, marketing, and payments that are simple, elegant, and reliable. Founded in 2016, Boulevard has earned the trust of thousands of businesses across the nation by delivering the world-class technology and genuine service they deserve. To learn more, visit joinblvd.com.

We cover the main users, features, and key integrations you need for your hotel spa software needs. Then, we review the top off-the-shelf tools and compare them to a fully custom roadmap (with some insider tips). ‍ What is spa management software? Spa management software is a purpose-built digital platform that handles the operational and business side of running a spa. It covers everything from booking appointments and tracking client histories to processing payments, managing staff schedules, and reporting revenue. Overall, it’s the nervous system of a spa business. Without it, everything runs on clipboards, spreadsheets, and memory, while with it, the whole operation connects. According to Samkange and his team, operations management in a spa context means transforming inputs such as staff, proprietary treatments, and physical facilities into measurable guest experiences. Spa management software is the tool that makes this transformation trackable, repeatable, and profitable. Market overview The global spa industry hit $18.1 billion in revenue in 2021, a 49% jump from the year before, with 173 million visits recorded in the U.S. alone. Globally, the market is on track to exceed $185 billion by 2030. The hotel spa software segment sits at the center of this growth. A 2025 CBRE Hotels analysis of 297 U.S. hotel spas found that spa revenue averaged $6,061 per available room, contributing 3.4% of total hotel revenue. At luxury properties, the share jumps to 4.2%. So if you’re still treating your spa returns as a side business, it’s time to rethink. Spa is a revenue line that hotel operators now manage as seriously as rooms or food and beverage. The spa business software market reflects that pressure. It’s projected to reach $2.92 billion by 2035, growing at a compound annual rate of 19.6%. However, challenges are still evident. For instance, 42% of small spa operators say upfront software costs are a genuine barrier, and 54% of SMEs using cloud-based systems report gaps in data compliance. There’s a massive demand, but the friction is big, as well. Core purpose The main purpose is clear: spa software exists to turn a complex, people-heavy operation into something one person can actually manage. Every hotel spa runs on a web of separate processes, services, and people. Therapists, rooms, products, bookings, guests, hotel systems, payroll. Hotel spa management software pulls all of that into a single place so nothing falls through the cracks and every decision is backed by real numbers. That one statement breaks down into four specific jobs the software does. FAQ Ready to join Boulevard? Get a Demo Feb.13.2026 UPDATED . Jun.25.2026 BY Skya Jones Modern salons need point-of-sale (POS) systems that handle it all. The right system can seriously up your game by improving client interactions and boosting revenue . The best salon POS system does more than process payments. Modern salon POS software helps businesses manage appointments, client profiles, inventory, reporting, and retail sales from one platform When it’s easy to buy the products as they check out and book appointments from home, clients are more likely to rebook again and again. In this guide, we’ll give you the inside scoop on POS software, like what it can actually do for your salon and which are the best POS systems for salons in 2026. What Is a Salon POS System? Salon POS systems are central hubs for the front desk. These software-forward systems support the client experience as much as the salon’s checkout process. They combine software with hardware like iPads and card readers so your clients can easily pay for their visit (and any retail products they’re picking up). A salon POS system is purpose-built for beauty businesses and helps manage payments, appointments, inventory, and client relationships from a single platform. A POS system handles most of your salon’s financial tasks in one place, processing payments, calculating tips and loyalty discounts, and managing retail and reporting programs. Some even make it easy to integrate with other software that tracks staff hours and performance, leading to less manual work on your end. Features To Look for in a Salon POS System Shopping for salon POS software gets a lot easier when you know what to look for. Every self-care business is unique, but here are a few features that most teams need. When comparing salon POS software, prioritize tools that improve both client experiences and day-to-day operations. Fast and flexible checkout: POS software should make paying fast and convenient for everyone, offering things like mobile payment options and easy-to-follow on-screen prompts.

Integrated payments and tipping: Your POS system should support multiple payment options, like mobile wallets and cards on file, so no one has to dig through their wallet for the one method you accept. Look for software that automatically calculates tips at set percentages (like 15%, 20%, and 25%) and applies loyalty rewards and discount codes, too.

Reporting and sales insights: Good salon POS software doesn’t stop working for you once the client has paid. It’ll also include high-level details like retail trends and retention data . These insights can help you adjust your strategies (such as scheduling a full-team workshop to perfect the latest TikTok hairstyle trend) and stay on top of your revenue flow before rent’s due.

Client profiles and purchase history: Choose tools that let you personalize the salon experience. Client profiles store information like their birthdays for special discounts and notes from their past sessions to help your stylists provide better service from moment one.

Retail and inventory management: Keep track of backbar inventory and retail products directly in your POS system. Your software should send an alert when you’re running low and automate order purchasing so you never have to run out of a dye color mid-service. How To Choose the Best Salon POS System Before you start researching and selecting a POS system , you need a game plan. There are lots of software solutions for spas out there, so knowing what you need ahead of time can side-step information overload. These tips will help you stay organized and focus on your salon’s long-term goals. The right POS system for a beauty salon should support your current workflows while giving you room to grow. Define Your Salon’s POS Needs Choosing software starts with taking stock of your needs, so assess your current POS processes. What does the checkout process look like? Where does it slow down? Are there features that overlap with your other software solutions or things you’d like to collapse into one program? Make a list of your wants and needs, then reference it during your search to narrow down your options. Evaluate Ease of Use for Your Staff Your chosen POS software should make your employees’ lives easier. Ideally, they’ll be able to pick it up in their first few days without tons of hands-on training. Part of this onboarding process includes the software company’s customer service, too. A program with a strong team behind it will help you set everything up and get questions answered along the way. Check How the POS Connects To Booking and Scheduling The best POS tools integrate with scheduling systems you already use. Appointment reminders, automated calendar syncing, and easy rebooking options can reduce no-shows and double-booking. This way, your front desk team can schedule clients for a touch-up or a fresh cut in six weeks while they’re still standing at the counter, so they’re more likely to keep coming back . Compare Pricing and Total Cost Price is always important to consider, especially if you're just getting established or planning your next location. But comparing upfront costs is only the first step. You also need to compare how different software options impact your long-term overhead. Some systems may seem affordable at first, but consider how they’ll impact your overhead over time. Study the fine print: Are there high processing fees? Are their long-term contracts undercut by unreasonable cancellation penalties? POS systems that don’t integrate well with other software means paying for more subscriptions every month, too. Plan for Growth and Scalability You shouldn't have to adjust your business goals around your software or do a massive overhaul every time you outgrow your current system, no matter how big your salon gets. So make sure your beauty salon’s POS has the flexibility to scale with your growing salon. It should be able to manage more locations and team members without glitching, process more complex loyalty and membership programs, and have the wiggle room to add new workflows as tech evolves. 5 Best Salon POS Systems Every POS system has its strengths, but not all of them are going to be the right fit for your needs. The best salon POS systems vary based on your budget, team size, and operational needs. We’ve gathered details on five of the best POS systems for salons so you can cut the noise and find software that works for you. 1. It is one of the best salon POS software solutions for growing salons that want scheduling, payments, reporting, and client management in one place. Adding appointment booking and calendars to your POS system can boost your client retention because it’s easier for front desk staff to book a client’s next appointment in the moment. It can also track commissions for a more accurate picture of your finances. When should a salon consider upgrading its POS system? It might be time to upgrade if there are lines forming at your front desk due to error messages and lag, or if it isn’t compatible with the latest hardware and payment methods. Feeling like it’s time to update your other hardware and software systems is also an indicator that it’s time to look into a new POS system—or an all-in-one choice like Boulevard . Boulevard Raises $80 Million in Series D Funding to Transform the Client Experience for Self-Care Businesses Share This Article Funding round led by JMI Equity enables Boulevard to accelerate delivery of enterprise capabilities and boost investment in AI research and development to help businesses create more personalized client experiences LOS ANGELES, July 17, 2025-- Boulevard (www.joinblvd.com), provider of the client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses, today announced that it has raised $80 million in Series D funding led by JMI Equity, a growth equity firm focused on investments in leading software companies, with continued participation from Index Ventures and VMG Partners. The funding enables Boulevard to accelerate the delivery of enterprise capabilities across multiple self-care verticals while fueling increased investment in AI research and development to help customers continue transforming the client experience through smart technology.



“We’re ecstatic about the opportunity to collaborate with the team at JMI Equity and benefit from their extensive experience helping vertical SaaS companies like Boulevard grow and create generational brands,” said Matt Danna, co-founder and CEO, Boulevard. “In addition to accelerating delivery of the enterprise capabilities customers want today, this new round of funding allows us to pour more resources into discovering and developing the most compelling AI features and building the smartest operational systems possible for these experience-centric businesses. We’re excited to take the self-care industry more fully into the era of AI-powered business growth.”



Boulevard’s boundary-pushing innovations, such as Precision Scheduling™, have already reshaped technology's role in helping self-care businesses deliver seamless client experiences. The game-changing feature on which Boulevard was founded, Precision Scheduling leverages artificial intelligence to analyze booking patterns, appointment durations, and provider availability to suggest the most efficient appointment times. With Precision Scheduling, Boulevard has transformed booking from an arduous, manual, and mostly offline process into a seamless online experience that enables self-care businesses to maximize revenue and exceed the highest of client expectations.



With this new round of funding, the company is positioned to more deeply explore the next generation of intelligence-based technologies for the self-care industry. From using AI to deliver smarter, more customized recommendations for clients, to helping them fine-tune their menu of services and optimize marketing and communications, to developing the most effective packages, promotions, and membership programs possible, Boulevard is poised to help self-care businesses drive greater revenue growth, deliver deeper personalization, and achieve operational excellence.



As part of the Series D investment, Matt Emery, Partner at JMI Equity, has joined Boulevard’s Board of Directors.



“Boulevard is already a clear leader in this fast-growing market, and they’re just getting started,” said Emery. “We’re thrilled to join them on this exciting journey as they continue to transform the client experience in this new era of intelligence-driven technology.”



Fueling growth through innovation



Since its last round of funding in 2022, Boulevard’s revenue has increased by more than 500% as it continues to redefine what’s possible for self-care businesses. Recent enhancements to Boulevard’s platform help customers more seamlessly embed payments into their checkout flow, expand the reach of their commerce and membership programs, and modernize how they market to and communicate with clients.



In addition, as part of its rapid expansion into the fast-growing medspa vertical, Boulevard also launched advanced charting for a more efficient treatment, documentation, and review process, plus technical capabilities, hands-on training, and additional support to help with HIPAA compliance. Less than three years after making its initial foray into the space, Boulevard now powers 15% of the burgeoning U.S. medspa market.



A trusted brand in self-care



Boulevard is now trusted by over 40,000 professionals in more than 5,000 self-care businesses to book more than 2 million monthly appointments and process nearly $5 billion in payments annually. These hair salons, nail salons, medspas, day spas, and barbershops across the U.S. rely on Boulevard for everything from online booking and payment processing to marketing and client communication.



About Boulevard



Boulevard offers the first and only client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses. Boulevard empowers business owners and professionals alike to deliver personable, enjoyable experiences to their clients through online appointment scheduling, messaging, marketing, and payments that are simple, elegant, and reliable. Founded in 2016, Boulevard has earned the trust of thousands of salons, spas, medspas, and barbershops across the nation by delivering the world-class technology and genuine, human, personable service they deserve. To learn more, visit joinblvd.com.

launches.title: 5 Questions With: Matt Danna, Co-Founder & CEO of Boulevard
launches.ai_summary: Boulevard, a Los Angeles-based AI-driven SaaS platform for salons and spas, secured an $80 million Series D round in July led by JMI Equity, valuing the company at approximately $800 million, bringing its total funding to roughly $188 million. In an interview with American Salon, co-founder and CEO Matt Danna outlined how the funding will support enterprise-grade features and AI tools designed to advance personalization and operational efficiency for appointment-based beauty businesses. The discussion highlighted broader industry trends, including the growing importance of anticipatory service, Gen Z's influence on beauty tech discovery, and the shift toward client-driven engagement models.
launches.author: American Salon Staff
launches.full_text:
Los Angeles-based Boulevard launched in 2016 as an online booking platform for salons and spas. Since then, it’s grown into an AI-driven SaaS platform designed to help appointment-based beauty and grooming businesses manage everything from scheduling and client communications to payments and marketing. That evolution reflects part of a broader shift across the beauty and wellness sector, where data, automation, and personalization are reshaping how professionals run their businesses — and how consumers experience self-care. To date, Boulevard has raised roughly $188 million in funding, including an $80 million Series D round in July led by JMI Equity, valuing the company at about $800 million. Co-founder and CEO Matt Danna said at the time the funding would help expand “the enterprise-grade features our customers are asking for” while advancing the AI tools “that will define the future of self-care.” Danna recently gave American Salon some insights on how technology is reshaping the beauty consumer experience (and vice versa) and what’s steering Boulevard’s latest investment. View this post on Instagram

AS: How do you see technology reshaping the beauty service consumer experience over the next 5 years? MD: I can’t possibly overstate how important personalization is and will continue to be. We already see this today. Something as simple as personalizing a text leads to 22% more revenue per appointment, 28% higher completion rates, and 16% higher client retention. Now think about how much more powerful personalization can become as software continues to get even more predictive. We’re not far from an era of what I call anticipatory service, where systems account for and act on a client’s history and preferences to proactively suggest services and treatments that are highly customized and strategically tailored to the individual. Already today, 66% of clients say that being remembered by their service provider drives long-term loyalty. That number is going nowhere but up. The question you should be asking yourself is: Is my platform making the client experience better? Your software has to make every single client interaction feel effortless. Otherwise, you’re detracting from the client experience, and that’s an opportunity tax you do not want to pay. AS: How is Gen Z (and soon Gen Alpha) influencing the direction of beauty tech? MD: They’re influencing it in more ways than I think even most salon owners realize. Young generations are discovering salons and stylists in entirely new ways, on their own terms. Fifty-five percent of Gen Z and 47% of Millennials say that your Instagram or TikTok activity is “very” or “extremely” important in deciding whether to book at your salon. Social networks, online communities, virtual marketplaces — these are the customer acquisition and referral channels of the present and future. It goes beyond discovery, though. Younger generations want every interaction to feel like it was designed just for them. They want every aspect of the experience to feel curated around their preferences. They expect you to offer what they want without them ever having to ask for it. In fact, 55% of clients today say they expect to be proactively offered add-ons, memberships, or retail options as part of their experience. All of this is pushing the boundaries of what we mean when we refer to the client experience, and technology has a huge role to play — not just in terms of automating tasks and personalizing experiences, but in ensuring your brand shows up with style at every single touchpoint. AS: Salon and barbershop owners generally want their software to help them save time and make money. What is the one platform feature every business should be using to accomplish those goals? MD: This one is simple for me: intelligent scheduling, which we at Boulevard call Precision Scheduling. Every salon and barbershop owner should be treating their calendar as if it’s their Profit and Loss statement, because it is. Every time you book an appointment, you are in effect managing your revenue. How intelligent your system is and how well it optimizes your daily calendar is what determines if you’re booking a profit or booking a loss. Your system should be able to learn from data such as historical booking patterns and appointment durations so that it can book appointments in a way that drives the most dollars per hour. And it has to be able to do this in a matter of seconds, because that’s often all you have. Clients aren’t interested in waiting around for you to figure out the best time. Your system has to be able to move at their speed. View this post on Instagram AS: Can you think of any digital platform capabilities that are widely used and appreciated by beauty businesses today, but were nonexistent just a few years ago? It’s wild how far the industry’s come in just a few years. Things that were once considered cutting edge, like online booking, client profiles, integrated payments, and text marketing, are now table stakes. I remember a time when proactive texting was considered pushy and intrusive. Now it’s not just OK; it’s expected, and expected to happen immediately: 41% of clients expect a same-day follow-up after their appointment, and 44% say they want those to come via text. We at Boulevard have been obsessed with creating the absolute best online booking experience in the industry, because it’s the digital equivalent of the exterior facade of your storefront. Online booking is such an important factor for prospective clients who are browsing and doing research for deciding to book. Two-thirds of prospective clients are lost if your booking experience isn’t what it needs to be. AS: On the flip side, what do you think will be the next must-have digital tool for beauty businesses that’s just now emerging or currently under development? MD: That’s thinking too small. The future of self-care tech isn’t about any single tool; it’s about evolving technology to match the shifting nature of the salon-client relationship. For the longest time, salons dictated the terms of engagement — how to interact with the business, when and how to book, what to buy, and the vehicles through which to do it all. But today, that dynamic has flipped. Clients are in the driver’s seat, which means the next generation of self-care technology has to be about allowing salons to meet clients where they are. It has to be about adapting in real time to their preferences, behaviors, and communication styles. View this post on Instagram AS: Boulevard recently secured an $80 million Series D investment. Can we get a sneak peek at what new and/or improved features the company is focusing on bringing to its platform? MD: Two big priorities, both of which were priorities even before we raised our Series D. The first is all about what we call enterprise without compromise. It’s ridiculous to me that franchises and multi-location brands have to trade elegance, usability, and platform stability for enterprise-grade capabilities. That should never happen. There’s no reason scale and design can’t co-exist, so we’re doubling down on ensuring that these larger enterprises can get the capabilities they need, along with the design and usability Boulevard is known for. The other area of focus is on high-quality AI. Our approach to AI is very simple: outcomes and impact are what matter. It has to be about doing something meaningful that delivers value beyond what humans can do on their own. Many of our team members come straight from salons and spas. They’ve been stylists, educators, front desk staff, coaches, and managers. They understand the challenges firsthand. AI is an incredibly valuable tool, but it’s not the goal. The goal is and always will be to help our customers deliver flawless, deeply personalized experiences that keep clients coming back.

funding_news.full_text:
Boulevard Raises $80 Million in Series D Funding to Transform the Client Experience for Self-Care Businesses Share This Article Funding round led by JMI Equity enables Boulevard to accelerate delivery of enterprise capabilities and boost investment in AI research and development to help businesses create more personalized client experiences LOS ANGELES, July 17, 2025-- Boulevard (www.joinblvd.com), provider of the client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses, today announced that it has raised $80 million in Series D funding led by JMI Equity, a growth equity firm focused on investments in leading software companies, with continued participation from Index Ventures and VMG Partners. The funding enables Boulevard to accelerate the delivery of enterprise capabilities across multiple self-care verticals while fueling increased investment in AI research and development to help customers continue transforming the client experience through smart technology.



“We’re ecstatic about the opportunity to collaborate with the team at JMI Equity and benefit from their extensive experience helping vertical SaaS companies like Boulevard grow and create generational brands,” said Matt Danna, co-founder and CEO, Boulevard. “In addition to accelerating delivery of the enterprise capabilities customers want today, this new round of funding allows us to pour more resources into discovering and developing the most compelling AI features and building the smartest operational systems possible for these experience-centric businesses. We’re excited to take the self-care industry more fully into the era of AI-powered business growth.”



Boulevard’s boundary-pushing innovations, such as Precision Scheduling™, have already reshaped technology's role in helping self-care businesses deliver seamless client experiences. The game-changing feature on which Boulevard was founded, Precision Scheduling leverages artificial intelligence to analyze booking patterns, appointment durations, and provider availability to suggest the most efficient appointment times. With Precision Scheduling, Boulevard has transformed booking from an arduous, manual, and mostly offline process into a seamless online experience that enables self-care businesses to maximize revenue and exceed the highest of client expectations.



With this new round of funding, the company is positioned to more deeply explore the next generation of intelligence-based technologies for the self-care industry. From using AI to deliver smarter, more customized recommendations for clients, to helping them fine-tune their menu of services and optimize marketing and communications, to developing the most effective packages, promotions, and membership programs possible, Boulevard is poised to help self-care businesses drive greater revenue growth, deliver deeper personalization, and achieve operational excellence.



As part of the Series D investment, Matt Emery, Partner at JMI Equity, has joined Boulevard’s Board of Directors.



“Boulevard is already a clear leader in this fast-growing market, and they’re just getting started,” said Emery. “We’re thrilled to join them on this exciting journey as they continue to transform the client experience in this new era of intelligence-driven technology.”



Fueling growth through innovation



Since its last round of funding in 2022, Boulevard’s revenue has increased by more than 500% as it continues to redefine what’s possible for self-care businesses. Recent enhancements to Boulevard’s platform help customers more seamlessly embed payments into their checkout flow, expand the reach of their commerce and membership programs, and modernize how they market to and communicate with clients.



In addition, as part of its rapid expansion into the fast-growing medspa vertical, Boulevard also launched advanced charting for a more efficient treatment, documentation, and review process, plus technical capabilities, hands-on training, and additional support to help with HIPAA compliance. Less than three years after making its initial foray into the space, Boulevard now powers 15% of the burgeoning U.S. medspa market.



A trusted brand in self-care



Boulevard is now trusted by over 40,000 professionals in more than 5,000 self-care businesses to book more than 2 million monthly appointments and process nearly $5 billion in payments annually. These hair salons, nail salons, medspas, day spas, and barbershops across the U.S. rely on Boulevard for everything from online booking and payment processing to marketing and client communication.



About Boulevard



Boulevard offers the first and only client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based, self-care businesses. Boulevard empowers business owners and professionals alike to deliver personable, enjoyable experiences to their clients through online appointment scheduling, messaging, marketing, and payments that are simple, elegant, and reliable. Founded in 2016, Boulevard has earned the trust of thousands of salons, spas, medspas, and barbershops across the nation by delivering the world-class technology and genuine, human, personable service they deserve. To learn more, visit joinblvd.com.



About JMI Equity



Founded in 1992, JMI Equity is a growth equity firm focused on investing in leading software companies. JMI has partnered and collaborated with countless entrepreneurs, founder-owners, and management teams over the past 33 years. JMI has invested in 190 software businesses, including 100+ cloud investments, 19 IPOs, and completed 120+ exits. Today, the Firm’s portfolio of industry-leading cloud software companies represents $10 billion in combined revenue, $80 billion in aggregate enterprise value, and over 36,000 jobs. funding_news.title: 5 Questions With: Matt Danna, Co-Founder & CEO of Boulevard
funding_news.ai_summary: Boulevard, a Los Angeles-based AI-driven SaaS platform for salons and spas, secured an $80 million Series D round in July led by JMI Equity, valuing the company at approximately $800 million, bringing its total funding to roughly $188 million. In an interview with American Salon, co-founder and CEO Matt Danna outlined how the funding will support enterprise-grade features and AI tools designed to advance personalization and operational efficiency for appointment-based beauty businesses. The discussion highlighted broader industry trends, including the growing importance of anticipatory service, Gen Z's influence on beauty tech discovery, and the shift toward client-driven engagement models.
funding_news.author: American Salon Staff
funding_news.full_text:
Los Angeles-based Boulevard launched in 2016 as an online booking platform for salons and spas. Since then, it’s grown into an AI-driven SaaS platform designed to help appointment-based beauty and grooming businesses manage everything from scheduling and client communications to payments and marketing. That evolution reflects part of a broader shift across the beauty and wellness sector, where data, automation, and personalization are reshaping how professionals run their businesses — and how consumers experience self-care. To date, Boulevard has raised roughly $188 million in funding, including an $80 million Series D round in July led by JMI Equity, valuing the company at about $800 million. Co-founder and CEO Matt Danna said at the time the funding would help expand “the enterprise-grade features our customers are asking for” while advancing the AI tools “that will define the future of self-care.” Danna recently gave American Salon some insights on how technology is reshaping the beauty consumer experience (and vice versa) and what’s steering Boulevard’s latest investment. View this post on Instagram

AS: How do you see technology reshaping the beauty service consumer experience over the next 5 years? MD: I can’t possibly overstate how important personalization is and will continue to be. We already see this today. Something as simple as personalizing a text leads to 22% more revenue per appointment, 28% higher completion rates, and 16% higher client retention. Now think about how much more powerful personalization can become as software continues to get even more predictive. We’re not far from an era of what I call anticipatory service, where systems account for and act on a client’s history and preferences to proactively suggest services and treatments that are highly customized and strategically tailored to the individual. Already today, 66% of clients say that being remembered by their service provider drives long-term loyalty. That number is going nowhere but up. The question you should be asking yourself is: Is my platform making the client experience better? Your software has to make every single client interaction feel effortless. Otherwise, you’re detracting from the client experience, and that’s an opportunity tax you do not want to pay. AS: How is Gen Z (and soon Gen Alpha) influencing the direction of beauty tech? MD: They’re influencing it in more ways than I think even most salon owners realize. Young generations are discovering salons and stylists in entirely new ways, on their own terms. Fifty-five percent of Gen Z and 47% of Millennials say that your Instagram or TikTok activity is “very” or “extremely” important in deciding whether to book at your salon. Social networks, online communities, virtual marketplaces — these are the customer acquisition and referral channels of the present and future. It goes beyond discovery, though. Younger generations want every interaction to feel like it was designed just for them. They want every aspect of the experience to feel curated around their preferences. They expect you to offer what they want without them ever having to ask for it. In fact, 55% of clients today say they expect to be proactively offered add-ons, memberships, or retail options as part of their experience. All of this is pushing the boundaries of what we mean when we refer to the client experience, and technology has a huge role to play — not just in terms of automating tasks and personalizing experiences, but in ensuring your brand shows up with style at every single touchpoint. AS: Salon and barbershop owners generally want their software to help them save time and make money. What is the one platform feature every business should be using to accomplish those goals? MD: This one is simple for me: intelligent scheduling, which we at Boulevard call Precision Scheduling. Every salon and barbershop owner should be treating their calendar as if it’s their Profit and Loss statement, because it is. Every time you book an appointment, you are in effect managing your revenue. How intelligent your system is and how well it optimizes your daily calendar is what determines if you’re booking a profit or booking a loss. Your system should be able to learn from data such as historical booking patterns and appointment durations so that it can book appointments in a way that drives the most dollars per hour. And it has to be able to do this in a matter of seconds, because that’s often all you have. Clients aren’t interested in waiting around for you to figure out the best time. Your system has to be able to move at their speed. View this post on Instagram AS: Can you think of any digital platform capabilities that are widely used and appreciated by beauty businesses today, but were nonexistent just a few years ago? It’s wild how far the industry’s come in just a few years. Things that were once considered cutting edge, like online booking, client profiles, integrated payments, and text marketing, are now table stakes. I remember a time when proactive texting was considered pushy and intrusive. Now it’s not just OK; it’s expected, and expected to happen immediately: 41% of clients expect a same-day follow-up after their appointment, and 44% say they want those to come via text. We at Boulevard have been obsessed with creating the absolute best online booking experience in the industry, because it’s the digital equivalent of the exterior facade of your storefront. Online booking is such an important factor for prospective clients who are browsing and doing research for deciding to book. Two-thirds of prospective clients are lost if your booking experience isn’t what it needs to be. AS: On the flip side, what do you think will be the next must-have digital tool for beauty businesses that’s just now emerging or currently under development? MD: That’s thinking too small. The future of self-care tech isn’t about any single tool; it’s about evolving technology to match the shifting nature of the salon-client relationship. For the longest time, salons dictated the terms of engagement — how to interact with the business, when and how to book, what to buy, and the vehicles through which to do it all. But today, that dynamic has flipped. Clients are in the driver’s seat, which means the next generation of self-care technology has to be about allowing salons to meet clients where they are. It has to be about adapting in real time to their preferences, behaviors, and communication styles. View this post on Instagram AS: Boulevard recently secured an $80 million Series D investment. Can we get a sneak peek at what new and/or improved features the company is focusing on bringing to its platform? MD: Two big priorities, both of which were priorities even before we raised our Series D. The first is all about what we call enterprise without compromise. It’s ridiculous to me that franchises and multi-location brands have to trade elegance, usability, and platform stability for enterprise-grade capabilities. That should never happen. There’s no reason scale and design can’t co-exist, so we’re doubling down on ensuring that these larger enterprises can get the capabilities they need, along with the design and usability Boulevard is known for. The other area of focus is on high-quality AI. Our approach to AI is very simple: outcomes and impact are what matter. It has to be about doing something meaningful that delivers value beyond what humans can do on their own. Many of our team members come straight from salons and spas. They’ve been stylists, educators, front desk staff, coaches, and managers. They understand the challenges firsthand. AI is an incredibly valuable tool, but it’s not the goal. The goal is and always will be to help our customers deliver flawless, deeply personalized experiences that keep clients coming back.

product_offering.core_offering: Boulevard is an AI-driven SaaS client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses including salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, nail salons, and massage businesses. 2025 launch of Boulevard AI (smart scheduling, automated messaging, personalization, chatbots) is a product-line expansion that monetizes the existing data flywheel across 40,000+ professionals and $5B in payments.

Distribution expansion through Reserve with Google, Facebook/Instagram Book Now, and Zapier integrations enables product-led client acquisition and embeds Boulevard into consumer discovery channels, reducing dependence on direct sales.

Add-on modules such as Boulevard Capital (business financing) and Boulevard Duo hardware extend monetization beyond subscription into financial services and hardware, increasing customer LTV within the existing base.

company_assessment.market_position: Boulevard is a privately held, AI-driven SaaS client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses including salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, nail salons, and massage businesses. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Los Angeles, the company serves more than 40,000 self-care professionals, processes approximately $5 billion in payments annually, and now powers approximately 15% of U.S. medspas. Following an $80 million Series D round led by JMI Equity in July 2025, the company is valued at approximately $800 million and has raised approximately $188 million in total funding across rounds led by Point72 Private Investments, Index Ventures, Toba Capital, and Bonfire Ventures.

strengths.details: At ~15% of US medspas today, Boulevard is in early innings of a HIPAA/EPCS-required vertical with higher willingness-to-pay than salons. Medspa add-ons at $500-$600/location/month expand ARPU and the ePrescribe launch (April 2026) creates a clinical lock-in that should compound into higher enterprise contracts and lower churn over time.
strengths.headline: Medspa expansion unlocks much larger clinical TAM

strengths.details: Processing ~$5B in annual payment volume through a native payfac means Boulevard earns a transaction fee on every dollar that flows through its 40,000+ professionals. As the customer base grows and per-location volume expands (especially with medspa add-ons), payment revenue compounds without proportional sales investment.
strengths.headline: Payments flywheel scales transaction revenue with no incremental CAC

strengths.details: Precision Scheduling™ and Boulevard AI are trained on aggregated booking and $5B payment data from 40,000+ professionals. This proprietary dataset enables personalization and recommendation features that improve with scale, making Boulevard's AI offering structurally harder to replicate by new entrants or generalist competitors.
strengths.headline: AI moat deepens with proprietary booking and transaction data

strengths.details: Boulevard has signed enterprise customers (TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday) and is gating API access, Snowflake Data Share, and advanced permissions behind the Enterprise tier. As the multi-location customer count grows, average contract value should expand materially and pull-through payments, ePrescribe, and Capital financing attach.
strengths.headline: Enterprise and franchise tier drives contract size expansion

strengths.details: The Capital add-on lets Boulevard underwrite or facilitate financing to its existing customer base, monetizing trust and cash-flow data already on the platform. This creates a high-margin fintech layer on top of SaaS and payments with low incremental customer acquisition cost.
strengths.headline: Embedded fintech (Capital) opens new revenue stream from same customers

weakness.details: Mindbody, Fresha (free core product), and Square Appointments (bundled with payments) compete on price and ecosystem breadth. As they push deeper into medspas, Boulevard may face pricing pressure and elevated CAC that compress the path-to-profitability and force discounting at renewal.
weakness.headline: Aggressive incumbents compress pricing and win rates

weakness.details: Serving medspas with HIPAA, EPCS, and clinical charting obligations increases product, security, and support overhead compared to plain salon software. As regulatory expectations evolve (e.g., controlled substance prescribing rules), Boulevard's engineering and compliance resources may be diverted from core salon/spa roadmap, weakening the broader platform.
weakness.headline: Medspa compliance burden could slow product velocity

weakness.details: ePrescribe is delivered through D.A.W. Systems' ScriptSure under a partnership arrangement. Any deterioration in the relationship, partner-side outages, regulatory action against the prescriber network, or unfavorable contract renewal terms directly undermine Boulevard's medspa differentiation and could force costly in-house development.
weakness.headline: Third-party ePrescribe dependency threatens medspa expansion

weakness.details: All revenue is tied to US self-care businesses — a discretionary consumer category. In an economic downturn, average ticket size, visit frequency, and new location openings contract, which directly reduces both SaaS seat revenue and transaction-fee volume from Boulevard Payments.
weakness.headline: Concentration in discretionary US self-care exposes to downturns

weakness.details: The Series D funds expanded enterprise sales, onboarding, and AI features. Enterprise contracts have longer sales cycles and higher service costs than SMB; if enterprise mix grows faster than SMB volume, near-term margins and cash efficiency could deteriorate before enterprise renewal economics kick in.
weakness.headline: Enterprise expansion burn may pressure unit economics before scale

competitive_moat.details: Boulevard's platform embeds memberships, client purchase history, payment processing, clinical charting, and e-prescribing into a single workflow. Once a salon, medspa, or franchise standardizes operations, payment routing, and clinical documentation on Boulevard, migrating that data and re-wiring integrations creates significant operational disruption.

Proprietary Precision Scheduling AI algorithm and the native Boulevard Payments payfac are purpose-built for appointment-based self-care workflows rather than adapted from generic POS/EMR software. The combination of a custom scheduling engine and a vertically-integrated payment stack is difficult for horizontal SaaS players to replicate quickly.

HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, EPCS, and Level 1 PCI certifications are required to serve medspas handling PHI and controlled substances, creating a compliance barrier for new entrants. Boulevard's ePrescribe integration (D.A.W. Systems/ScriptSure) is also operationalized across 30,000+ prescribers nationwide.

Boulevard aggregates behavioral data from 40,000+ self-care professionals and approximately $5 billion in annual payment volume, which feeds the Precision Scheduling algorithm and marketing personalization. This dataset compounds with scale and improves AI quality over time.

Boulevard's native payfac eliminates third-party processor dependencies, while Open APIs (Admin, Client, Credit Card Tokenization, Report Export) at the Enterprise tier create integration stickiness with ERPs, Snowflake, Okta SSO, OPERA PMS, Shopify, and QuickBooks. Hardware (Boulevard Duo) and the Capital financing add-on further entrench customers.

key_risks.details: Boulevard's operations are explicitly domestic USA-only with no global footprint claim. This concentrates risk in a single market and limits TAM relative to international peers like Treatwell or Phorest.
key_risks.headline: US-only geographic concentration limits addressable market

key_risks.details: The self-care booking space includes Mindbody, Vagaro, Fresha, Square Appointments, Booksy, GlossGenius, Zenoti, and Mangomint. Several competitors are VC-backed and price aggressively (Fresha is free for core), pressuring win rates and pricing.
key_risks.headline: Crowded competitive landscape with well-funded incumbents and pure-plays

key_risks.details: Boulevard's new medspa ePrescribe feature is powered entirely by D.A.W. Systems' ScriptSure. Any disruption to this partnership, pricing change, or compliance failure at the partner level directly impacts Boulevard's medspa expansion thesis.
key_risks.headline: Dependency on D.A.W. Systems / ScriptSure for ePrescribe functionality

key_risks.details: Serving medspas requires HIPAA, EPCS, and clinical charting compliance plus medical director workflows — a meaningful operational lift. Compliance failures could trigger regulatory exposure and reputational damage that affect the broader platform.
key_risks.headline: Medspa regulatory complexity raises execution and compliance risk

key_risks.details: Matt Danna (Co-Founder & CEO) is the single named executive with detailed visibility; only a handful of additional leaders (CTO, CFO, CMO) are surfaced. Concentrated founder dependency and limited public detail on the broader bench create succession and execution risk.
key_risks.headline: Key-person dependency on founder-CEO with thin disclosed leadership bench

key_risks.details: Salon, spa, and medspa demand is correlated with discretionary consumer spending. A consumer downturn would directly reduce bookings, payment volume, and customer retention — Boulevard's transaction-fee and subscription revenue are both exposed.
key_risks.headline: Self-care vertical cyclicality tied to discretionary consumer spend

key_highlights.details: Per company materials, Boulevard now serves 40,000+ self-care professionals (up from 25,000 in 2,000 locations at the 2022 Series C) and powers approximately 15% of US medspas, indicating rapid customer growth and vertical penetration.
key_highlights.headline: Strong traction: 40,000+ self-care professionals and ~15% US medspa market share

key_highlights.details: JMI Equity-led $80M Series D in July 2025 valued Boulevard at ~$800M with ~$188M total raised. The platform processes ~$5B in payments annually, indicating significant scale relative to capital deployed.
key_highlights.headline: $800M valuation on $188M cumulative funding and $5B annual payment volume

key_highlights.details: Revenue streams include SaaS subscriptions (medspa add-ons at $500-$600/location/month), transaction fees through Boulevard Payments™ native payfac, and Boulevard Duo™ EMV-certified POS hardware sales, reducing dependency on any single stream.
key_highlights.headline: Diversified revenue model combining SaaS subscription, payment processing, and hardware

key_highlights.details: Certifications across data security (SOC 2 Type 2), healthcare (HIPAA), payments (PCI Level 1), and controlled substance prescribing (EPCS) enable Boulevard to credibly serve medspa and clinical-aesthetics customers where generalist competitors fall short.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade compliance stack: SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, PCI Level 1, EPCS

key_highlights.details: Enterprise customers include TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, and Heyday, demonstrating credibility with multi-location and franchise brands where contract sizes and switching costs are larger.
key_highlights.headline: Strong enterprise and franchise logos: TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday

key_highlights.details: Boulevard combines scheduling (Precision Scheduling™ AI), CRM, POS, marketing, ePrescribe, and payments in one stack, eliminating the fragmented toolset typical of salon/spa operators. The native payfac eliminates third-party processors.
key_highlights.headline: Differentiated all-in-one platform with native payfac and AI scheduling

key_highlights.details: Named to the 2024 Deloitte Technology Fast 500 and recognized as 'Best Value 2025' by Capterra and on G2, providing third-party credibility on growth and customer satisfaction.
key_highlights.headline: External validation: Deloitte Fast 500, Capterra Best Value, G2 recognition

customer_concentration.details: Customer base is broad with 40,000+ self-care professionals served across an estimated thousands of business locations, suggesting a long-tail, volume-driven model rather than reliance on a small number of anchor contracts. Named enterprise and franchise logos (TONI&GUY USA, Face Foundrié, Heyday) indicate Boulevard is winning flagship multi-location brands, but these appear as reference accounts rather than dominant revenue contributors. The vertical segmentation (medspas, salons, spas, barbershops, nail, massage) and explicit SMB/mid-market/enterprise tiering further distribute exposure. Overall concentration risk is Low to Moderate: enterprise wins support marketing credibility, but no single logo appears to materially drive revenue.

launches.title: Curve Dental Introduces Curve Memberships, Helping Practices Strengthen Patient Retention & Profitability Through Membership-Driven Care
launches.ai_summary: Curve Dental announced Curve Memberships, a tool to help practices identify and enroll patients in in-house dental membership plans. The feature automates invitations, posts payments to patient accounts, and integrates with existing workflows. It will roll out to eligible Curve customers this month.
launches.author: Curve Dental
launches.full_text:
Integrated seamlessly with Curve, Curve Memberships helps practices identify enrollment opportunities, automate patient outreach and keep payments connected to billing and collections ALPHARETTA, Ga., Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Curve Dental®, the leader in AI-powered, cloud-native, all-in-one dental practice management software, today announced Curve Memberships, designed to help practices identify patients who could benefit from an in-house dental membership plan, simplify enrollment and build more predictable recurring revenue. Continue Reading

Curve Memberships works seamlessly with Curve Dental practice management software to help practices manage enrollment, membership payments and member activity alongside the workflows they already use every day. Curve Memberships works seamlessly with the patient information dental teams already manage in Curve. Practices can engage uninsured patients and those interested in services outside their insurance coverage—such as whitening and other elective care not covered by their plan—while creating a simpler path to membership enrollment. Once patients enroll, membership payments automatically post to the patient account in Curve, keeping membership billing, collections and patient records connected to the system the practice already uses every day. The result is stronger patient loyalty and a more streamlined membership experience for the practice. "Dental membership plans work—until they become one more thing the front desk has to remember, " said Luke Anderson, Chief Product Officer at Curve Dental. "Curve Memberships connects with the software the team already uses all day, so identifying patients, driving enrollment and managing membership payments becomes part of the workflow—not more tasks to manage. That means practices can grow revenue without adding more work to the team's day." Turning the Schedule Into an Enrollment Engine More than 1 in 5 working-age U.S. adults have no dental benefits, according to the American Dental Association Health Policy Institute, underscoring the need for more flexible ways for patients to access and pay for dental care. In-house dental membership plans can help meet that need, but they often depend on staff recognizing an opportunity, explaining the program during a busy patient interaction and remembering to follow up afterward. Curve Memberships streamlines that process by automatically delivering personalized invitations, helping practices grow enrollment without maintaining separate lists, spreadsheets or manual outreach campaigns. For patients, these plans provide a straightforward, subscription-style way to understand the cost and value of their care. For practices, they can strengthen loyalty and create a more direct, predictable financial relationship with patients. Memberships that Support a Healthier Practice A healthy, growing practice doesn't have to depend on insurance reimbursement alone. Membership plans can help create more predictable recurring revenue while reducing some of the administrative burden that comes with insurance-based care. They can also support case acceptance by giving patients clearer, more approachable costs for services they may otherwise delay or decline—particularly care that falls outside insurance coverage. Dental membership plans create a more direct relationship between the practice and patient, helping practices strengthen loyalty while giving patients a clearer path to care they value. Practices can also use the reports they already rely on in Curve to see production and collections trends across their membership patients and better understand the impact of their program. "Membership-driven care gives practices more control over the economics of care while giving patients a clearer way to say yes to treatment," said Anderson. "Curve Memberships helps make that easier to manage—from identifying opportunities and enrollment through payments and performance." Built for the Way Practices Work Curve Memberships connects membership information with the patient record and everyday workflows dental teams already manage in Curve, giving teams greater visibility into member status and relevant care opportunities without adding another disconnected process. Practices also receive dedicated support for setup and launch, along with a marketing toolkit designed to help introduce, promote and build participation in their membership program. With Curve Memberships, practices can: Identify patients who may benefit from a membership plan

Automatically deliver personalized invitations

See membership information within existing patient workflows

Auto-post payments to the patient account in Curve

Launch and promote plans with dedicated support and marketing resources

Reduce manual tracking, spreadsheets and disconnected processes

Measure contribution through Curve reporting Expanding the Platform Practices Won't Outgrow Curve Memberships is the latest expansion of Curve's end-to-end cloud platform and follows the company's recently announced $200 million commitment to research and development. Curve continues to invest across AI, automation, payments and other tools designed to reduce complexity and help dental practices operate and grow more efficiently. Curve Memberships will be rolled out to eligible Curve customers this month. Practices interested in learning more can visit curvedental.com/membership-plans. About Curve Dental Curve Dental provides an intelligent, cloud-based operating system designed to help dental practices manage and grow their businesses while giving teams more time to focus on patient care. Curve brings together practice management, clinical workflows, revenue cycle capabilities, payments, patient engagement, artificial intelligence and an expanding ecosystem of connected solutions in one platform built for modern dentistry. Curve Dental serves dental professionals and practices across the United States and Canada and is privately held, with operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland. Curve Dental is proud to be named a 2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces award winner. Visit www.curvedental.com or call 1-888-910-HERO for more information. SOURCE Curve Dental

launches.full_text: Appointment reinforces Curve’s $200 million R&D commitment as the company approaches $100 million in annual recurring revenue and accelerates the cloud platform dental practices won’t outgrow ALPHARETTA, Ga., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Curve Dental®, the leader in AI-powered, cloud native all-in-one dental practice management software, today announced the promotion of Luke Anderson to Chief Product Officer, strengthening its executive leadership as the company accelerates an ambitious product roadmap. Anderson joined Curve in 2025 as Senior Vice President of Product, leading product and User Experience. In his expanded role, he will lead Curve’s global product strategy and roadmap, with a focus on native AI, automation, connected workflows and the continued expansion of its end-to-end cloud platform. “The pressures on dental teams have changed dramatically, but many of the solutions in this industry haven’t kept pace,” said Dave Cormack, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Curve Dental. “We are investing heavily in our people and products to change that. Luke brings the product vision, AI expertise and operating discipline to turn that investment into solutions that make running a dental practice dramatically easier. Our goal is to build the most compelling native end-to-end cloud platform in the market—a platform practices won’t outgrow.” Anderson’s appointment is another step in Curve’s broader investment in product innovation. The company supports more than 6,000 dental practice locations across North America and is approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue, driven almost entirely by organic growth. Curve also recently announced a further $200 million commitment to research and development. In 2026, HealthStream Ventures, a leading healthcare business advisory firm, recognized Curve as the cloud-native leader in dental software. Curve’s product strategy is built around a simple premise: dental teams should not have to manage a patchwork of disconnected technology to run their practices. Curve is building around the way dental teams actually work, bringing clinical, financial, administrative and patient-facing workflows together in one cloud-based dental platform, using AI and automation to reduce complexity, remove friction and give teams more time to focus on patients and growth. “The opportunity here is bigger than shipping more features,” said Anderson. “Our job is to listen to dental teams, find where technology slows them down instead of helping, and fix that — simply, and in ways that actually work together. We’re moving quickly, and there’s a lot more coming.” Leadership for Curve’s Next Chapter Anderson brings more than two decades of leadership experience across product strategy, AI and machine learning, high-growth SaaS, private equity and management consulting. Before joining Curve, he led AI and machine learning initiatives at Chick-fil-A and served as Head of Product at OfficeSpace Software, where he led product strategy during a period in which the company nearly tripled annual recurring revenue. Earlier, he held roles with Resurgens Technology Partners and Bain & Company. Anderson began his career as an officer in the United States Marine Corps, serving in leadership and product and program management roles. He is a graduate of the United States Naval Academy and holds an MBA from the University of Virginia’s Darden School of Business. Curve Dental will announce a series of new product launches and platform capabilities over the coming weeks as the company puts its expanded R&D investment to work. Curve Dental serves dental professionals and practices across the United States and Canada and is privately held, with operations in Provo, Utah; Alpharetta, Georgia; Calgary, Alberta; and Aberdeen, Scotland.
