launches.author: Curve Dental
launches.full_text: As Curve Approaches $100 Million in Annual Recurring Revenue, Chairman and CEO Dave Cormack Predicts Major Shift in Dental Software Market ALPHARETTA, Ga., Aug. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Curve Dental®, the leader in modern AI-driven all-in-one dental software with an integrated end-to-end cloud platform, today announced a further $200 million investment in its Curve Hero product and comprehensive ecosystem of native best-in-class capabilities. Record-breaking year-over-year growth since 2018, driven by rapid customer adoption, has enabled Curve to reinvest tens of millions of dollars each year in product development and customer services. The company is rapidly approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue, almost entirely generated through organic growth. With around 20% of the cloud dental practice market, Curve is fulfilling its promise to deliver best-in-class native functionality for single-location, small-group, and DSO practices—without requiring customers to contract with and manage multiple software vendors. Recognizing market demand for an open platform, Curve's API capability supports vendor integrations that meet rigorous standards for quality, security, reliability, interoperability and customer experience. Dave Cormack, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Curve Dental and a 40-year veteran of high-growth software companies, reflected on the company's journey: "Nine years ago, today's leadership team at Curve, having previously grown Brightree from a startup to the most successful cloud software platform in the homecare market, fell in love with the opportunity to deliver the most compelling solution for the dental industry when we saw that close to 100% of the market was relying on 20- to 30-year-old client-server solutions. No other opportunity in healthcare came close. "We acquired Curve Dental because it provided an excellent foundation for us to build a fully integrated, end-to-end cloud platform. In my experience, multi-practice software cannot be scaled down for single locations or small-group practices. It must be built natively from the ground up—and that is exactly what we did. "After $100 million of R&D investment in the last eight years, Curve has continually modernized into a fully native, single sign-on platform for solo practices to small multi-location groups and DSOs, including patient engagement, intelligent phone integration, advanced eligibility, credit card payments, auto payment posting, RCM, membership plans, orthodontics workflow, business intelligence and more. Curve is giving the dental industry a new way to practice and a better way to grow." Investing for the Long Term Cormack said Curve's financial position gives practices confidence that the company will continue investing for the long term: "As a $100 million annual recurring revenue business, we are profitable and growing while reinvesting tens of millions of dollars each year in product development and customer services. As such, the dental market can be confident that we are here for the long term. "My strong advice to any dental practice considering a move to a cloud system is to make sure that the software vendor is profitable, so it can continue to reinvest, and compare what they plan to spend on research and development against Curve's $200 million commitment." Reflecting on Curve's extensive R&D commitment and what he believes will be a major consolidation of the dental software market, Cormack said: "Our leadership has lived this journey many times and, as they say, we've seen this movie before, bought the T-shirt, and we always deliver for our customers. "With 85% of the roughly 160,000 dental practices in North America still on a legacy client-server system, Curve will focus all its efforts on delivering the most compelling native end-to-end cloud platform in the market—one that meets the needs of practices of all sizes and stages of growth, so that they'll never outgrow Curve. "We will achieve that by continuing to hire and retain great people who have a passion and desire to delight our customers. It's the only way." A Market at an Inflection Point Cormack believes the shift from legacy client-server systems to integrated cloud platforms will also drive significant consolidation across the dental software market over the next several years. "A dental software death spiral is upon us. As the market rapidly shifts from legacy systems to the cloud, the vendor market across the ecosystem is oversaturated—from core practice-management platforms to add-on solutions for patient engagement, analytics, imaging and more. "But moving to the cloud is only part of the equation. Practices should look beyond the cloud label to understand how a platform has actually been built and how well its products work together. While Curve has been 100% natively-built, many competitors have acquired a mismatched collection of products that leaves practices with fragmented data, multiple user interfaces, inconsistent workflows and integration complexity. These platforms do anything but operate as one unified system. "I predict that over 40 percent of practice management software vendors, with an alarming number burning through cash to buy market share at the expense of R&D and customer services, will not exist in 36 to 48 months. The same pressure will affect point solutions that create more complexity than differentiated customer value, as AI-driven cloud platforms increasingly deliver those capabilities natively in a fully integrated manner and at a lower total cost of ownership than practices currently employ through licensing software from five or six different vendors. Cormack concluded by returning to Curve's commitment to its customers: "Our customers' success is how we measure our own success. We work to earn their business every single day by listening, responding promptly and continually keeping the Curve Hero platform ahead of our competition. "If you haven't seen Curve in action recently—or at all—I encourage you to talk with us about the challenges you face and see how we can better serve you." launches.full_text:
New voice-driven AI suite helps dental teams streamline documentation, charting, and perio workflows directly inside Curve’s cloud-based practice management platform. Curve Care+ helps dental teams streamline clinical documentation, charting, and perio workflows with native AI built directly into Curve Dental’s cloud-based platform Curve Dental®, the leading provider of all-in-one, cloud-based dental practice management software, recently announced the launch of Curve Care+, a native, voice-driven clinical AI suite designed to help providers reduce documentation burden, streamline charting, and create more time for patient care. Embedded directly into the Curve platform, Curve Care+ introduces three native AI-powered solutions—Notes+, Charting+, and Perio+—giving dental teams ambient intelligence that lives in their existing clinical workflows, without bolted-on extensions, separate logins, or disconnected third-party tools. “Dental teams are under constant pressure to do more with less time,” said Suzanne Henderson, Chief Technology Officer at Curve Dental. “Curve Care+ was built to further simplify the tools providers already use every day, helping teams work more efficiently while preserving the human connection at the center of patient care.” A New Approach to Clinical Documentation Curve Care+ is designed around a simple goal: ensuring documentation happens while care is happening—not during lunch breaks, between appointments, or after hours. Offered as part of the broader Curve+ AI Suite, the Curve Care+ clinical AI solution includes the following: Notes+ ambiently captures clinical conversations and drafts provider-ready notes in either SOAP format or the practice’s own templates.

Innovations such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and 3D imaging integration are enhancing the efficiency, accuracy, and accessibility of dental care. Cloud-based platforms offer real-time access to patient records, enabling seamless data sharing and remote consultations, especially beneficial for multi-location practices and tele-dentistry. AI-powered tools assist in diagnostic support, treatment planning, and predictive analytics, improving patient outcomes and workflow automation. Additionally, the integration of dental imaging with electronic health records (EHRs) allows for more precise and data-driven decision-making. Voice recognition, automated billing, and appointment scheduling further reduce administrative burdens on dental staff. These technologies not only optimize clinic operations but also elevate the overall patient experience. As digital transformation accelerates, technological innovation will continue to be a cornerstone of growth and competitive differentiation in the dental software market. Pricing Analysis of the Dental Software Market The pricing structure of dental software varies significantly based on deployment model, features offered, and practice size. Cloud-based solutions typically operate on a subscription model, with monthly fees ranging from $100 to $800 depending on the number of users, storage capacity, and included functionalities such as imaging integration, billing, and patient communication tools. On-premise software often involves a one-time licensing fee, which can range from $2,000 to $10,000, along with additional costs for maintenance, updates, and IT support. Basic practice management tools are priced lower, while comprehensive platforms offering AI diagnostics, EHR integration, and analytics capabilities command premium pricing. Customization, training, and scalability options also influence overall costs. Small and mid-sized clinics prefer cost-effective, modular solutions, while large dental service organizations invest in enterprise-grade platforms. As competition intensifies and cloud adoption rises, vendors are increasingly offering flexible pricing plans and tiered subscriptions to cater to diverse practice needs and budgets. Market Concentration and Competitive Landscape To learn more about this report, Request Free Sample Dental Software Market Trends Rising demand for dental practice management software With the growing complexity of dental practices and rising pressures to reduce costs and boost efficiency, the demand for robust dental practice management software has increased tremendously in recent years. Traditional paper-based methods for managing patient records, billing, insurance claims, and appointment scheduling have become outdated and inefficient. Dental practice management software allows practices to digitize and streamline these operations in one centralized system. It ensures smooth workflows, timely follow-ups with patients, proper documentation of treatments, and hassle-free billing and claims processing. Moreover, dental practice management software offers valuable data-driven insights that help dental professionals enhance the patient experience and decision making. Features like analytics dashboards provide actionable information on practice performance, treatment trends, top referral sources, and more. In June 2025, The Times of India reported that King George’s Medical University in Lucknow has introduced laser-assisted root canal treatment (RCT) using Er:YAG, Nd:YAG, and diode lasers reducing procedure time and pain while improving precision. Though not software per se, the adoption of laser-integrated digital workflows reflects growing digitization and computer-assisted technology integration in modern dental care systems. Integration of modern technologies There is a growing interest among dental professionals and patients in advanced dental technologies like cone beam CT scans, intraoral cameras, imaging software and digital x-rays that enhance accuracy of diagnoses and treatment outcomes. Concerns around radiation exposure from traditional x-rays are spurring wider use of digital alternatives. To leverage modern tools and cater to evolving patient needs, dental practices require specialized software solutions that allow seamless integration of these technologies. Dental software vendors are addressing this need by developing programs compatible with the latest dental equipment and tools. Features like tools for 3D imaging and scans, digital recordkeeping of x-rays, and screen sharing functionalities are attractive to dental practices. These offer productivity gains over peripherals or manual workarounds. The availability of such specialized yet affordable software encourages dental practices to invest in innovative technologies. In June 2025, The Times of India also reported that Inamdar Multispeciality Hospital in Pune has inaugurated a 24×7 Dental & Face Surgery Clinic, equipped for trauma and implant care. Such clinics increasingly rely on advanced digital diagnostic and treatment planning software, including imaging and surgical simulation tools, to support complex procedures and improve patient outcomes. Opportunities in the Dental Software Market Emergence of cloud-based dental practice management and imaging solutions Cloud software eliminates the need for large upfront investments in hardware and infrastructure. It allows dental practices of all sizes to access advanced features and functionalities traditionally available only to large enterprise customers. The low total cost of ownership along with flexibility and scalability offered by cloud makes it attractive for small and medium dental clinics. With cloud, dental practices can focus more on patient care rather than IT maintenance and upgrades. This enables more dentists to adopt practice management and imaging software. company_assessment.market_position: Curve Dental (legally CD Newco, LLC) is a privately held provider of cloud-based dental practice management software founded in 2004, headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia with a Provo, Utah presence. The company serves over 80,000 dental professionals across North America with a self-positioned #1 ranking in cloud-based dental software and recognition as the cloud-native leader in the HealthStream Ventures 2026 Dental Technology Landscape report. The company serves dental practices ranging from solo startups through multi-location groups and Dental Support Organizations (DSOs).

strengths.details: Curve Pay (Sept 2025) and the AI Suite (Eligibility+, Pearl, Ask CurveAI, Curve Flo Care) move Curve from per-seat subscription to higher-leverage transaction-fee and AI-module monetization. With 80K+ professionals already on the platform, even modest attach rates on payments volume and AI modules can materially expand revenue per customer without equivalent sales-cost scaling.
strengths.headline: Embedded payments + AI attach unlock ARR-expansion beyond seat-based SaaS

strengths.details: Most dental practices still run server-based PMS (Dentrix, Eaglesoft). Curve's 2,500 migrations this year and 4,500+ total conversions from 90+ platforms point to ongoing secular shift to cloud-native. Each migration locks in multi-year recurring revenue and creates cross-sell/upsell runway for AI and payments products on top of the base SaaS contract.
strengths.headline: Dental cloud migration is early innings with massive legacy installed base

strengths.details: Multi-location practices and DSOs are Curve's fastest-scaling segment, with named accounts including Link DSO and Emerson Dental having scaled from single-digit to 22+ offices on Curve. As healthcare consolidation accelerates, large multi-site contracts tend to be larger, stickier, and command enterprise pricing—lifting blended ARPU and net retention.
strengths.headline: DSO consolidation drives upmarket land-and-expand

strengths.details: Curve's multi-modal AI stack (computer vision via Pearl, ambient documentation via Curve Flo Care, NLP via Ask CurveAI, process automation via Eligibility+) compounds with proprietary SmartSync data layer. As AI training data and integrations accumulate, the gap between Curve and bolt-on or server-based competitors should widen, supporting premium pricing and lower churn.
strengths.headline: AI-native feature suite deepens competitive moat over bolt-on rivals

weakness.details: Henry Schein One and Patterson have launched or acquired cloud-native products and have far larger sales reach, financing arms, and bundled supply/hardware relationships. If incumbents achieve feature parity on cloud PMS while preserving their existing install base, Curve's land-and-expand motion in legacy accounts becomes significantly harder and customer acquisition costs rise.
weakness.headline: Incumbents are aggressively cloud-ifying and could close the gap

weakness.details: Curve is entirely dependent on dental-practice economics. Insurance reimbursement compression, rising labor costs, soft patient volumes, and a potential recession could push practices to defer SaaS upgrades, reduce add-on module spend, or consolidate vendors—pressuring net retention and gross margins despite a sticky recurring base.
weakness.headline: Dental sector headwinds could compress software budget cycles

weakness.details: Curve Pay depends on Stripe, key AI imaging features run through Pearl, and Eligibility+ runs through DentalXChange. Any of these partners raising prices, changing terms, launching competing products, or being acquired by a competitor could directly undermine Curve's differentiated value proposition and create revenue disruption.
weakness.headline: Partner concentration risk on Stripe, Pearl, and DentalXChange

weakness.details: Limited to U.S. (and Canada in 2026), Curve's addressable market is roughly 200K+ U.S. dental practices. Without international expansion, long-term growth eventually becomes a function of U.S. penetration depth rather than market breadth—limiting the ultimate multiple a strategic or PE buyer would pay relative to globally diversified vertical SaaS peers.
weakness.headline: Geographic concentration caps TAM without successful international push

competitive_moat.details: Data conversion services across 90+ legacy platforms and 4,500+ historical migrations create high switching friction in both directions; once practices migrate clinical, billing, and imaging data onto the platform, the cost and operational risk of returning to an alternative is meaningful. Steady migration cadence (2,500+ this year) signals ongoing new-logo accretion that strengthens installed-base lock-in.

An unusually dense integration ecosystem spanning AI diagnostics (Pearl Second Opinion, Practice Intelligence), ambient documentation (Bola AI, Mango Voice), patient acquisition (Patient Prism), payments (Stripe, Affirm, Klarna), insurance (DentalXChange), and membership plans (DentalHQ) makes Curve a de facto connective layer for downstream dental software stacks. Partners gain distribution and Curve gains stickier workflows that competitors must replicate one-by-one.

Proprietary SmartSync technology underpins insurance verification and multi-location data integrity; cloud-native architecture is recognized as the leader for single-location and small/mid multi-location practices by HealthStream Ventures' 2026 Dental Technology Landscape report. Brand is positioned as the #1 cloud-based dental software, reinforced by 80K+ practitioner footprint.

80K+ dental professionals on a unified cloud instance generate aggregated, cross-practice workflow, claims, and scheduling data that improves AI features such as Eligibility+, Ask CurveAI recommendations, and Pearl-powered analytics. This data flywheel compounds versus fragmented on-prem incumbents that cannot pool signal across their user base.

Cloud-native delivery eliminates $20K+ on-premise server costs and roughly $500/month IT overhead per practice, and reduces multi-location IT spend by ~90% — a structural TCO advantage over server-based incumbents that compounds for DSOs and multi-location groups.

key_risks.details: Curve Dental competes against Henry Schein One (Dentrix, Eaglesoft), Patterson Dental, Open Dental, CareStack, Planet DDS/Denticon, tab32, and a long tail of regional vendors. Incumbents have decades of installed base and bundled hardware/services relationships, raising customer-acquisition costs.
key_risks.headline: Highly competitive dental PMS market with deep-pocketed incumbents

key_risks.details: Curve Dental operates exclusively in the dental vertical and primarily in the U.S., making revenue dependent on dental-practice formation rates, consumer discretionary spending on dental care, insurance reimbursement trends, and consolidation velocity among DSOs—all of which are sensitive to macro conditions.
key_risks.headline: End-market concentration in U.S. dentistry creates sector-cyclical exposure

key_risks.details: Several headline features depend on external partners: Pearl (AI imaging/analytics), DentalXChange (Eligibility+), Stripe (Curve Pay), Mango Voice (call documentation), Bola AI (clinical notes), and Patient Prism (marketing AI). Partner pricing changes, product pivots, or competitive conflicts could materially weaken Curve's value proposition.
key_risks.headline: Heavy reliance on third-party AI/integration partners for differentiated capabilities

key_risks.details: Operating geographies are limited to the U.S. (primary) and Canada (newly expanding with Curve Pay in 2026). The company has no stated roadmap for international expansion, restricting growth to North American dental markets while global SaaS peers extend internationally.
key_risks.headline: Limited geographic reach caps TAM ceiling near-term

key_risks.details: Curve Dental's '#1 Ranked Cloud-Based Dental Software' claim is self-positioned rather than awarded by an independent third party. The HealthStream Ventures 2026 analyst recognition as cloud-native leader is more credible but limited in scope to single-location and small/mid multi-location segments.
key_risks.headline: Self-positioned #1 ranking is weaker than independent verification

key_risks.details: Public data indicates only a 2018 Battery Ventures investment with undisclosed amount; no subsequent rounds, board composition, cap-table signals, or named institutional backers are disclosed. Lack of funding transparency makes it harder to assess burn, runway, and capital efficiency.
key_risks.headline: Ownership/investor details are opaque and no funding history is disclosed

key_highlights.details: Curve Dental reports being trusted by over 80,000 dental professionals across practices of all sizes including startups, single-location, and multi-location/DSO segments, providing a substantial recurring-revenue foundation and reference base.
key_highlights.headline: Large installed base of 80,000+ dental professionals across North America

key_highlights.details: The company has completed 2,500+ migrations in the current year and 4,500+ total data conversions from 90+ legacy platforms, indicating strong win-rate against entrenched server-based incumbents and effective product-led onboarding.
key_highlights.headline: Sustained customer-acquisition engine with 2,500 successful migrations in the current year

key_highlights.details: Customer-reported outcomes include up to 5x ROI, 20% higher collections, 25% more new patients, and 30% better case acceptance, providing concrete value-prop ammunition that supports pricing power and a high switching-cost story.
key_highlights.headline: Quantified customer ROI: 5x returns, 20% higher collections, 25% more new patients, 30% better case acceptance

key_highlights.details: SmartSync enables real-time cross-location data synchronization, while a unified platform covers scheduling, charting, imaging, billing, payments, and patient engagement in one system—reducing the IT complexity and integration overhead typical of dental practices using multiple legacy tools.
key_highlights.headline: Cloud-native all-in-one architecture with proprietary SmartSync differentiates from bolt-on competitors

key_highlights.details: Curve Dental maintains SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and SOX compliance at its data center, qualifying it for DSOs and enterprise buyers with stringent security/procurement requirements.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade security and compliance stack: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, SOX

key_highlights.details: Multiple AI-powered launches in 2025 include the AI Analytics Module (Mar 2025), Mango Voice integration (Feb 2025), Eligibility+ with DentalXChange (Aug 2025), expanded Pearl Practice Intelligence (Aug 2025), and Curve Flo Care ambient AI documentation, positioning Curve as an AI-forward category leader.
key_highlights.headline: Active AI productization across imaging, voice, ambient documentation, and NLP support

key_highlights.details: Revenue is generated through monthly SaaS subscriptions (location/doctor/user-based), Curve Pay transaction fees (Stripe-powered), and one-time implementation/data-conversion services, creating multiple monetization vectors beyond core seat-based SaaS.
key_highlights.headline: Diversified revenue model spanning subscription, transaction fees, and professional services

customer_concentration.details: The customer base spans thousands of independent dental practices plus mid-market multi-location groups (e.g., Emerson Dental, Town Dentistry, a practice scaled from 15 to 22 offices under Dr. Hans Herchen) and at least one named DSO (Link DSO), with a cited 80,000+ dental professional footprint that implies a meaningfully distributed revenue base. Pricing is subscription-based per location/doctor/user — a structure that, together with high migration volumes (2,500 this year), points to recurring diversified revenue rather than a small number of large anchors; no single customer is identified as materially driving revenue. The principal concentration risk is vertical — 100% of revenue is exposed to U.S./Canadian dental practice economics, insurance reimbursement cycles, and small-business discretionary spending — rather than customer-level concentration. This produces predictable churn patterns but limited defense against vertical downturns.

They leave a negative review of your inefficient spa booking. Or maybe it’s time to get some good spa management software and let them book in a few taps, knowing availability in real-time? If you want to give zen to your guests and spa receptionists (and unite it with accounting, management, and marketing), this guide is for you. We cover the main users, features, and key integrations you need for your hotel spa software needs. Then, we review the top off-the-shelf tools and compare them to a fully custom roadmap (with some insider tips). ‍ What is spa management software? Spa management software is a purpose-built digital platform that handles the operational and business side of running a spa. It covers everything from booking appointments and tracking client histories to processing payments, managing staff schedules, and reporting revenue. Overall, it’s the nervous system of a spa business. Without it, everything runs on clipboards, spreadsheets, and memory, while with it, the whole operation connects. According to Samkange and his team, operations management in a spa context means transforming inputs such as staff, proprietary treatments, and physical facilities into measurable guest experiences. Spa management software is the tool that makes this transformation trackable, repeatable, and profitable. Market overview The global spa industry hit $18.1 billion in revenue in 2021, a 49% jump from the year before, with 173 million visits recorded in the U.S. alone. Globally, the market is on track to exceed $185 billion by 2030. The hotel spa software segment sits at the center of this growth. A 2025 CBRE Hotels analysis of 297 U.S. hotel spas found that spa revenue averaged $6,061 per available room, contributing 3.4% of total hotel revenue. At luxury properties, the share jumps to 4.2%. So if you’re still treating your spa returns as a side business, it’s time to rethink. Spa is a revenue line that hotel operators now manage as seriously as rooms or food and beverage. The spa business software market reflects that pressure. It’s projected to reach $2.92 billion by 2035, growing at a compound annual rate of 19.6%. However, challenges are still evident. For instance, 42% of small spa operators say upfront software costs are a genuine barrier, and 54% of SMEs using cloud-based systems report gaps in data compliance. There’s a massive demand, but the friction is big, as well. Core purpose The main purpose is clear: spa software exists to turn a complex, people-heavy operation into something one person can actually manage. Every hotel spa runs on a web of separate processes, services, and people. Therapists, rooms, products, bookings, guests, hotel systems, payroll. Hotel spa management software pulls all of that into a single place so nothing falls through the cracks and every decision is backed by real numbers. That one statement breaks down into four specific jobs the software does. Function What it solves Business result Scheduling and capacity Empty rooms, double bookings, therapist conflicts Higher room utilization, fewer errors, optimized labor Guest experience tracking Impersonal service, lost client preferences, zero continuity Repeat visits, stronger loyalty, personalized treatment Revenue management Underpriced packages, missed upsells, opaque retail performance Higher revenue per visit, better package design, and retail growth Operations and compliance Manual scheduling, inventory gaps, payroll complexity Reduced admin time, accurate stock levels, and clear cost reporting Scheduling and capacity control. Staff scheduling, payroll data, inventory levels, product usage logs. The system keeps daily operations running and gives managers a clear picture of where costs are going. Now that we know why you need such a type of solution for your business, let’s define who exactly benefits from using it daily. Key users: who uses this software day to day? The short answer is everyone who touches the spa operation, and that group is larger than most people assume. Mandelbaum and Grigg found that staffing structures in 297 hotels range from lean urban operations relying heavily on contract therapists (up to 17.9% of payroll at city hotels) to full resort spa teams with senior therapists, front-of-house hosts, retail staff, and dedicated spa managers. Each of these roles interacts with the software differently. Front desk and reception staff are the primary daily users of spa appointment software. They manage the booking flow: new reservations, cancellations, rebooking, check-ins, and waitlists. At a resort spa seeing hundreds of guests a week, this happens in real time across multiple channels: walk-in, phone, hotel concierge, and online booking. The software needs to be fast and impossible to break under pressure.

They manage the booking flow: new reservations, cancellations, rebooking, check-ins, and waitlists. At a resort spa seeing hundreds of guests a week, this happens in real time across multiple channels: walk-in, phone, hotel concierge, and online booking. The software needs to be fast and impossible to break under pressure. Spa directors and operations managers spend more time in reporting and staffing views. They track therapist utilization, monitor revenue by service type, and manage scheduling to balance labor costs against demand.

They track therapist utilization, monitor revenue by service type, and manage scheduling to balance labor costs against demand. Finance and back-office teams work primarily in spa accounting software, pulling reports on revenue per treatment room, cost of goods sold, retail margins, and labor as a percentage of revenue. In 2024, CBRE data showed that labor costs rose 3.9% while spa revenues grew only 1.4%. That kind of pressure makes accurate, real-time financial data non-negotiable. Therapists and treatment staff use the system indirectly, accessing client notes before appointments and logging treatment records after. Hotels like The Retreat at Blue Lagoon in Iceland or luxury urban properties expanding their local market reach (a trend Mandelbaum and Grigg highlight) need software that works for all of these users simultaneously, across different access levels and different daily realities. ‍ Why hotels need spa management software Hotels do not run spas the way standalone day spas do. The context is completely different, and that difference is exactly why generic wellness software falls short and purpose-built hotel spa software exists. Here is what makes the hotel spa environment uniquely demanding. Your spa is inside a larger operational machine. A hotel is a system. company_assessment.market_position: Mangomint, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based, privately held SaaS company founded in 2017 that sells cloud-based salon, spa, and med spa management software to U.S. beauty and wellness operators. The company positions itself as the "#1 highest-rated by thousands of beauty & wellness professionals," supported by 2025–2026 badges from G2, Capterra, GetApp, and Software Advice, and inclusion on Deloitte's 2025 Technology Fast 500 among 20 Los Angeles/Orange County companies. It competes in the vertical SaaS market for beauty and wellness alongside legacy and modern salon-software vendors, and differentiates on a modern UI, an all-in-one product surface area (scheduling, POS, client management, marketing automation, unified communications, payroll), and a HIPAA-compliant Med Spa offering with BAA.

strengths.details: Mangomint's vertically integrated platform spans scheduling, POS, payments, marketing automation, memberships, payroll, and now unified communications — replacing the fragmented tool stacks used by most independent operators. With 'thousands' of salons/spas already on the platform across twelve beauty/wellness verticals, each new module adoption deepens account stickiness and expands wallet share, compounding into a higher-LTV customer base as the platform becomes irreplaceable in operators' daily workflows.
strengths.headline: System of record for beauty & wellness SMBs

strengths.details: Med spas are among the fastest-growing segments in beauty/wellness, with willingness to pay meaningfully above traditional salons due to clinical workflows, charting needs, and HIPAA obligations. Forms & Charting add-on and BAA availability position Mangomint to capture disproportionate share of this segment; as the Med Spa customer base grows, blended ARPU should rise because these accounts typically upgrade to higher-tier plans and consume more add-ons (Forms, Connect, Payroll).
strengths.headline: Med Spa vertical tailwind unlocks higher-ACV expansion

strengths.details: Mangomint Connect (launched Oct 2025) unifies phone, SMS, and web chat against the client record — and Mangomint's revenue leaders presented on 'AI in B2B sales' at SaaStr AI London, signaling active investment in AI-driven features. Bundling AI-powered two-way texting, voicemail summarization, and automated client rebooking into the existing communications stack creates a defensible automation moat vs. legacy salon software that lacks a native unified inbox to feed AI workflows.
strengths.headline: Connect + AI turn Mangomint into a front-desk automation layer

strengths.details: Pricing model is explicitly engineered for expansion: Essentials ($165/mo) up to Unlimited ($375/mo), with per-location add-on pricing for Connect, Forms & Charting, and Shopify, plus usage-based marketing credits and integrated payment processing. As customer counts scale and operators add locations or upgrade plans, ARR compounds without proportional sales-cost growth — a classic SMB SaaS expansion flywheel already validated by the Multi-Location feature module.
strengths.headline: Land-and-expand via per-location add-ons

strengths.details: Free 1:1 onboarding, free data import, and cancel-anytime positioning have translated into six 2025-2026 G2/Capterra/GetApp/Software Advice badges and Deloitte Fast 500 recognition. As review-site reputation compounds, organic top-of-funnel acquisition should continue to scale efficiently — lowering blended CAC relative to paid-channel-dependent competitors and supporting the path to sustained Rule-of-40+ SaaS economics.
strengths.headline: Free onboarding + zero contracts drive viral review-site acquisition

weakness.details: Fresha offers free salon/spa software monetized on payment processing, and Square Appointments is bundled free with Square's broader SMB POS ecosystem — both raising the floor on customer expectations around price. Mangomint's $165-$375/month subscription tiers assume a willingness to pay for premium UX and bundled modules; if either free competitor closes feature gaps (especially on payments or unified communications), Mangomint's pricing power and gross retention could deteriorate meaningfully.
weakness.headline: Fresha + Square compress price umbrella

weakness.details: Mindbody (private equity-backed, vertically integrated with ClassPass) and Vagaro dominate the mid-market and enterprise end of the market with deep integrations to consumer marketplaces, distribution networks, and class/wellness platforms that Mangomint lacks. As independent salons and spas grow into multi-location mid-market operators, switching costs to enterprise-grade incumbents could displace Mangomint at the high-value end of its customer base, compressing net dollar retention.
weakness.headline: Mindbody/Vagaro enterprise lock-in pressure intensifies

weakness.details: Mangomint's marketing and product positioning emphasize UI polish, automation, and unified communications — areas where generative AI could allow leanly-capitalized AI-native startups to replicate core workflows (booking, reminders, marketing copy, re-engagement) at lower price points. If AI-native competitors compress development cost and time-to-feature parity, Mangomint's engineering investment advantage (justified by its $35M Series B) erodes, and category leadership becomes contested.
weakness.headline: AI-native booking entrants disrupt SMB funnel

weakness.details: Operating geographies are exclusively US-based, with US-specific regulatory positioning (HIPAA BAA, US payment processors, US-focused content and customer logos). International salon/spa software markets (Europe, APAC, LATAM) are served by Phorest, Treatwell, Zenoti, and regional players; without geographic expansion, Mangomint's TAM is structurally capped at US SMB beauty/wellness, limiting the upside path to a $1B+ outcome that international peers can pursue.
weakness.headline: Geographic confinement caps addressable expansion

weakness.details: Transaction-based revenue from Mangomint's integrated payment processing (2.45% + 15¢ in-person / 2.90% + 30¢ virtual) is directly correlated with end-customer spend at salons and spas. In a consumer downturn or rising SMB churn, transaction revenue contracts before subscription revenue, magnifying revenue volatility — and merchants on Mangomint's processor who switch to external processors (preserving only the subscription) directly reduce blended ARPU without reducing churn risk.
weakness.headline: Payment-processing dependency ties revenue to consumer cycles

competitive_moat.details: Once onboarded, customers embed client history, memberships, automated marketing flows, stored payment methods, and payroll records in Mangomint. Mangomint itself offers free 1:1 onboarding and free data import to lower the initial switching barrier, which paradoxically seeds durable retention by loading operational complexity into the platform.

HIPAA-compliant Forms & Charting with a BAA available on Standard and Unlimited plans positions Mangomint to credibly serve the regulated med spa and clinical aesthetics vertical. This compliance posture is a documented prerequisite for that segment and is not universally offered by all salon-software competitors.

Brand positioning as the "#1 highest-rated" platform, corroborated by multiple 2025-2026 G2, Capterra, GetApp, and Software Advice badges, plus Deloitte Technology Fast 500 inclusion. Brand recognition is genuine within a narrow vertical but not broad enough to constitute a wide-moat asset.

Free 1:1 personalized onboarding with a dedicated onboarding manager and free data import (clients, products, gift cards, notes, services, transactions, history) shortens sales cycles and is a tangible differentiator against legacy salon software. Combined with a dual inside-sales + PLG trial funnel and SEO-rich vertical landing pages, distribution is a real, if not extraordinary, advantage.

Aggregated appointment, payment, and retention data across "thousands" of salons and spas could power benchmarking and smarter defaults over time, but the company has not disclosed any data-network effects, proprietary models, or benchmarking products. Data advantage is therefore latent rather than realized.

No cost advantage is documented. Pricing is at or above category norms (Essentials $165/mo to Unlimited $375/mo), and payment processing rates (2.45% + 15¢ in-person) are standard rather than discount-driven. Capital from the $35M Series B enables product and support investment but does not translate to unit-economics superiority.

key_risks.details: Salon/spa software is one of the most crowded vertical SaaS categories, with several well-capitalized competitors (Mindbody/ClassPass-owned, Boulevard, Zenoti) and free alternatives (Fresha) pursuing overlapping customer bases. Mangomint must continuously out-execute on UX and bundling to defend share, and any pricing pressure from a free or low-cost competitor directly threatens ARPU.
key_risks.headline: Hyper-competitive vertical with well-funded direct peers (Mindbody, Vagaro, Boulevard, Zenoti, Fresha, GlossGenius)

key_risks.details: Operating geographies and regulatory certifications are exclusively US-based; content, HIPAA positioning, payment processing, and customer base all reference US salons, medspas, and beauty/wellness operators. International competitors like Phorest (Europe/global) and Zenoti (global) operate across geographies where Mangomint does not compete, limiting long-term expansion optionality.
key_risks.headline: US-only geographic footprint caps TAM and leaves international markets to global competitors

key_risks.details: Pricing is explicitly no-contract, cancel-anytime, monthly billing starting at $165 — characteristic of an SMB-heavy customer base that historically exhibits 2-3x higher gross dollar churn than mid-market SaaS. Featured customers skew toward single-location and small multi-location operators, which amplifies churn sensitivity to economic cycles and competitive pricing pressure.
key_risks.headline: SMB customer base with monthly no-contract billing creates structurally higher churn exposure

key_risks.details: Source data confirms no public or partner-facing API, SDK, or developer portal is documented — only a native Shopify integration is offered as a paid add-on. The absence of an API limits third-party ecosystem development (custom integrations, app marketplace, agency channel), constraining the platform's reach relative to peers that have built developer ecosystems.
key_risks.headline: No documented public API or developer ecosystem creates lock-in ceiling and ecosystem dependency

key_risks.details: Transaction-based revenue from Mangomint's integrated payment processing (2.45% + 15¢ in-person / 2.90% + 30¢ virtual) is tied to end-customer payment volume. While customers can opt out by using their own processor, doing so forfeits Express Booking, cards-on-file, deposits, and self checkout — concentrating a non-trivial revenue stream in a volume-sensitive channel vulnerable to consumer spending downturns.
key_risks.headline: Dependency on integrated payment processing ties a portion of revenue to payment-volume cycles

key_risks.details: Explicit HIPAA posture and Forms & Charting add-on serve med spas and IV therapy clinics — categories that handle protected health information and operate under state medical board oversight. Any breach, audit, or regulatory tightening (e.g., changing HIPAA enforcement, state telehealth rules) creates direct liability exposure and could require unplanned compliance investment that smaller SaaS competitors may not need to bear.
key_risks.headline: Med Spa vertical exposure increases regulatory and clinical workflow risk

key_highlights.details: Featured among 20 LA/Orange County companies on Deloitte's 2025 Technology Fast 500 for revenue growth from 2021 to 2024 — one of the most credible external validations of a high-growth B2B SaaS business. The company sits alongside peers that registered growth rates up to 29,738% over the measurement window.
key_highlights.headline: Deloitte 2025 Technology Fast 500 honoree validating sustained triple-digit revenue growth (2021-2024)

key_highlights.details: Closed a $35M Series B led by Altos Ventures in Sept 2024, with OpenView and SaaStr Fund participating, and a $12M debt facility from Avidbank. Cumulative capital raised exceeds $60M, explicitly earmarked for product expansion and customer support scale-up — a strong runway relative to its Series B stage.
key_highlights.headline: Well-capitalized with $35M Series B led by Altos Ventures in September 2024

key_highlights.details: Mangomint Connect (launched Oct 2025) consolidates phone calls, two-way SMS, and web chat into a single inbox synced with the client record — a bundled native capability that legacy competitors typically require third-party integrations to assemble. Includes dedicated per-location numbers, unlimited domestic minutes, and a web chat widget.
key_highlights.headline: Unified communications (Mangomint Connect) is a genuine product differentiator vs. legacy salon software

key_highlights.details: Serves hair salons, med spas, IV therapy, skincare studios, beauty studios, massage studios, hair removal studios, tattoo & piercing studios, nail salons, barbershops, wellness centers, and day spas from a single codebase — broadening the addressable customer base while concentrating engineering investment.
key_highlights.headline: Multi-vertical platform serving twelve distinct beauty/wellness segments reduces segment-specific risk

key_highlights.details: Includes free 1:1 personalized onboarding with a dedicated onboarding manager and free data import (clients, products, gift cards, notes, services, transaction and appointment history) with every plan. No contracts, cancel anytime. This GTM motion is a tangible competitive advantage against legacy salon software with self-serve or fee-based onboarding.
key_highlights.headline: Differentiated white-glove onboarding and free data import lower customer acquisition friction

key_highlights.details: Holds six 2025-2026 third-party review badges (Capterra Best for Ease of Use 2026, G2 High Performer Winter 2026, G2 Best Support Winter 2026, G2 Easiest to Use Winter 2026, GetApp Best Functionality & Features 2025, Software Advice Best Customer Support 2026), positioned on the homepage as the '#1 highest-rated by thousands of beauty & wellness professionals.'
key_highlights.headline: Stack of six 2025-2026 G2/Capterra/GetApp/Software Advice badges reinforces category-leading brand reputation

key_highlights.details: Forms & Charting add-on plus BAA availability on Standard and Unlimited plans explicitly target the regulated Med Spa segment — a fast-growing vertical with higher willingness to pay, longer retention, and stricter compliance requirements that deter undifferentiated competitors. Named customers include Bare Laser Med Spa and Pure Beauty Aesthetics.
key_highlights.headline: HIPAA-compliant Med Spa offering opens a regulated, high-ACV vertical with structural tailwinds

customer_concentration.details: Mangomint's logo wall is dominated by independent and small-chain operators (Atomic Tattoo, Cape Cod Nail Co, Cheeks and Co, Glassskin, Mero Mero, My Little Beautique, Pony Studios Co, Yello, Sugarmoon, House of Aanuko, Goldust Studios, Pure Beauty Aesthetics, Vanity Projects, N Natural Hair Studio) with only a handful of larger brands (Anastasia Beverly Hills, Ouidad). Per-location subscription pricing ($165-$375/mo plus add-ons) and explicit language describing "thousands of salons and spas" indicate a long-tail, distributed revenue base with no single-customer dependency. The risk to revenue predictability is therefore not concentration but SMB churn, where the Unlimited plan ($375/mo) and med spa vertical likely anchor a more stable mid-market tier.

Lyra Health Launches Comprehensive Care for Youth and Young Adults Facing Severe Mental Health Crises
Lyra Health Launches Comprehensive Care for Youth and Young Adults Facing Severe Mental Health Crises
New Behavioral Health Urgent Care and Virtual Intensive Outpatient Programs Expand the Center of Excellence with Industry-first Integrated Model
BURLINGAME, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Lyra Health today announced the next evolution of its Center of Excellence (COE) for Pediatric and Young Adult Mental Health. Through new specialized programs — Behavioral Health Urgent Care, High-Risk Behavioral Skills Therapy, and Virtual Intensive Outpatient (vIOP) — Lyra now offers the industry’s most comprehensive support system for families navigating severe mental health crises.
Industry-wide, the average wait time for an initial pediatric mental health appointment is 7.5 weeks. This delay often forces young people into emergency departments as caregivers struggle to navigate fragmented care systems. One in three caregivers of children with significant mental health challenges ends up changing jobs or quitting entirely. Lyra’s COE is designed to provide immediate clinical intervention, preventing escalation and emergency care.
A New Standard for Pediatric Intensive Care
With a specialized network of over 15,500 pediatric providers globally, Lyra offers unparalleled expertise, access to an appointment in one day, and family support for pediatric patients and young adults up to 25 years old. In early 2027, Lyra is enhancing its Center of Excellence in the US to include:
- Behavioral Health Urgent Care: Readily accessible pediatric clinicians provide in-the-moment guidance and triage to the appropriate level of care, along with specialized age-appropriate assessment and comprehensive care planning.
- Virtual Intensive Outpatient (vIOP): Designed for rapid stabilization, this structured, high-frequency program is delivered at home (9-12 hours/week) and can serve as a direct alternative to costly inpatient care. To support the entire household, this program also includes dedicated Behavioral Care Managers (BCMs) who coordinate clinical handoffs and manage school IEP/504 advocacy.
- High-Acuity Behavioral Skills Therapy: This program supports young people struggling with chronic suicidal thoughts and self-harming behaviors, and those experiencing severe emotion dysregulation with evidence-based skills. Caregivers are integrated into the clinical model, learning the same skills to actively support the member’s recovery and home environment.
“When a young person is in crisis, immediate and specialized intervention is vital, not just for the child, but for the caregiver and the entire family,” said Alethea Varra, Chief Clinical Officer, Lyra Health. “By providing integrated care across all levels of need, we get families the care they need quickly with seamless handoffs that mean no one falls through the cracks. Our goal is to turn unpredictable crisis events into a clear path to recovery, providing families with lasting support and stability.”
Lyra is transforming both the lives of families in need and the economics of youth mental health care. Lyra’s focus on early intervention has yielded a 54% reduction in pediatric health care spend, an average savings of $3,307 per child. The expansion of Lyra’s Center of Excellence for Pediatric & Young Adult Mental Health further accelerates these savings while providing the clinical and administrative support families need to achieve sustainable, long-term recovery.
For more information about Lyra Health and the Center of Excellence for Pediatric and Young Adult Mental Health, please visit.
About Lyra Health
Lyra Health is the leading provider of workforce mental health benefits, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with leading employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions for members, providers and HR leaders. Empower works in the background to quickly connect members to the largest global network of evidence-based mental health providers, deliver actionable insights to benefit leaders, and free up providers to focus on client care—driving outstanding positive outcomes that are equitable across diverse racial and ethnic groups. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall health care claims costs. For more information, visit lyrahealth.com.

Lyra Health Launches Manager Coaching to Reduce Organizational Burnout
Lyra Health Launches Manager Coaching to Reduce Organizational Burnout
1:1 Support Helps Managers Thrive While Fostering More Resilient Teams
BURLINGAME, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Lyra Health, the leader in workforce mental health care, today announced the launch of AI-enhanced manager coaching. The new program supports people leaders to do their best and helps them tackle team-wide hurdles including burnout and broken workflows.
Managers are the front line of any workforce, and they are struggling. More than half of them say being a manager has negatively affected their mental health and 48% say they’ve considered leaving their role due to mental health pressure. Lyra’s Manager Coaching gives them the personalized, specialty support they need. It also goes beyond leadership training to teach them how to diagnose the root of team struggles, such as mismatched communication styles, the need for individual coping skills, or broken work design.
“Most programs teach managers what to do; we teach them how to think,” said Joe Grasso, Vice President Workforce Transformation, Lyra Health. “By learning to spot whether a problem is personal or structural, managers can stop wasting time on the wrong fixes and start enacting solutions that truly enhance wellbeing and performance.”
Practical Support for Real Work
Lyra’s Manager Coaching program is built on five pillars that set it apart from traditional professional coaching:
- Highly personalized: Lyra gives managers specialized insights tailored to their specific role and their employers’ business goals.
- Around the clock: Manager coaching includes an always-on, 24/7 AI Guide designed to provide support between sessions.
- Clear escalation: Our coaches are trained to identify when a manager’s needs go beyond professional support and require coordinated clinical intervention.
- Strategic solutions: We give managers a step-by-step process to solve root issues like role clarity and resourcing to drive sustainable team performance.
- Data-driven: Our science-backed learning and development curriculum delivers consistent and measurable guidance.
Our ICF-certified coaches use a proprietary framework that exceeds industry standards. This ensures every manager learns a shared leadership language and the same diagnostic skills to scale a consistent, high-quality culture.

Dublin, Feb. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The "Emotional Counseling Service Market Report 2026" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering.



The emotional counseling service market is experiencing remarkable growth, with its size projected to increase from $4.72 billion in 2025 to $6.38 billion in 2026, maintaining a CAGR of 35.2%. This surge can be attributed to heightened awareness of mental health issues, expanded healthcare setting counseling services, demand for emotional wellness support, and increasing therapy acceptance. The availability of trained mental health professionals further fuels this growth. By 2030, the market size is forecasted to reach $21.21 billion at a CAGR of 35%. Key factors driving this growth include the adoption of digital therapy platforms, rising mental health infrastructure investments, the expansion of employer-sponsored counseling services, and a focus on adolescent mental health. Significant trends emerging in this period involve tele-counseling platforms, digital mental health tools, personalized therapy plans, schooling and workplace counseling programs, and preventive mental health initiatives. The rising prevalence of mental health disorders is a fundamental driver of this market growth. For example, the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare estimated that by 2058, the number of Australians with dementia will more than double, impacting 533,800 women and 315,500 men. Such statistics underscore the increasing demand for emotional counseling services, which are integral in supporting individuals with mental health disorders. Leading companies in the market are leveraging advanced technologies like AI-based wellness coaches to offer personalized support and enhance mental health care's accessibility and effectiveness. For instance, Fortis Healthcare, an Indian healthcare company, launched the Adayu Mindfulness app in April 2024, featuring an AI virtual wellness coach named Stella. This platform improves access to mental health services, offering self-assessments and connecting users with mental health professionals. In another strategic move, Acentra Health, a U.S.-based company, acquired EAP Consultants LLC in January 2024. This acquisition aims to strengthen Acentra Health's Employee Assistance Program offerings, enhancing employee support, productivity, and alignment with federal EAP guidance. Notable companies in the market include Cleveland Clinic, Teladoc Health Inc., LifeStance Health, GoodRx Inc., Thriveworks Counseling, Headspace Inc., Lyra Health Inc., MDLive Inc., Doctor On Demand, and more. The 7 Best Employee Wellness Programs to Boost ROI in 2026 The days of office fruit bowls and pizza parties defining corporate wellness are over. Modern workplaces demand a more sophisticated, strategic approach to employee well-being, one that addresses the complex challenges of burnout, stress, and mental health head-on. A study in the Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine found that comprehensive wellness initiatives can lead to a 25% reduction in absenteeism and healthcare costs. This shift is not just about perks; it’s about creating a resilient, engaged, and productive workforce. Truly strategic wellness extends beyond basic offerings to include fundamental support for employee well-being. For instance, companies can explore a comprehensive guide on implementing reasonable adjustments for mental health at work to build a genuinely inclusive culture. Investing in the best employee wellness programs is no longer a luxury but a core business imperative that directly impacts retention, performance, and your bottom line. This guide cuts through the noise to help you find the right fit for your team. We’ve curated a list of top-tier platforms and services, from innovative breathwork to comprehensive mental health support. For each program, you’ll find a direct link, a clear breakdown of its pros and cons, target audience, and actionable implementation tips to help you make an informed decision. Let’s explore the solutions that will genuinely support your employees’ health and drive your organization forward. 1. 9D Breathwork 9D Breathwork emerges as a powerful and innovative contender in the landscape of the best employee wellness programs, offering a deeply transformative experience that goes far beyond conventional stress-management techniques. It integrates ancient breathing practices with a modern, multi-sensory technological approach, creating a full-spectrum journey designed to address the root causes of workplace stress, burnout, and dissatisfaction. A study in Frontiers in Psychology found that breathwork interventions can significantly reduce stress and improve mental health. This platform is uniquely positioned for organizations seeking to provide employees with a tool for profound and lasting change, rather than a superficial fix. The core of the 9D Breathwork experience is its multi-layered methodology. Each session combines guided breathwork, binaural beats for brainwave entrainment, hypnotic suggestion, Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), and subliminal messaging. This potent combination is engineered to bypass the conscious mind’s resistance and directly influence the subconscious, where limiting beliefs and stress patterns are stored. For corporate teams, this translates into a powerful tool for dismantling the deep-seated drivers of anxiety and overwhelm, fostering genuine resilience from the inside out. Key Features and Strengths Multi-Modal Approach: By layering multiple therapeutic modalities, 9D Breathwork creates a synergistic effect that targets the body, mind, and subconscious simultaneously for deeper, more sustainable shifts in well-being.

Corporate Suitability: The program is explicitly designed to address common workplace challenges like burnout, job dissatisfaction, and high-stress environments, making it a highly relevant corporate wellness solution.

Implementation and Actionable Insights To integrate 9D Breathwork effectively, introduce it as the cornerstone of a mental resilience initiative. Start with a pilot program for a specific department experiencing high stress, such as sales or project management. Action Step: Schedule a 60-minute introductory “Stress Release & Reset” session for the pilot group, facilitated by a certified 9D practitioner. Frame it as an innovative experience-based workshop, not just another webinar. Collect pre- and post-session feedback using a simple 1-10 rating scale for stress, focus, and overwhelm to measure immediate impact. Based on the positive results, you can then develop a quarterly series of sessions focused on different themes like “Enhancing Focus” or “Overcoming Burnout.” Learn more about the foundations of breathwork therapy on 9dbreathwork.com to better understand its mechanisms. What to Consider While the approach is innovative, organizations should perform their own due diligence. Pricing, formal certifications, and specific corporate case studies are not publicly listed and should be requested directly. It’s also crucial to communicate that this is a powerful wellness tool, not a substitute for clinical mental health treatment. Employees with pre-existing medical conditions should be advised to consult a clinician before participating. Despite this, its unique, tech-forward approach makes 9D Breathwork a standout choice for companies ready to invest in a truly transformational wellness program. Website: https://9dbreathwork.com 2. It excels at consolidating disparate benefits, care navigation, and wellness initiatives into one cohesive experience, making it one of the best employee wellness programs for large, complex organizations aiming to reduce vendor sprawl and simplify benefits for their workforce. The platform integrates everything from mental health support and fitness challenges to chronic condition management and benefits navigation. This holistic approach is grounded in behavioral science, using nudges, gamification, and personalized content to drive sustained engagement and healthy habits. launches.ai_summary: Lyra Health announced positive results from a 10-week pilot of its AI Sessions Summaries tool, which drafts session summaries for mental health providers. The pilot found that providers saved an average of three administrative hours per week and rated the summaries 4.3 out of 5 for usefulness and accuracy. The tool, integrated into the Lyra Engage provider platform, is now being used in approximately 75% of sessions.

launches.full_text:
Author Jennifer Lee, PhD Director, Clinical Research Share this article

December 9, 2025 The work mental health providers do is profoundly meaningful—and often incredibly demanding as they balance their client’s needs with required administrative tasks. The Lyra AI Sessions Summaries tool helps lighten this administrative load, allowing providers to be even more focused and present with their clients throughout their day. Built in close collaboration with clinicians, Lyra’s AI tool supports providers while keeping their professional autonomy and judgement at the center. It drafts a summary of each session they can review, edit, and finalize in their notes, ensuring documentation reflects their clinical expertise and perspective. Built with providers in mind Integrated into the Lyra Engage provider platform, Lyra AI Session Summaries streamlines paperwork so providers can stay engaged in their workflow. As part of the development, Lyra conducted a 10-week pilot study, designed to measure the usability and impact of the new Lyra AI Session Summaries. In the pilot, providers saved an average of three administrative hours per week from using the tool—time they could reinvest in planning, reflection, or recharging. Providers also saw real potential for AI to reduce their administrative work. The pilot study found the tool to be: Accurate - AI-generated summaries closely matched provider notes and required minimal editing

- AI-generated summaries closely matched provider notes and required minimal editing Highly rated - Providers gave summaries an average of 4.3 out of 5 stars for usefulness and accuracy

- Providers gave summaries an average of 4.3 out of 5 stars for usefulness and accuracy Easy to adopt - Providers used the tool in 3 out of 4 eligible sessions

- Providers used the tool in 3 out of 4 eligible sessions Supportive - Providers reported feeling more present in sessions and hopeful about AI easing administrative work Tested, trusted, and clinician-approved Rigorous research is core to how we validate our results and build trust. Every Lyra AI tool is guided by Lyra’s Polaris Principles, our framework for safe, responsible AI in mental health care. The pilot study shows that when AI is designed and implemented thoughtfully, it can reduce administrative strain while supporting high-quality documentation. Technology that supports providers With around 75% of sessions now using Lyra AI Session Summaries, the tool is becoming a seamless part of providers’ workflow. With less paperwork, providers can dedicate more attention to the work they care about most—helping clients get better. See how Lyra is driving responsible AI in mental health Learn more

product_offering.product_overview: Lyra Health offers a unified mental health benefits platform built around the Lyra Empower AI Platform, which combines four interoperating modules: Lyra Connect (dashboard and AI insights for HR leaders), Lyra Engage (clinical system for providers), Lyra Care (member-facing experience powered by Lyra AI), and Lyra Link (HR and benefits ecosystem integration layer, including the Workday Wellness integration). On top of this platform, Lyra delivers care services including Therapy, Coaching, Medication Management, Self-Care, Specialty Care, Manager Coaching, and Substance Use Disorder support, organized under multiple Centers of Excellence (Pediatric & Young Adult Mental Health, Neurodiversity, Women's Mental Health, and Chronic Conditions). Lyra AI is the clinical-grade AI suite that powers conversational support, voice interaction, AI-drafted documentation, and predictive insights across the platform. Acquired brands Bend Health (pediatric) and ICAS World (global EAP, branded Lyra International) extend the portfolio, and the Lyra Mobile App delivers the member experience on iOS and Android.
